title: Keyframes: ease presets apply saved curves to keyframe pairs (#254)
author: bflatastic
body:
Ease presets for issue #254, our own take on what ease-curve plug-ins are used for: easing curves kept by name, drawn and edited in a value graph, and applied to pairs of keyframes.

| Part | What |
|---|---|
| `effectcraft-keyframe` | `EaseCurve`: the out side of the first key plus the in side of the second, as influence (%) and speed relative to the segment's average speed. It converts to and from cubic-bezier handles. `apply` eases a key pair per dimension, along the motion path for spatial values, and as overall progress for paths and gradients, the way Easy Ease shapes them. An Auto Bezier key keeps its other side. `measure` reads the curve a segment actually plays. |
| Engine | `keys.easePreset.apply {preset \| curve}` eases every pair of neighbouring selected keys on each selected property, as one undo step. `curve` takes `{outInfluence, outSpeed, inInfluence, inSpeed}` or `[x1, y1, x2, y2]`. Also `.capture`, `.save {name, curve?}`, `.list`, `.rename {name, newName}` and `.delete {name}`. There are 12 built-in curves with our own numbers; they are read-only. User presets are stored in the config store as `ease_presets.json` and loaded leniently: bad JSON or bad entries are skipped and logged. |
| UI | **Window ▸ Ease Presets** is a dockable panel. It has a value graph with two draggable handles that edit a working curve, plus Apply, From Keys, a name field with Save Current, Rename and Delete. Every preset shows as a thumbnail drawn in code; clicking one applies it. Wide panels put the thumbnails beside the graph, narrow panels put them below. The panel state is serde, and every control registers an `easePresets.*` automation id. `widgets::text_field` is the search field without its icon. |
| Docs | A new section in `docs/parity.md`, and a line under G8 in `docs/gaps.md`. |

title: Render: render.backend says why it renders on the CPU; mcp --gpu documented (#262)
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #262: `get_project` reported `{"active":"cpu","adapter":null,"gpuAcceleration":true}` with no reason, `mcp --gpu` was undocumented, and a failed `--gpu` hid the adapter's error.

**Fix**
- The session keeps the host's reason there's no GPU compositor (`accel_note`): the headless CLI's "renders on the CPU unless started with --gpu", or the desktop app's compositor setup or retirement error.
- `render.backend` / `get_project` report it as `why` whenever rendering is on the CPU, or say the project's renderer is Software Only. `why` is null on the GPU.

mcp --gpu: {"active":"gpu","adapter":"NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 (Vulkan)",…,"why":null}

title: Effects: Fractal Noise's Soft Linear has no lattice creases (#259)
author: bflatastic
body:
Fractal Noise and Turbulent Noise with Noise Type Soft Linear no longer show a square grid under the turbulent types and high contrast (#259).

**Cause:** Soft Linear was value noise with a quintic fade between two lattice values per axis. The fade has zero slope across every lattice line and at every lattice point, so contours met the lattice at right angles and flattened around its points; the turbulent fold `1 − |s|` and Contrast 140 / Brightness −35 made that a visible grid at each layer's cell size. Measured at the issue's settings (1920×1080, Scale 420, Turbulent Basic): gradients were 1.28× as strong along the lattice axes as along the diagonals (Spline 1.08–1.10, Linear 1.0); across a lattice line the slope was 2% of the average.

**Fix:** Soft Linear is now linear interpolation softened by a one-cell box filter, which is the uniform quadratic B-spline over the 3 × 3 lattice values around the nearest one (evolution still fades between two slices). It is smooth everywhere, its slope on lattice lines is half the neighbours' difference, and it costs 9 taps against Spline's 16. Averaging lowers the noise's spread, so a fixed gain about mid-grey restores the quintic fade's variance and existing projects keep their contrast and brightness (issue settings: mean 0.356 → 0.362, std 0.147 → 0.152, axis bias 1.28 → 1.05). Only Fractal / Turbulent Noise's Soft Linear changes: `generate::value_noise` and its other callers are untouched. `noise3` now reuses `generate`'s lattice hash and fade instead of a copy. Both GPU kernels (the pointwise Fractal Noise case and `fxn_fractal`) call the same `soft_linear_noise`.

**Test:** `noise3::tests::soft_linear_has_no_lattice_creases`: the slope across one layer's lattice lines relative to the average (0.019 before, 0.75 now; must be > 0.5) and the axis/diagonal gradient ratio at the issue's settings (1.21 before, 1.03 now; must be < 1.15). title: MCP: preserve unsaved work across server restarts (#258)
author: jonassneu
body:
Headless MCP sessions lost unsaved projects when the client disconnected or restarted the server. I reproduced this with an unsaved composition and text layer: restarting returned an empty project with no recovery files.

I added opt-in recovery with `effectcraft-cli mcp --autosave`. Changed dirty projects are checkpointed before the tool reply is sent, so edits with successful checkpoints survive a forced server kill. Startup metadata lists previous checkpoints for explicit recovery with `open_project`, followed by `save_project` to a normal project file.

- I isolated each server's checkpoint folder and rotating versions, including engine-triggered auto-saves.
- I kept desktop preferences, shortcuts, and recovery state untouched.
- I added visible warnings and retries for failed checkpoints without asking the client to repeat the edit.
- I added a final flush on disconnect and transport errors, plus regression coverage for forced kills, partial tool failures, batches, concurrent sessions, and failed writes.
- I opted into using my public GitHub profile name for the About-window contributor credit.

Recovery is explicit, and the mode is opt-in. Synchronous saves can add latency to large-project edits; old session folders remain available until manually removed. An edit interrupted before its reply may be absent from the checkpoint.

### Validation

- I reproduced the original failure and confirmed the new regression failed before the fix.
- I force-killed a real MCP process after receiving its replies, restarted it, and verified that its composition, text, and keyframes were restored exactly.
- 2,099 workspace tests passed excluding the GPU crate; 471 engine, automation, and CLI tests passed in the focused run.
- Formatting, strict workspace Clippy, layering, asset attribution, and all 32 WebAssembly crate checks passed.

Full CI is not green: two existing NVIDIA Dust & Scratches tests fail in unchanged GPU code (`dust_threshold_on_quantized_input` and `medians`). …

title: App: a second copy opening, or OpenGL that fails, no longer strands Window Graphics
author: prekabreki
body:
Opening EffectCraft twice in quick succession can leave it unable to start at all, on machines where OpenGL can't open a window.

This is rare: it needs two launches within a fraction of a second, with Window Graphics still on Automatic, on a machine where OpenGL can't open a window. It applies to every platform, though it was reproduced and tested on Linux only.

**Repro (Linux, NVIDIA RTX 4080, Plasma X11):** start two copies a fraction of a second apart with a fresh settings folder (`XDG_CONFIG_HOME=<empty dir>`). On `main` the settings end up at `windowGraphics: "gl"`, and from then on every launch fails with `WGPU error: No suitable graphics adapter found; … gl not compatible with provided surface`. The setting that would fix it is in the app that no longer opens.

**Cause:** the #243 launch guard can't tell a crashed launch from one that is still opening its window. The second copy finds the first one's `launch-pending` marker, takes it for a crash and switches Window Graphics to OpenGL. The guard switches only from Automatic, and nothing switches back, so a machine whose OpenGL can't present stays on it for good.

**Fix (two small changes, `launch_guard.rs` and four lines in `main.rs`):**
- Each launch holds an OS lock (`File::try_lock`) on its marker until the window draws. A marker that is still locked belongs to a launch that is still running, so it isn't counted as a crash. A crash releases the lock with the process, so #243's case is unchanged. Where locks aren't available, the guard works as before.
- If the window fails to open (eframe returns an error) while on OpenGL, `opengl_failed` sets Window Graphics back to Automatic and removes the marker, so the next launch tries the default graphics again.

`Launch::begin`'s signature and the startup error message are unchanged.

**Test:** `launch_guard::tests::a_second_copy_or_failed_opengl_doesnt_strand_window_graphics` covers both: a second launch while the first is still open stays Automatic, a real crash…

title: Engine: adding a 3D model switches a Classic 3D comp to Advanced 3D (#264)
author: bflatastic
body:
Imported GLB/glTF models now show when they are added to a new composition: adding a 3D model (or primitive) switches a Classic 3D comp to Advanced 3D, as After Effects does (#264).

**Cause:** not the GPU. Only the Advanced 3D renderer draws model and primitive layers, new compositions (and New Comp from Selection) default to Classic 3D, and adding a model layer left the renderer alone, so the model drew nothing on every backend while text layers showed. Reproduced headlessly on this Windows machine with `quad.glb` → New Comp from Selection: the viewer was empty with the GPU compositor (Vulkan, RTX 4090) and with Mercury Software Only; after switching the comp to Advanced 3D both showed the model with identical pixels. The CPU path (software Advanced 3D rasteriser) renders models fine, so an Intel HD Graphics 5500 without the GPU compositor isn't the problem.

**Fix:** as After Effects' help describes ("Advanced 3D gets automatically selected when you add a 3D model to the composition"), `layer.newModel` / `layer.addItem` of a model and `layer.newPrimitive` switch a Classic 3D comp to Advanced 3D inside the same edit: one undo step, with Geometry Options added to the comp's text and shape layers as Composition Settings does. A toast says the comp changed renderer. Switching a comp that has model layers back to Classic 3D toasts that Classic 3D doesn't draw them (Classic 3D still draws no models, as before). title: Effects: effect points on shape layers start at the layer centre (#227)
author: bflatastic
body:
Part of #227

## What was wrong
Shape and text layers have comp-sized effect bounds centred on their origin, but effects measured positions from that origin. An effect point left at its default "layer centre" therefore sat at the comp's bottom-right corner. On a 180×80 rectangle centred in a 200×100 comp, Twirl changed nothing and Bulge changed only the bottom-right quarter. The Turbulent Displace Offset handle was also drawn in the viewer's bottom-right corner.

## The fix
Effects now work in **effect space**, as After Effects does: layer pixels measured from the top-left of the layer's effect bounds. The source rectangle, or the comp-sized bounds for shape and text layers.

- **Renderer** (`crates/render`): `effect_bounds` / `EvalCtx::effect_to_comp`. The layer buffer is moved into effect space once for the whole stack (`Buf::rebase`), so the CPU and GPU kernels need no per-effect changes. Effects also get everything else in effect space:
  - masks
  - other layers' pixels for layer parameters, each in its own effect space, so Set Matte and displacement maps now see a whole shape layer
  - `layer_input` / `self_at` frames
  - the comp camera (`CompScene::rebased`)

  `pin_rect` and `EffectEnv::bounds_origin` from #235 are removed: `layer_rect` is now correct everywhere. Adjustment layers still run their effects on the comp below, unchanged.
- **UI / engine**: these all map through effect space:
  - effect point handles and eyedroppers
  - Puppet pins and mesh
  - the Layer panel (Paint, Roto Brush)
  - the tracker's Corner Pin output

  The repeated "comp size when there is no source" snippets are replaced by `effect_bounds`.
- **Disk cache**: the render version is bumped, so stale entries for shape layers aren't reused.

## Saved projects: migration (schema 1 → 2)
`SCHEMA_VERSION` is now 2. Opening a schema 1 project (`upgrade_effects`, also used for imported `.ectemplate`s) moves the positions held by effects on shape and text layers by half the comp size, so **…

title: Import: a 3D model doesn't ask how to interpret its alpha (#264)
author: bflatastic
body:

title: M9: place Japanese vertical punctuation using font metrics
author: midasdf
body:
Vertical Source Text shapes Japanese punctuation using horizontal glyphs, then keeps them upright around a horizontal-font centre. Enable `vert`/`vrt2` only for CJK runs and position their outlines from the font's VORG/vmtx vertical origin and horizontal advance. Update `outline_xf` with the same placement so animated/variable-outline redraws agree. Half-width Roman text stays sideways and tate-chu-yoko stays horizontally shaped.

The regression fails on unchanged main and verifies vertical glyph IDs, upper-right comma/full-stop ink, unchanged horizontal cache entries and tracking-independent cross-column placement. Text-package debug/release tests pass (43 unit + 2 integration), including the new punctuation regression in its own process so native font probing does not affect fallback tests. Package Clippy (with the existing `collapsible_match` exception) and wasm check pass; Shippori Mincho output was also rasterized and inspected using locally loaded OFL font data. No font assets, project-schema fields, UI controls or ROADMAP log are added. This is independent of the open toolbar PR #213.

Stock `cargo xtask ci` stops at existing `clippy::collapsible_match` warnings in unchanged path_text/audio_fx/generate code. Asset/layer checks and the full lower-crate wasm gate passed. This fixes vertical forms/origins, not complete Japanese paragraph composition.

Reference: [OpenType vertical forms](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/typography/opentype/spec/features_uz#tag-vert), [JLReq punctuation placement](https://www.w3.org/TR/jlreq/#positioning_of_punctuation_marks).

title: Media: footage audio at another sample rate no longer stutters (#274)
author: bflatastic
body:
Issue #274 (Windows, 0.4.0, H.264 MP4 clips): once preview sound played it stuttered and sounded like a much lower sample rate, and the exported MP4 had the same stutter. The other half of the report, silence until Cache Before Playback, is #208, fixed after 0.4.0: `preview_with_audio_sounds_once_rendering_keeps_up` passes on current main (sound starts within 2 s without caching the work area).

Reproduced with ffmpeg fixtures (H.264 + AAC in MP4 at 44.1 and 48 kHz, stereo and mono, a 440 Hz tone and a sweep), read through `MediaPool::audio_samples` one frame at a time at 29.97, 30 and 25 fps, as export and the preview mix do, and compared sample by sample with ffmpeg's decode. Footage at the mix rate matched (max error 0.002, no lag) at every frame rate; footage at the other rate (44.1 kHz read at 48 kHz, or 48 kHz at 44.1 kHz) came out with values up to about 100 against a 0.5 tone, repeating at every read. Chunk rounding (1601.6 samples per frame at 29.97), the export's audio cursor and the MP4 muxer's timestamps were fine.

**Cause:** FilmCraft's MP4 reader (`Mp4Source::audio`, `crates/codecs/src/mp4.rs` at the pinned rev `2c5ba7a`), asked for audio at a rate other than the file's, applied the edit list's priming offset (−1024 samples for AAC) twice: the window was decoded from the offset position, then the resampler took its phase from that same offset again, so each read started about 1024 source samples early, was clamped to index 0 with a large negative fraction, and linear interpolation extrapolated a ramp over its first ~940 output samples. Export asks for audio a batch of frames at a time and the preview a device buffer at a time, so the ramp repeated dozens of times a second: the stutter, and the "low sample rate" sound. A same-rate read takes FilmCraft's copy path and was exact. FilmCraft has already fixed this upstream in storytold/filmcraft@5bf2203 ("codecs: resampled MP4 audio reads apply the edit list once", PR storytold/filmcraft#42), 87 commits pa…

title: Text: fallback skips a font whose glyph for the character is empty (#285)
author: DWAA1660
body:
Fixes #285.

## Problem
`Face::has_char` counted any non-zero cmap entry as coverage. Some fonts map whole scripts to empty glyphs; the report's Black Mountain maps 57,524 code points, CJK included, to glyphs with no contours. Once such a face was loaded, `fallback_for` could return it for Japanese text, which then rendered as nothing. That is why `cjk_falls_back_to_a_system_family` failed in parallel runs.

## Fix
- `has_char`, and `file_covers` for faces not loaded yet, now also require the glyph to draw something. That means an outline with at least one segment, a COLR/CPAL colour glyph, or a bitmap in any strike, all checked through skrifa.
- Characters that are blank by nature still count as covered by any mapping: whitespace (U+0020, U+3000…) and the default-ignorable code points (soft hyphen, ZWJ/ZWNJ, bidi controls, variation selectors, tags).
- `Face::glyph` is unchanged, so shaping with the chosen face behaves as before.

## Tests
- New `fonts::tests::an_empty_glyph_does_not_cover_its_character`. It builds a minimal TrueType font in code, so no font file is added and `cargo xtask assets` is unaffected. The font maps U+E000 to an empty glyph, U+E001 to a triangle, and space to the empty glyph. The test asserts that `has_char` is false, true and true respectively, that `fallback_for(U+E000)` never returns this face, and that `fallback_for(U+E001)` does.
- `cargo test -p effectcraft-text --lib fonts::`: 8 passed, including `cjk_falls_back_to_a_system_family`.
- `cargo clippy -p effectcraft-text --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

title: text, ui: the CJK fallback fonts follow the interface language
author: FeiLiuEM
body:
Makes the CJK system fallback follow the interface language.

Today `theme::install` registers one fallback resolved for `あ`, so Han text is drawn by whichever face the locale environment points at (`han_order()` → `LANG` / `LC_ALL`). On a machine whose locale is not `zh` that is the Japanese face, so Chinese text — a Chinese interface, or Chinese file, layer and template names on any locale — is drawn with Japanese glyph forms, and Simplified-only characters need a fallback that actually covers them.

### What it does

- `effectcraft_text::fonts::set_cjk_locale(tag)` lets the host say which language's face should draw Han ideographs: `han_order` prefers that request over the environment, and the fallback cache is dropped when it changes so a switch takes effect. The tag → order rule moves into the pure `han_order_for`, which keeps it testable without process state.
- `theme::install(ctx, tokens, language)` takes the stored `general.language` value and registers one CJK fallback per script in every font family, the interface's own script first: kana (`あ`) for Japanese, a Han character (`文`) for `zh-hans` / `zh-hant`, then the other script so names in it still render. A face is registered at most once, and a machine with no CJK font installs nothing — exactly as before.
- An English (or `system`) interface keeps the previous behaviour: the environment decides.
- The Chinese values are inert until the Chinese catalogs land (#309); this only names what the setting can hold.

### Tests

- The tag → order rule: `zh`, `zh-CN`, `zh_Hans`, `ZH-Hant-TW.UTF-8` and `zh_MO` → Han first; `ko-KR` → Korean first; `ja_JP.UTF-8`, `en-US`, `de` and the empty tag → Japanese first.
- For a Chinese, a Japanese and an English interface: the probe order, the names registered in every family, and that no face is registered twice. Each assertion is skipped on a machine that has no CJK font installed, which is also the case that registers nothing.

title: fix: rewrite Audio Spectrum to match After Effects linear frequency/amplitude model
author: thanhcong2k7
body:
## What was wrong?

The Audio Spectrum effect in EffectCraft looked completely different from After Effects - the waveform bars were the wrong size and in the wrong places. If you put the same audio through both apps, you'd get two totally different-looking visualisations.

There were three root causes:

1. **Bars were in the wrong positions** - EffectCraft spread frequency bands on a *logarithmic* curve (cramming low frequencies together, spreading highs apart). After Effects uses a simple *even spacing* from start to end frequency. So the same 440 Hz tone would peak at a completely different bar in each app.

2. **Quiet sounds were way too loud visually** - The old code converted amplitudes to decibels before drawing, which compresses the range and artificially boosts quiet signals. After Effects just draws height proportional to volume - quiet = short bar, loud = tall bar. The old approach made everything look like a solid "wall of sound".

3. **Band sampling was inaccurate** - Each bar only sampled 4 fixed points inside its frequency range, which could miss peaks or read between bins. The new code properly reads all FFT bins that fall inside a band and picks the strongest one.

## What's fixed

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| Frequency bars bunched up at the left (log scale) | Bars evenly spread across the baseline (linear, like AE) |
| Silent frequencies still showed tall bars (dB boost) | Silent = zero height, loud = tall (linear amplitude) |
| Some bars flickered or missed peaks (4-point sample) | Accurate bin interpolation + peak-across-band |

## Other improvements in this PR

- **Duration Averaging** now works - when enabled, the effect analyses three overlapping time slices and averages them, which smooths out sudden spikes and gives a calmer visualisation.
- **Dynamic Hue Phase** - a new option that slowly cycles the bar colours over time.
- **Tiny-bar cleanup** - in "Digital" display mode, bars shorter than half a pixel are hidden instead of drawing as n…

title: CLI: render --out is relative to the working directory (#300)
author: Oldrich333
body:
> Agent-written on behalf of @Oldrich333 · agent: hive-admin/main · model: claude-cli/claude-opus-5-5 · code: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5 · review: openai/gpt-6.1-sol · origin: owner-requested

## Problem

`effectcraft-cli render --out <relative path>` resolved the path like a Render Queue output (default output folder, else the project file's folder) instead of against the current working directory. Every other CLI path (`--project` included) is relative to the working directory, so a path that already named the project folder was doubled (`--out proj/out/d.mp4` with `--project proj/x.ecproj` wrote `proj/proj/out/d.mp4`), and from another directory the file landed beside the project instead of where the shell user expects.

## Fix

The CLI makes a relative `--out` absolute against the working directory (`std::path::absolute`, no filesystem access) before it queues the render. An absolute `--out` is unchanged. The usage text and the module doc now say that a relative `--out` is relative to the working directory.

The engine is not changed. `Session::resolve_output` keeps its order for Render Queue outputs set in a project and for `render --queue`: tokens expanded, an absolute path as is, else `export.defaultOutputFolder`, the project's folder, the working directory. `--out` itself is not documented as project-relative anywhere (README, `docs/agents.md`, CLI help), so only the CLI's own argument changes. `render --bridge` is refused as before, and MCP / `exec renderQueue.*` parameters are untouched.

Visible change for JSON consumers: with an explicit `--out`, `rendered[].output` is now the absolute path that was written (it was already a resolved path, sometimes absolute).

title: Puppet: the first pin no longer turns the layer about it (#313)
author: HEOJUNFO
body:
Fixes #313.

## What and why

Adding the first Puppet Position pin can turn and shift the layer, even though nothing was dragged. How much depends on where you click.

The cause is in `arap::deform`. With one fixed vertex and no edge targets (no Bend pins), a rotation or scale about the pin costs nothing in the ARAP energy. The only thing holding the solve in place is `REG = 1e-9`, which becomes about 1e-12 after scaling by the mean edge length. That is too weak, so the conjugate-gradient solve turns round-off into a visible rotation.

Example: on an 800×600 solid traced from its alpha, one pin at [40, 40], left at its rest position, moved vertices by up to 4.55 px. Other spots I measured with the same setup moved them by up to about 19 px.

The exact solution in this case is the rest mesh translated by the pin's offset. That is the initial guess `deform` already builds, so it now returns it whenever there is exactly one fixed handle and no edge targets.

- Starch pins only change triangle weights, and a rigid translation costs nothing whatever the weights, so they don't affect this.
- Two or more pins, or any Bend pin, still go through the solver.

## How it was tested

- `puppet::tests::single_pin_on_a_traced_solid_does_not_rotate_it` (effects): traces an 800×600 solid the way the Puppet tool does, then puts one pin at six spots, both at rest and moved by (35, −20). Every vertex must move by exactly the pin's offset (within 1e-6). On `main` it fails: `pin at [40.0, 40.0] moved by [0.0, 0.0]: vertices off by up to 4.55 px`.
- `tests_paint::first_puppet_pin_leaves_the_layer_still` (engine) follows the issue's steps. It renders an 800×600 solid in a 1920×1080 comp, runs `puppet.addPin` at three spots, and compares the frame. On `main`, `pin at [40, 40] changed 5795 pixels`. With the fix, 0 pixels change.
- The existing puppet tests pass: 15 in effects, 9 in engine.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes: fmt, clippy, tests, layers, assets, wasm.

title: fix(macos): prevent SIGILL crash on exit by replacing viewport close …
author: onemannoplan
body:
…with clean process exit

### Summary
When selecting the "Quit" menu option on macOS, the application occasionally crashes with an `EXC_BAD_INSTRUCTION` (SIGILL) error report during shutdown.

### Root Cause
1. The app menu command mapped `"app.quit"` directly to `ctx.send_viewport_cmd(egui::ViewportCommand::Close)`.
2. Forcing an explicit viewport close via the command queue while macOS and AppKit are initiating their own termination sequence creates a race condition with `winit`.
3. This conflict during native window, view, and observer teardown leads to an illegal instruction fault.

### Solution
- Replaced the manual `ViewportCommand::Close` trigger for `"app.quit"` with a clean `std::process::exit(0)`.
- This bypasses the problematic `winit`/AppKit teardown race condition on macOS, allowing the application to shut down instantly and cleanly without generating crash reports.

title: Export: AIFF 32-bit float writes AIFF-C fl32 instead of 24-bit (#317)
author: HEOJUNFO
body:
Fixes #317.

## What and why

When you choose 32 Bit Float for an AIFF output, the Render Queue reports `F32`, but `export::webm::audio_file` mapped `F32` to `S24` for AIFF and wrote 24-bit integer PCM without saying so.

This PR writes the float data instead of dropping precision. Plain AIFF has no float format, so for 32-bit float the file is AIFF-C. The layout follows Apple's public AIFF-C spec (1991):

- `FORM` type `AIFC`
- an `FVER` chunk with AIFC Version 1 (`0xA2805140`)
- a `COMM` chunk with the usual AIFF fields, followed by the compression type `fl32` and its Pascal-string name `"32-bit floating point"`
- big-endian IEEE float samples in `SSND`. `pcm_bytes` already produced these.

16- and 24-bit exports are unchanged and stay plain AIFF. So the delivered file now matches both the request and the format the queue reports, and the 32 Bit Float option the UI already offers for AIFF actually works.

midasdf's comment on the issue describes a different local fix that rejects float AIFF and points the user to WAV. This PR supports the format instead, so existing projects and queues that ask for float AIFF keep working.

## How it was tested

- `crates/export/tests/render_settings.rs` › `wav_and_aiff_channels_and_formats`: the old assertion expected 24-bit for an F32 AIFF. It now checks the whole AIFF-C layout: the FORM size equals the file length, FVER, the COMM length (44), channels, frame count, sample size 32, `fl32` and its name, and the SSND length. A 24-bit AIFF still checks as plain `AIFF`.
- I followed the issue's steps with the release `effectcraft-cli`: a 48 kHz stereo float WAV with samples `(0.25 + 2^-25, -0.125 - 2^-26)`, then `renderQueue.add` with `format: aiff` and `audioFormat: 32`. Results:
  - `ffprobe`: `pcm_f32be`, 32 bits, 2 ch, 48000 Hz, `duration_ts` 24000. On `main` this was `pcm_s24be`.
  - Decoding with `ffmpeg -f f32le`: all 24,000 frames equal the source floats bit for bit, `(0.2500000298023224, -0.1250000149011612)`.

title: Fix #367: weighted_nms terminates on NaN or zero-area boxes
author: bflatastic
body:
## What was wrong
`mediapipe::weighted_nms` partitioned all remaining detections, `top` included, by `iou(d, top) > NMS_IOU`. For a degenerate box (any NaN coordinate, or zero area) `iou` returns `0.0` even against itself, so `top` landed in `rest`, `dets` never shrank, and `while let Some(top) = dets.first()` spun forever. Not reachable with the pinned official detector (SHA-256 checked), but reachable through the public `FaceLandmarker::from_task` with another detector, and a hang rather than an error.

## Fix
`top` always joins its own cluster: the partition runs over the detections after it, and `top` is inserted at the front of its cluster. Every pass now removes at least one detection. Well-formed boxes are unchanged, since `iou(top, top) = 1 > 0.3` already put `top` first in its cluster.

## Tests
- New `mediapipe::tests::nms_terminates_on_degenerate_boxes`: NaN boxes, zero-area boxes with zero score, and a NaN score each come out as one detection apiece instead of hanging.
- `cargo test -p effectcraft-segment` (18 passed), `cargo clippy -p effectcraft-segment --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`.

Thanks to @KazW for the report, the analysis and the suggested fix, which this applies.

Fixes #367

title: Fix #368: tflite rejects models whose scratch or work exceeds a budget
author: bflatastic
body:
## What was wrong
`tflite::Model::read` capped each tensor at 2^28 values and nothing else. An 8 KB model with one 64×64 `CONV_2D` over a `[1, 1, 2^25, 1]` input loaded fine, then `Model::run` allocated an `ow·kh·kw·cin` patch row (512 GB) and the process aborted, which `catch_unwind` cannot catch. Total work was unbounded too: 2,000 `RELU`s over 2^25 values loaded and ran for minutes. The app path is not exposed (models are SHA-256 pinned), but the public `Model::read` / `Model::run` and `FaceLandmarker::from_task` are.

## Fix
`Model::read` now works out what one run takes from the static shapes (`Model::cost`, all checked arithmetic, overflow is an error) and refuses a model over any fixed budget:

| Budget | Limit | MediaPipe selfie segmentation (256×256, measured) |
|---|---|---|
| Conv / depthwise / pool kernel side | 32 | 5 |
| One operator's working space (conv patch row, `ow·kh·kw·cin`) | 2^22 floats | 3,456 |
| Multiply-adds + pooling comparisons | 2^33 | 58 M |
| Values written by all operators (elementwise work) | 2^30 | 7.4 M |
| Floats alive at once (mirrors `run`'s freeing) | 2^29 | (not loadable, see below) |
| Constant values decoded / laid out at load | 2^27 | 106 K params |

The official `face_landmarker.task` was not available locally, so I could not measure it here. The selfie segmentation model above is a MediaPipe model of the same family and input size. It uses `HARD_SWISH`, so it doesn't load in this interpreter, and its numbers come from walking its graph. The issue estimates the face models at about 0.1 GMAC, which leaves more than 80× headroom on multiply-adds. A new gated test, `official_face_models_fit_the_budgets` (`EFFECTCRAFT_FACE_LANDMARKER=path/to/face_landmarker.task`), prints both face models' costs and asserts at least 8× headroom on every budget (4× on kernel side).

Same class of bug, also closed:
- `PAD`, `CONCATENATION` and `MAX_POOL_2D` sized their outputs from the pads, the parts or the input channels, not from the declare…

title: Render Queue: output files end in their format's extension once (#293)
author: bflatastic
body:
Issue #293 (macOS, Render Queue): renders sometimes came out as `Comp1.<format>.ecproj` (for a PNG sequence, every frame), and DaVinci Resolve failed on a clip named `Comp 2.mov.mov` (a doubled extension; Resolve's error dialog and timeline show that file name). title: segment: sample crops like MediaPipe's ImageToTensor; no overflow in crop
author: KazW
body:
## What

`face::crop` in `crates/segment` now samples like MediaPipe's CPU `ImageToTensor`, and no longer overflows on absurd frame sizes.

- Corner-aligned output pixels (`u = i/n`), the source position read as a pixel-centre index, and the result rounded to a whole 0-255 value.
- A `Border` parameter: `Zero` for the face detector, `Replicate` for the mesh.
- `w * h` is checked; a frame that overflows or has a short buffer gives an `lo`-filled tensor (an empty frame did the same through the zero border before, but returned 0.0 in the early return).

Fixes #385
Fixes #386

## Evidence

- Against OpenCV `warpPerspective` on a synthetic 64x48 frame (16x16 crop, rotated ROI), the max absolute difference went from 242.7 to 0.0 (0-255 scale).
- In a downstream copy of this code, landmarks against Python `mediapipe` 1.1.0 differed by about 0.2 to 0.4 px mean on the 360x288 and 480x360 frames and 1.4 to 2.0 px mean (max 6 px) on the 720x480 and 1280x720 frames, before the fix; after the fix they differ by 0.004 to 0.07 px mean on corpus frames.
- `crop_survives_absurd_frame_sizes` panicked with "attempt to multiply with overflow" before the change.

## Tests

`cargo test -p effectcraft-segment`, `cargo clippy -p effectcraft-segment --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check` pass. New tests: `crop_follows_mediapipe_corner_aligned_sampling`, `crop_borders_are_zero_or_replicated`, `crop_survives_absurd_frame_sizes` (replacing `crop_samples_pixel_centres`). I could not run the full `cargo xtask ci` here (the build filled the disk).

title: i18n: translate the interface below the menu bar (panels, dialogs, tooltips)
author: FeiLiuEM
body:
The menu bar has been translatable since #229, but everything below it — panel labels, buttons, field
names, tooltips, the sentences a panel draws itself — was written straight into the code and stayed
English in every language. That is #333, and this is the plumbing plus the translations.

**384 strings in 49 files** now read their text through a catalog, in Simplified and Traditional
Chinese, so a Chinese interface is Chinese all the way down instead of only in its menus.

### How it works

`crates/ui-egui/src/i18n/ui.rs` is a second catalog next to the menu one:

- Rows are keyed by **the English source string**, so a panel wraps a literal it already has
  (`tr("Composition Name:")`) instead of inventing an id, and a missing row falls back to English
  rather than to an empty label. A filename, layer name or workspace name is never translated.
- `tr_args("Proxy Use: {}", &[&quality])` handles the rows that carry values: it writes `{}` in
  order into its own buffer, so it cannot panic on a mismatch, and a test keeps every row's
  placeholder count equal to its English source, so a translation can never drop a value.
  (A runtime format string is not an option in Rust — `format!` needs a literal — which is why the
  values are substituted rather than formatted.)
- The language in force is set once per frame from the **resolved** interface language — the same
  value the CJK fallback fonts are installed for (#312) — and kept in a thread-local, so a panel
  does not have to thread it through every function. It is documented at the top of the module; the
  render threads never draw interface text. If you would rather pass the language explicitly at each
  call site, that is a mechanical change to the same 426 calls and I am happy to do it.

title: Text: the variable-font test picks an axis that moves the advance
author: FeiLiuEM
body:
`style_variations_change_advances_and_outlines` picked `wdth`, else `wght`, else the first axis with a range, then asserted that the advance moves. That assumes the chosen axis changes advances — which a monospaced family does not.

On Linux the first variable face installed here is **Google Sans Code**: along `wght` its *outlines* move (ink 1284 → 2946 for `H`) but its *advances* stay fixed (780 → 780), because it is monospaced. So the test failed with `wght 300..800: advances 780 vs 780` while both `measure` and the font were right. (`Bahnschrift`, also installed, behaves the same along `wght` and moves both along `wdth`.)

The test now tries the axes in order and uses the first one whose **advance** actually moves — Google Sans Code answers on its own `MONO` axis, Bahnschrift on `wdth`, a normal weight-varying family on `wght` — and skips with a message on a machine whose variable faces never move an advance, the same shape as the "no variable font installed" skip beside it. The outline assertion keeps its teeth: the axis is picked for moving the advance, but whether the outline follows is still checked.

Test-only change, one file, no production code touched.

**Verified** on Linux with Google Sans Code and Bahnschrift installed: `cargo test -p effectcraft-text` reported 43 passed / 1 failed before and **44 passed** after; `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy -p effectcraft-text --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean.

title: UI: Add appearance styles aligned with PhotoCraft
author: cdinhoo
body:
This proposes appearance choices aligned with PhotoCraft’s approach: distinct styles that change surfaces, corners, tabs, and control treatment while preserving familiar layouts.

EffectCraft's themes currently share the same visual style, and several custom effect/timeline surfaces keep dark colors even in Light. This adds Studio Dark, Studio Light, and Classic alongside the existing themes, with a checked Appearance submenu in the macOS application menu and View on other platforms. The new menu entries are covered by the existing Japanese and Simplified/Traditional Chinese catalogs.

Studio uses rounded panels, selected tab backgrounds, and violet accents. Classic uses neutral gray panels, lighter gray fields, square controls, subtle beveled edges, and restrained blue editing accents. Effect headers and timeline surfaces now use theme colors. The existing default, control geometry, workspaces, semantic label/cache colors, and composition data are preserved.

Choices apply immediately and persist through the existing preferences, CLI/control channel, and UI commands. Settings retains live preview/Cancel and adds Reset Appearance. No new dependencies or project-format changes.

Validation: `CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO=false RUST_TEST_THREADS=1 TMPDIR=/private/tmp cargo xtask ci` passes (formatting, release clippy with warnings denied, all workspace tests, dependency layers, asset attribution, and WebAssembly checks). Four new appearance tests cover menu switching/checkmarks, saved preference IDs, backwards compatibility, contrast, and unchanged document/layout geometry. title: Import: Interpret Footage has Start Timecode, as in After Effects (#297)
author: bflatastic
body:
Follow-up to #384, which landed with an Interpret Footage ▸ **Start Frame** field that trimmed or padded an image sequence's head. After Effects has no such field: its Interpret Footage has **Start Timecode** — *Use Source File Timecode*, or *Override Start*, which changes the timecode the footage shows and leaves its frames alone. This replaces Start Frame with that.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Interpret Footage | Start Frame (sequences only) | Start Timecode: Use Source File Timecode / Override Start (all footage with time) |
| Frames of `shot_[1001-1004]` | changed by Start Frame | always 1001 to 1004 |
| Footage panel time | from 0:00:00:00 | from Override Start |
| `file.interpretFootage` | `startFrame: number\|"file"` | `overrideStart: bool`, `startTimecode: timecode\|frame` |

`Footage.start_timecode` holds Override Start in frames at the footage's rate (`None` = Use Source, 0 because file timecode isn't read). Timecode is read at the footage's rate after any frame rate change in the same call; frame numbers are 0 to 1e9. Reload keeps it. `footage.info` reports the panel's `timecode`.

## Tests
- `start_timecode_only_relabels_source_time` (project): frames unchanged, `timecode()`, hostile values.
- `interpret_footage_start_timecode_relabels_source_time` (engine): the reply, the Footage panel's timecode, frame numbers, Use Source, reading at the footage's rate, bad values, undo.
- `replace_footage_and_reload_keep_sequences` keeps Override Start; `ui_drag_drop` checks the dialog's Start Timecode fields.
- Looked at the Interpret Footage dialog in a headless snapshot.

## Not checked
macOS / Linux, the browser build in a browser (wasm builds).

`cargo fmt --check`; clippy `-D warnings --all-targets` (project, engine, ui-egui, web); project, engine, media footage and ui-egui lib / ui_drag_drop / ui_panels tests; `cargo xtask wasm`.

title: Export: Render Queue jobs keep a layer cache and render on one compositor (#413, #414)
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #413 and #414, both reported by @pat-the-wizard, whose diagnoses this follows. One commit per issue.

## #413: Render Queue export never used the layer cache
**Cause:** `pipeline::Cx::render_at` built the job's `Renderer` without a `cache`. Every layer of every frame rendered from scratch (source, masks, effects, styles). The GPU compositor keys its uploads by the cached buffers, so it also uploaded every layer again on every frame.

**Fix:** each job (`Cx`) now owns a `LayerCache`, the same type the viewer uses. Its budget is the cache's default of 1 GiB, which is also the default Settings ▸ Memory & CPU layer cache. The job's parallel frames share it, and it is dropped when the job ends. With deferred GPU readbacks (browser job workers) it holds the accelerator's miss gate, as the workers' own caches do. `Cx::renderer` builds the job's renderer (options, accelerator, cache).

## #414: GPU export gave different pixels from run to run
**Cause:** jobs rendered with `Backend::Auto`. Auto picks the CPU or the GPU compositor for each frame from measured frame times (`AutoPick`: warm-up on both sides, then a re-probe every 48 frames). The two compositors differ slightly, so a frame came out differently depending on which side the timings favoured in that run.

**Fix:** a job renders every frame on the project's renderer, as After Effects renders a job with one renderer. That means `Backend::Gpu` with Mercury GPU Acceleration and `Backend::Cpu` with Mercury Software Only. Frames the GPU declines still render on the CPU, as in every GPU render, and that choice depends on the frame's content, not on timing. The viewer and previews keep Auto. architecture.md, parity.md and web.md now say this.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Layer cache in Render Queue jobs | none | one per job (1 GiB) |
| Compositor per frame (GPU project, accelerator attached) | Auto, from frame times | always the GPU |
| Demo comp, 60 frames 1920×1080, `render --gpu`, debug build, Vulkan | ≈ 4…

title: Fix live preview freezing during rapid property edits
author: cdinhoo
body:
Rapid property edits can leave the Composition viewer frozen until the drag stops, even when individual frames render in a few milliseconds. Each UI pass may apply the next edit before the viewer looks up its frame. The cache then contains completed revision N, but the viewer only accepts the exact key for N+1 and keeps showing the image from before the drag.

This change prefers the exact requested frame, then advances to the newest completed edit at the same composition, time, scale, view and render settings while that frame is pending. Revision bounds prevent out-of-order completions from making the preview jump backward. The final edit still converges to its exact frame, and undo continues to reuse cached content. Active and passive composition viewers use the same selection rule; passive viewers also refresh the revision when they reuse an unchanged texture.

Validation:

- Deterministic regression fails on the original code: an 80% opacity frame finishes, another edit is pending, and the viewer incorrectly remains at 100% opacity. It passes with the fix.
- Regression coverage includes opacity, position, anchor point, Gaussian Blur, an effect center, exact final convergence, undo/cache reuse, out-of-order completion, and rejection of other times/views/render settings.
- All 344 UI tests passed on Apple Silicon macOS, including the Metal-backed ScriptUI rendering test; 11 optional/manual tests were skipped. UI crate clippy passed with warnings denied.
- Native-worker probe: a plain 1920×1080 solid with 120 opacity edits at 60 inputs/second produced 0 displayed updates before this change and 119 after. The longest hold fell from approximately 2,003 ms to 25 ms. This probe includes headless egui layout and native frame workers, not OS window presentation or GPU upload; it is not a universal FPS claim.
- Interactive Mac test: the reporter ran a release build and confirmed that dragging and scrubbing Opacity now update smoothly.

author: Aavirash
body:
Three viewer/direct-manipulation fixes and one credit entry, found while testing the shape tools on macOS. Rebased onto v0.7.0.

## The shape tools' drag preview

The preview was a bare 1 px axis-aligned rectangle for every tool (rectangle, rounded rectangle, ellipse, polygon, star), which reads as no preview at all against most comps. It now draws the tool's own path, from the engine's own geometry, filled with the Tools bar's Fill and outlined in its Stroke, with a caption saying where the shape lands — a mask on the selected layer, into the selected shape layer, or a new shape layer.

The ghost and the released shape go through one normalisation, so the drag shows exactly what it commits. Three tests, including one that measures the ghost's pixels mid-drag (it fails against the old code).

## A layer drag moves the picture

Every pointer move replaces the comp's content identity, giving the frame on screen a new cache key while its render is still in flight. The viewer only ever showed an exact key, so the picture froze on the last completed frame until the drag ended. While a drag or a property scrub is running it now shows the newest frame of the same comp, frame, scale, view and render options that is ready — a render behind, as After Effects does — and returns to exact frames when it stops. This merges with v0.7.0's `minify`/`refit` handling in the same block. A test drags a layer and checks its pixels move while the button is still down (it fails against the old code).

title: Text and viewer fidelity: glyph seams, overlay fringes, text raster scale, viewer minification (#415, #416, #390, #417)
author: bflatastic
body:
Rendering-fidelity fixes from the measured reports (G1). One commit per issue.

## #415 Text: a light seam where two glyphs touch

**Cause:** every glyph's fill was rasterised and composited on its own. Where two glyphs share an edge (the crossbars of "ff"), two half-covered pixels composited to 0.75 coverage instead of 1, which shows as a thin light seam. After Effects draws the line as one outline.

**Fix:** consecutive fill passes of the same opaque colour, without Blur, under Normal Inter-Character Blending, are rasterised as one coverage mask. The glyph outlines are taken in layer space and wound the same way, so overlaps add up under NonZero instead of cancelling (mirrored characters, mixed fonts). Characters of other colours, translucent or blurred characters, strokes and the other blending modes are still drawn one by one, as before.

## #416 Gradient Overlay: light fringe on anti-aliased edges

**Cause:** the interior styles were blended over the layer body with the content's coverage folded into their opacity. On a half-covered edge pixel, the overlay went over the half-transparent body as a half-transparent layer. The result kept a quarter of the layer's own fill, and its alpha rose to 0.75: a light rim on styled white text.

**Fix:** `blend_clipped` composites the interior styles onto the layer *within its shape*, like a clipped layer: it divides the body by the content coverage, blends in the style at the style's own opacity, then multiplies the coverage back. The layer keeps its alpha, and an edge pixel mixes only the style and the background. This covers Gradient Overlay, Color Overlay, Satin, Inner Glow, Inner Shadow and the inside part of Stroke. Fill Opacity and Blend Interior Styles as Group work as before. (There is no Pattern Overlay style in EffectCraft yet.)

## #390 Text sharp at any scale (Continuously Rasterize), reworking #200

**Why kinetic_typography failed:** the test's time-remap key at 1.9 s sits on frame 23 (1.917 s). So at main-comp…

author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #412, #411, #410 (Romasikkk's Blender EXR / OCIO workflow).

## #412 Layered EXR shows the beauty pass, not Cryptomatte

**Cause.** A multi-layer OpenEXR without an unnamed RGB layer showed its first colour layer unless one was named combined / beauty / rgba. A Blender compositor File Output names the beauty pass `Image`, and Cryptomatte layers (lowercase `r, g, b, a`) sort first, so the picture was `CryptoMaterial00`.

**Fix.** `crates/media/src/exr_channels.rs` picks the unnamed RGB layer, else the beauty pass by the last part of its name (Combined, Beauty, Image, RGBA, RGB, Color), else the first colour layer that isn't a data pass. Cryptomatte, depth, mist, normals, vectors, positions and IDs are never the picture. A layer without R/G/B now shows its own first channel as grey, not the file's first channel. After Effects shows a file's main RGBA channels and leaves other layers to EXtractoR; this does the same for files that keep the beauty in a named layer. No layer picker was added to Interpret Footage, because After Effects has none.

## #411 Interpret Footage ▸ Preserve RGB

**Cause.** Float footage was always sRGB-encoded on decode (`convert.rs`), and Interpret Footage had no way to turn that off. An OCIO effect on the layer therefore converted values that were already encoded.

**Fix.** Added After Effects' Interpret Footage ▸ Color ▸ **Preserve RGB** (`Footage::preserve_rgb`, `file.interpretFootage {"preserveRgb": true}`, a checkbox in the Interpret Footage form, carried by Remember / Apply Interpretation). With it, the decoder keeps a float file's linear values. The working-space conversion from the colour profile and Interpret As Linear Light don't apply, so the file's values enter the comp unconverted. The media cache key includes the flag, so both interpretations of one file decode separately.

My reading of After Effects: Preserve RGB means "no colour conversion for this item", which is why it also overrides Assign Profile (AE greys that out) an…

title: Timeline: every property has a pick whip in the Parent & Link column (#363)
author: bflatastic
body:
The last part of #363: since CC 2018, After Effects has a property pick whip next to every property in the Timeline's Parent & Link column. This PR adds it.

## What
- **Property pick whip.** Every property row that can take an expression (it has a stopwatch) now has a pick whip in the Parent & Link column. It sits where the layer's parent pick whip sits and looks the same. Its automation id is `timeline.prop.<uid>.propertyPickWhip`; the expression row's existing pick whip keeps `timeline.prop.<uid>.pickWhip`.
- **What a drop does.** Dragging it onto another property's name or value runs `prop.pickWhip`. The reference becomes the property's expression: it is added if there is none and replaces the existing one otherwise, and the expression is turned on even if it was disabled. Dropping on one value of a multi-dimensional property picks that dimension (`transform.position[1]`). `prop.pickWhip` already handles mismatched dimensions (`temp = …; [temp, temp]`).
- **Shared code.** The parent, expression and property pick whips now use one widget (`pick_whip`) and one drop path, which covers the rubber band, the target highlight, autoscroll at the edges and the dimension pick. Only the expression pick whip inserts at the cursor of an expression being edited.
- **Drops in Effect Controls.** The expression and property pick whips can now also be dropped on properties in Effect Controls, as in After Effects. While a pick whip is being dragged, Effect Controls registers its property rows as targets, along with the value field of each dimension. It works whichever panel draws first.
- `docs/parity.md` and `docs/agents.md` are updated.

After Effects behaviour, from Adobe's public docs:
- Adobe's April 2018 release notes: the Property Link pick whip adds an expression to the linked property "without having to enable expressions first".

title: Effects: CC Particle World follows the comp camera (#397)
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #397: CC Particle World ignored the comp's 3D camera and looked flat.

## Cause
`particle_world_plan` (crates/effects/src/sim.rs) projected the particles through a fixed camera: 2 layer widths in front of the layer centre (`cam = 2.0`). It never asked the host for the comp camera, so moving or orbiting a camera layer left the particles flat on the layer. The effect also had no Extras ▸ Effect Camera.

While testing the fix, I found a second bug. The layer cache key left out the comp camera and lights. So the effects that read them (Card Dance / Shatter / Card Wipe with Comp Camera or First Comp Light, Caustics, and now Particle World) kept showing a stale frame after the camera, a light or the layer moved.

## Fix
- **Comp camera.** The Cycore FX HD manual (CC Particle World) says the effect "automatically selects an AE comp camera if present and enabled", and that the Camera controls "are used only when no AE camera is present". So when the comp has an active camera layer, Particle World now sees its particles through that camera. It uses Card Dance's comp-camera projection, factored out as `card3d::comp_proj`. A new `Proj::view` returns each particle's depth, sprite scale and screen velocity. `CompScene::camera_layer` tells a camera layer apart from the comp's default view. Card Dance and the other effects still use the default view as before.
- **Extras ▸ Effect Camera.** Otherwise the effect uses its own camera, with new controls: Distance (default 2), Rotation X / Y / Z (0) and FOV (50). The camera orbits the world origin, which is the layer centre. Changing FOV moves the camera so that the origin's plane keeps the scale Distance gives it; the manual says "the camera automatically adjusts its distance to the FOV value". With the defaults, the result is exactly the old fixed camera: the golden hashes don't change, and projects saved before this change render as before. Bad values are clamped (Distance ≥ 0.01, FOV 1–179°, non-finite values fall back to the …

title: MCP: return on write errors while stdin is open; document requests during a render
author: storybored379
body:
Follow-ups to the review on #365, thanks for the careful read.

1. **Hang in `serve`.** Confirmed: with stdin still open, a failed write left `thread::scope` waiting on the input thread. The reader thread is now detached, so `serve` returns the write error at once. `serve` takes a `'static` reader as a result: `serve_stdio` is unchanged, and four tests now pass an owned `Cursor`. New test `broken_output_returns_while_stdin_stays_open` keeps stdin open with a `Broken` writer. It times out on main and passes with the change.
2. **Edits during a render.** New test `second_render_is_refused_and_edits_apply_during_a_render`. While a blocking render runs, a second render is refused whether it is blocking, `wait: false` or inside a batch. A `comp.new` sent mid-render is applied, and the job finishes its one item from its snapshot. docs/mcp.md has a new "Requests during a render" section covering this: edits change the project but not the running job, and an item removed mid-render is counted in `failed`. It also says that `renderQueue.render {"wait": false}` is not an MCP long call: it returns the ids at once, you poll `renderQueue.list` and stop it with `renderQueue.stop`.
3. **Docs.** docs/mcp.md now says that `isError` is true for any JSON result with `failed > 0` (a batch with a failed step, a render with unfinished items), and to read `results` / `items` for details.

Validation: automation unit tests 37/37 over five runs, plus the integration tests. Formatting, strict workspace clippy, layers and assets pass.

Found and fixed with Claude Code (AI-assisted).

title: Viewer: each composition keeps its Resolution in the project, as in After Effects (#417)
author: bflatastic
body:
Completes #417. #444 fixed the soft text. The open part was that After Effects saves each composition's viewer Resolution with the project, and EffectCraft didn't.

## What
- **The Resolution belongs to the comp.** `Resolution` (Auto, Full, Half, Third, Quarter, Custom) moved from the UI into the project crate, and the comp stores it as `Comp::resolution`. The viewer reads the active comp's value (`EffectcraftApp::viewer_res`); `ViewerState` no longer has a global `res`. Switching to another comp shows that comp's resolution. Switching back, or saving and reopening the project, shows the one it had.
- **File format.** `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Resolution::is_auto")]`: Auto isn't written. Projects saved before this change open with Auto, and older versions ignore the new field. A hostile Custom factor in a file is clamped to 1..40 when it is rendered.
- **No undo step, project modified.** After Effects keeps view changes like this out of the undo history. `Session::set_resolution` changes the project without recording a step and marks it modified, because the value is saved in the file. Undo, redo and History jumps restore everything else but carry the current resolutions over (`keep_view_settings`). Without that, undoing an unrelated edit would also reset the resolution.
- **Caches stay valid.** The Resolution is outside `Comp::same_pixels` and is normalised in `Comp::pixel_form`, as Hide Shy is (#103). Changing it keeps the comp's RAM frame identity and disk-cache key, so the frames already cached at the new scale show at once.
- **Commands and agent access.** `view.res.full|half|third|quarter|custom` are now engine commands instead of frontend-only ones, so they work headless too. `view.res.auto` is new (the panel popup's Auto). Each takes an optional `comp`. `view.res.custom` without a `factor` still opens the Custom Resolution dialog through the frontend. `ui.set {viewer: {res}}` sets the active comp's resolution and now rejects an unknown name in…

title: Windows installer: choose the install folder, and keep it on upgrade
author: tylerjenningsw
body:
The Windows MSI installs straight into Program Files with no way to pick another folder: `effectcraft.wxs` authors no setup dialogs. This adds a small setup wizard with a destination-folder page, and makes later installs reuse the chosen folder.

Related: #343 (desktop shortcut option during install). That's a separate request, but it would add a checkbox to the same wizard.

## What changes for people installing

- **Fresh install:** a destination page (default `C:\Program Files\EffectCraft\`, editable, **Change...** opens a folder browser with Up / New folder), then a Ready page that shows the exact folder before anything is written.
- **Upgrade:** goes straight to the Ready page with the installed copy's folder ("Version X will replace it in the same folder"); Back is disabled, so an upgrade can't move the install.
- **Opening the MSI when that version is already installed:** Repair or Remove.
- Cancel, finished, cancelled, failed, files-in-use and Windows Installer error dialogs are all authored.
- **Silent installs** still need no UI: `msiexec /i effectcraft-<ver>-windows-x64.msi /qn INSTALLFOLDER="D:\Apps\EffectCraft"`. Without `INSTALLFOLDER`, a silent upgrade stays in the existing folder.

## How

- `effectcraft.wxs`: writes the folder as the App Paths `Path` value (the standard place for an app's folder), reads it back with a `RegistrySearch` into `PREVIOUSINSTALLFOLDER`, and sets `INSTALLFOLDER` from it after `AppSearch` unless `INSTALLFOLDER` was given. `INSTALLFOLDER` is `Secure` so the folder chosen in the UI reaches the elevated install. v0.6.0 and earlier have no `Path` value, so they upgrade in Program Files, where they already are.
- `installer-ui.wxs` (new): the dialogs, using only Windows Installer's built-in controls and events (`PathEdit`, `DirectoryCombo`, `DirectoryList`, `SetTargetPath`, ...). **It deliberately doesn't use WiX's `WixUI_InstallDir`:** the WixUI dialog library is MS-RL, which isn't on the allowed-licence list in AGENTS.md. The …

title: fix: CLI --bitrate now applies to VP9 WebM (#440)
author: mjohnson7cd
body:
Fixes #440

## Summary
The CLI `--bitrate` flag was silently ignored for VP9 WebM output. It set the render queue bitrate parameter but never enabled `webmBitrate`, so the VP9 encoder used quality mode instead of targeting the specified bitrate.

## Changes
- **apps/effectcraft-cli/src/main.rs**: When `--bitrate` is specified, check if format is WebM (via `OutputFormat::from_name`) and set `webmBitrate:true`
  - Uses the format parser itself, so automatically covers all aliases: `webm`, `vp9`, `webmvp9opus`, etc.
- **apps/effectcraft-cli/tests/cli.rs**: Added `render_bitrate_applies_to_vp9_webm` test verifying different bitrates produce different file sizes

## Testing
**Automated:**
```bash
CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target/gate cargo test -p effectcraft-cli render_bitrate_applies_to_vp9_webm
```
✅ Test passes: 100 kbps < 8000 kbps file size  
✅ Test verified to FAIL without fix (byte-identical output)

**Manual verification:**
- `--format webm --bitrate 100`: 9,531 bytes
- `--format vp9 --bitrate 100`: 9,531 bytes  
- `--format webmvp9opus --bitrate 100`: 9,531 bytes
- `.webm` extension inference: 9,531 bytes
- `--bitrate 8000`: 17,601 bytes (correctly larger)
- `--video-quality 40` (no bitrate): still works

**Quality gates:**
✅ `cargo fmt`  
✅ `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`

## Code Review
Reviewed by independent Claude Opus instance in ponytail mode - **APPROVED**

## Notes
- Matches existing behavior for H.264
- Does not cover AV1 WebM (uses separate encoder path that already handles bitrate correctly)
- Does not affect UI (which already sends `webmBitrate`)
- Quality mode (`--video-quality`) still works when `--bitrate` not specified

title: Scripting: importFile(ImportOptions) imports one file unless sequence is set (#475)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #475.

In After Effects, `ImportOptions.sequence` defaults to `false`, so `app.project.importFile(io)` imports only the picked file; with `io.sequence = true` it imports the numbered run. EffectCraft always imported the whole run because the scripting prelude never passed the flag to `file.import`.

- `Project.importFile` now passes `sequence: !!opts.sequence` when it gets an `ImportOptions`. A bare `File` argument keeps today's call unchanged.
- New script test: three numbered PNGs in a temp dir; `ImportOptions` with the default `sequence` imports `shot_0002.png` as a Still, and with `sequence = true` it imports `shot_[0001-0003].png` as a Sequence. The first assertion fails without the fix.

title: Expressions: Add Expression applies to the selected properties (#476)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #476.

**Animation > Add Expression** (Alt+Shift+=) sends `prop.setExpression` with no parameters. `set_expr` started with `prop_ref`, which needs `path` or `prop`, so the command always failed with "missing `path` ... or `prop` uid", even with a property selected in the Timeline.

**Change** (`crates/engine/src/commands/prop.rs`)
- When `path` or `prop` is given, nothing changes: the stopwatch Alt-click, scripts, the pick whip and the other internal callers resolve the property through `prop_ref` as before.
- When both are missing, the command uses the properties selected in the Timeline (`selected_leaf_props`, so a selected group expands to its properties). Each one gets the same add-or-toggle as an Alt-click on its stopwatch, starting from the property's own reference. All of them change in one undoable "Expression" edit.
- With nothing selected, it returns the same message as `essential.addProperty`: "select a property in the timeline (or give `layer` and `path`)".
- The per-property logic moved into `apply_expr` so that both paths share it. For a single explicit property the return value is the same as before. Without `path`/`prop` it returns an array with one entry per property.

**Test**
`add_expression_without_path_uses_the_selected_property` (`tests_timeline.rs`): `{}` with nothing selected gives the select-a-property error. After `prop.select` on Opacity, `{}` adds `transform.opacity`, and one undo removes it. Without the fix the first assertion fails because the old error is "missing `path`".

title: EXR: do not double the part name of Blender 5 per-pass parts (#481)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #481.

Blender 5.0-5.2 save a multi-layer EXR with one part per pass. Each part is named after its pass, and its channels keep the full name: part `ViewLayer.Depth` holds `ViewLayer.Depth.Z`. `read_exr_channels` put the part name in front of every channel, so the plane became `ViewLayer.Depth.ViewLayer.Depth.Z`. EXtractoR did not find Mist/Depth, and Cryptomatte lost ranks 2-5.

The plane name now comes from a small helper, `channel_name`. It adds the part name only when the channel name does not already start with `<part>.` (the dot is part of the check). Single-part files and named parts with bare channels (`R`, `Z`) keep the names they get today. Blender 5 names now match what a single-part Blender file gives, so Cryptomatte rank and manifest matching works the same way for both.

Tests:
- `part_name_is_not_doubled_when_channels_carry_it`: Blender 5 style (already prefixed), a bare channel in a named part, a channel that only starts with the part name without the dot, and the unnamed part.
- `blender5_multipart_file_keeps_pass_names`: writes a two-part EXR (`ViewLayer.Depth` + `ViewLayer.Combined`) and checks that `ViewLayer.Depth.Z` is read and the doubled name is gone. Without the fix this test fails.

title: Project: Shift+Delete skips the deletion confirmation (#484)
author: tylerjenningsw
body:
Adds Shift+Delete in the Project panel to delete the selected items without the in-use confirmation. Reuses the existing `project.delete` command, so dependent layers go with the items and one Undo restores everything. Files on disk are untouched.

Closes #484.

## Changes

- **New command:** `project.deleteWithoutConfirmation` ("Delete Project Items Without Confirmation"), default **Shift+Delete**. It's a frontend command, so it appears in Keyboard Shortcuts (rebindable) and runs by id over the control channel and MCP. The UI runs `project.delete` for it.
- **Project panel only:** with another panel focused it does nothing. Like every shortcut, it doesn't fire while typing or with a dialog open. Plain Delete/Backspace are unchanged: they still ask when compositions use the items.
- **Windows:** egui-winit sends Shift+Delete as a **Cut** event, not a key press (Windows' old Cut shortcut; `is_cut_command` in egui-winit). EffectCraft mapped that to Ctrl+X, which is why Shift+Delete only showed "Project clipboard actions are not supported yet". In the Project panel, which has no clipboard, a Cut with only Shift held is now Shift+Delete. Elsewhere it still cuts. Clipboard events carry no modifiers, and `i.modifiers` is the state after the whole frame, so Cut, Copy and Paste are now read with the modifiers at their place in the frame's events. The walk starts from the state the previous pass ended with. When that isn't known, a Cut is never Shift+Delete, so a Ctrl+X followed in the same frame by Ctrl up and Shift down can't delete anything.
- **No hidden bypass flag:** the Delete Items prompt used to set `answered` so the next `project.delete` skipped the prompt. Its Delete button now runs that request directly (`delete_items::delete_confirmed`), the same path Shift+Delete uses, so a confirmation can't carry over to a later deletion.

- A comp, a solid in…

title: Render: text layers are always continuously rasterised, at exactly their on-screen scale (re-land #200)
author: EthanSuquet
body:
Re-lands #200 (reverted in 29c4d3a), with a fix for the `kinetic::kinetic_typography` failure @echelon found.

**Why the QA test broke.** Your guess was right: it's the quarter-octave rounding in `raster_scale`. With #200 the "Sub" text layer, whose scale is driven by an expression, became continuously rasterised. At the line-78 comparison the two renders land on either side of the 2^-¼ ≈ 84.09 % step:

| Render | Time in "Type Pre" | Sub's on-screen scale | Raster scale |
|---|---|---|---|
| precomp directly at 1.6 s | 1.600000 | 0.840003 | 0.8409 |
| parent at 0.3 s, through the time remap | 1.602609 (the 1.9 s key snaps to frame 23) | 0.841047 | **1.0** |

So a 0.1 % scale difference rasterised the text at a different resolution. On macOS that stays under the 1.0 threshold, but FreeBSD went over it. It's also a visible bug on its own: any text whose scale animates would pop each time it crossed a step.

**Fix:** text is rasterised at *exactly* its on-screen scale, with no quarter-octave rounding. `text::render` is continuous in its scale, so the output now changes smoothly with Scale. Shape layers and vector footage keep the quarter-octave steps under Continuously Rasterize, and the clamp and the 16-million-pixel cap still apply to text. `docs/architecture.md` is updated.

**Tests**
- New `text_scale_changes_smoothly_across_a_raster_step` renders 60 px text at 83.8 %, 84.0 % and 84.2 % scale. It checks that crossing the step changes the image no more than 1.5× as much as the same change within a step:
  - with #200 alone: across 0.00197 vs within 0.00055 (3.6×), **fails**;
  - with this PR: 0.00089 vs 0.00077 (1.16×), passes.
- `text_scaled_up_stays_sharp_without_the_switch` from #200 is back and passes.
- `kinetic_typography` line 78, `mean_diff(fwd, rev)` with a 1.0 threshold, on macOS: main 0.656, #200 alone 0.744, this PR **0.644**.
- `cargo xtask ci` on macOS: fmt, clippy, layers and assets pass. The workspace tests (`--release --no-fail-fast`) give 2445 pas…

title: Fix web playback performance with stacked footage
author: daijro
body:
Fixes performance issues in web builds by shrinking the caches, converting video frames at the size they're shown, and rounding faster.

- **Smaller caches in the browser.** Layer cache is capped at 512 MB and footage cache at 256 MB on wasm. Before, eight stacked 1080p clips ran the page out of memory after about 45s. Now it levels off around 3.8 GB.
- **Convert frames at the shown size.** Below Full resolution, movie frames were converted to RGBA at full size and then scaled down. Now they're downscaled in YUV first. Conversion goes from about 16ms to 4ms per 1080p layer.
- **Faster 8/16 bpc rounding on wasm.** Uses `floor` instead of the integer cast, with identical values. Goes from 16ms to 10ms per layer.

Playback at Third resolution, 1/2/4/8 layers: 24/12/6/3 fps → 29/15/7.5/3.9 fps. Full resolution is 5–18% faster.

Full-resolution frames are pixel-identical to main. Reduced-size frames differ by 0.01/255 on average. All tests pass. Clippy on stable (1.99) only flags `crates/effects/src/ocio.rs`, which this doesn't touch, and it does the same on main.

title: Plug-ins: opt-in OpenFX host (feature openfx)
author: glumbis
body:
An **opt-in OpenFX (OFX) plug-in host**, so OFX image-effect plug-ins (the cross-host standard used by Nuke, Resolve, Vegas, Natron…) run as ordinary EffectCraft effects. Opened as a **draft for discussion**: I asked on Discord whether this could be welcome upstream, and I'm happy to change the approach, split it up, or keep it in my fork if it doesn't fit.

## ⚠️ The `unsafe` question (please read first)

AGENTS.md forbids `unsafe` and EffectCraft's plug-ins are deliberately sandboxed WebAssembly. An OFX host **cannot** follow either rule: OFX plug-ins are native C/C++ libraries, and calling them from Rust needs `unsafe` (Rust can't check code it didn't compile). So this PR is built to keep that contained:

- **Off by default.** Nothing changes for normal builds. The host is only compiled in with `--features openfx` (`effectcraft-host/openfx`, forwarded by `effectcraft` and `effectcraft-cli`). Without it the two new commands are disabled ("OpenFX plug-ins are not available in this build") and no native code is ever loaded.
- **One crate.** All `unsafe` lives in `crates/ofx` (`effectcraft-ofx`), the only crate that doesn't opt into `[lints] workspace = true`. It keeps the never-crash lints (`deny(unwrap_used, expect_used, panic, …)`); every host callback is wrapped in `catch_unwind`, null-checks pointers and validates handles by magic number. On wasm32 the crate is empty.
- **Plug-ins can still crash the app.** A bug in a native plug-in can't be caught. A crash *while loading* is remembered in a blocklist (`ofx_blocklist.txt` in the config folder) and that plug-in is skipped next launch; `EFFECTCRAFT_NO_OFX=1` skips OFX entirely. This is documented as the reason it's opt-in (`docs/ofx.md`).

If you'd rather not have native plug-ins in the repo at all, that's completely fine; the plug-in API 2 part (below) might still be useful on its own.

## What's in it

| Part | What |
|---|---|
| **Plug-in API 2** (`crates/effects/src/plugin.rs`) | Additive to API 1 (WebAssembly…

title: fix(engine): layer.setText schema requires optional OpenType keys (#520)
author: mjohnson7cd
body:
## Summary
Fixes #520 — the `layer.setText` command schema now correctly marks `OpenType` and `ss01` as optional parameters instead of required.

## Problem
The parameter doc string had:
- `OpenType: discretionaryLigatures?` — prose label parsed as a required key
- `ss01…ss20?` — shorthand parsed as a required `ss01` key

The schema generator treated `key:` syntax as a required parameter. This caused JSON Schema validators to reject valid font/style edits that didn't include OpenType features:

```json
{"layer":"Title", "font":"Arial", "style":"Regular"}
```

## Solution
Changed the parameter doc to mark both as optional:
- `OpenType: discretionaryLigatures?` → `OpenType?: discretionaryLigatures?`
- `ss01…ss20?` → `ss01?…ss20?`

The schema generator now correctly treats them as optional (line 316 in `commands/mod.rs` checks for `key?` pattern).

## Files Changed
- `crates/engine/src/commands/layer.rs`: Updated `layer.setText` params doc
- `crates/effects/src/ocio.rs`: Fixed clippy lint (use `as_chunks` instead of `chunks_exact`)

## Testing
✅ `cargo fmt --check` — passed  
✅ `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` — passed  
✅ `cargo test -p effectcraft-engine` — all 445 tests passed  

The fix is a schema correction. Existing tests verify `layer.setText` works with font/style edits.

## Verification
After this fix, the schema correctly accepts:
```json
{"layer":"Title", "font":"Arial", "style":"Regular"}
```

And still accepts OpenType features when provided:
```json
{"layer":"Title", "font":"Arial", "style":"Regular", "discretionaryLigatures": true, "ss01": true}
```
