title: PDF: bound what any stream filter may decode to
author: haranishi
body:
`object::decode_stream` put no limit on what a `/Filter` chain may decode to. Deflate expands up to about 1000:1, the other filters can also turn a few bytes into a lot, and a `/Filter` array may repeat a filter, so each stage multiplies the last; a failed allocation aborts the process. `File::parse` decodes every `/Type /ObjStm` stream eagerly, before any page is chosen, so a PDF of a few MB holding such a stream asks for gigabytes just by being imported or probed (`media/layered.rs`). The PSD and segment decoders already use bounded variants.

## What changes

Two commits, so each can be read on its own.

**FlateDecode** (`crates/pdf/src/object.rs`)

- `inflate(data, max)` uses the `*_with_limit` functions. A stream that inflates to more than `max` is undecodable (`None`); it is not salvaged as a truncated one. The buffer of the truncated-stream fallback is bounded by `max` too (`salvage_len`): it was eight times the input.
- `decode_stream` bounds each filter to `MAX_INFLATED` = 1 GiB. The largest image `image::decode` accepts (64 Mi pixels of four 16-bit components) is 512 MiB, so this leaves room. The eager object-stream loop in `File::parse` uses `MAX_OBJECT_STREAM` = 256 MiB, because those streams hold only dictionaries, arrays, numbers and strings. On 32-bit targets (the web build) both are a quarter of that, because the inflater's growing buffer can reserve about twice the limit and the address space is 4 GiB.
- `inflate` takes the limit as its second argument; it is only called inside this crate.

**The other filters** (`crates/pdf/src/object.rs`, `crates/pdf/src/ccitt.rs`)

- `decode_stream_within(…, max)` now requires the output of every stage, and of the predictor after it, to be at most `max`; otherwise the stream is undecodable (`None`, never a truncated prefix). Below `max` nothing changes.
- RunLengthDecode, LZWDecode, ASCIIHexDecode and ASCII85Decode stop as soon as their output would pass `max`. `ascii85` keeps its unbounded signature (the PostScr…

title: Scripts: a script name is a file name, not a path
author: haranishi
body:
`file.uninstallScript` joined the `name` from the request into `Scripts/<name>` and handed it to the settings store, which takes names as relative paths (`DirConfig` does `dir.join(name)`). So `name = "../../x.txt"` reached a file next to the settings folder and deleted it if it read as UTF-8 text, and `../prefs.json` deleted a settings file. `file.installScript` already reduces its path to a file name; `uninstall` did not. The same unsanitised join is in `script_code`, used by `file.runScript` and by opening a ScriptUI panel by name: it read such a file and ran it as a script. The commands are reachable through MCP and the control channel, and `file.uninstallScript` also from a script via `app.run` (only `file.runScript` and `script.run` are refused there).

## What changes

- `crates/engine/src/commands/scripts.rs`:
  - `is_bare_name`, on every platform: a name is one path component, so not empty, not `.` or `..`, and without `/`, `\` or NUL.
  - `windows_unsafe_name`, applied only on Windows (elsewhere those are ordinary file names): a `:` (drive or stream), a trailing `.` or space, and the device names `CON`, `PRN`, `AUX`, `NUL`, `CONIN$`, `CONOUT$`, `COM0`-`COM9` and `LPT0`-`LPT9` (also with the superscript digits), which Windows treats as the device in any folder and with any extension (`con.jsx`).
  - `uninstall` and `script_code` require a `.jsx`/`.js` name that passes `is_script_name` (an invalid name is a `BadParams` error, or "not found" for run-by-name); `install` refuses a file name that could not then be run or uninstalled (a `\` in the file name on Unix); the script list skips such files so the menu does not offer what run and uninstall would refuse. The settings store is untouched.
- Scope: `../x` only reaches the settings root (for example `prefs.json`); `../../x` leaves it.

## Tests

title: Import animated GIFs as movies
author: Limestudio90
body:
## Problem

Animated GIFs were imported as a single still image (one frame, zero duration): `probe_bytes` sent every format `image` recognises, GIF included, through the still path, and FilmCraft's movie decoders don't read GIF.

## Fix

In `effectcraft-media`:

- A GIF with two or more frames is probed as a `Video` footage item. Its frame rate is `100 / gcd(frame delays in hundredths of a second)`, so every delay is a whole number of frames and uneven timing is kept exactly. Duration is the sum of the delays. Delays of 0 or 1 count as 10, like in browsers.
- `MediaPool` decodes the GIF once per file (frames composited on the full canvas by the `image` crate, kept as 8-bit RGBA, capped at 1 GiB) and returns the frame shown at the requested time.
- A single-frame GIF stays a still. A damaged GIF returns an error; a damaged tail keeps the frames before it.
- New `gif_anim` module, plus `gif` added to the crate's dependencies (already in the workspace).

## Tests

Four new unit tests in `gif_anim.rs`: timing and frame lookup with uneven delays, zero delay, single-frame GIF, damaged file. `cargo test -p effectcraft-media`, `cargo clippy -p effectcraft-media --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check -p effectcraft-media` pass on Rust 1.95. I also imported an animated GIF in the desktop app on Windows 11 and it plays.

## Notes

- The GIF imports with a single play (`loop_count` 1); looping can be set in Interpret Footage. The file's own loop count is not read.
- I couldn't get a green `cargo xtask ci` to compare against: at `813c7c4`, clippy `-D warnings` already fails on Rust 1.95 (`crates/psd/src/lib.rs:660`, `collapsible_match`) and on 1.99 (`crates/effects/src/ocio.rs:375`, `chunks_exact_to_as_chunks`), unrelated to this change.

title: PDF colour spaces and functions: bound sizes, depth and stacks
author: haranishi
body:
A PDF's colour spaces and functions are read when its pages are, that is, just by opening or probing the file (`color_space`, `Func::read`). Several numbers and references in them were trusted, and each let a few hundred bytes abort the process: an allocation that fails, a stack that overflows, or a panic.

## What changes (`crates/pdf/src/color.rs`)

- **Indexed colour spaces.** `hival` is clamped to 255. An image builds its palette from every entry up to it, so `[/Indexed /DeviceRGB 1000000000000 <00>]` asked for 24 TB.
- **Sampled functions (FunctionType 0).** The table is `entries × outputs`, and the outputs (one per `/Range` pair) had no bound and were multiplied unchecked. `sample_count` multiplies with `checked_mul` and refuses a table over 2^24 samples (128 MiB; a 33 × 33 × 33 × 33 CMYK grid with four outputs fits), and a function has at most 32 inputs and 32 outputs (no colour space has more components than that, and every evaluation allocates `outputs` values). The samples are an `Arc<[f64]>`: the graphics state is copied at every `q`, which copied the table each time.
- **Fan-out through references.** One top-level `Func::read` has a budget: at most 10,000 `Func` nodes and 2^24 samples in total, and past it the whole function is `Func::Unsupported` (a colour space then takes its usual fallback, a Separation tint reads as grey). A function array (one function per output) holds at most 32 elements, and an object listed several times in an array is read once; a stitching function's pieces have no cap of their own, because a repeating gradient lists one piece once per repeat (the node budget bounds it). Before, objects listing each other 32 times over eight levels built 32^8 sub-functions, and a hundred references to one 128 MiB table built it a hundred times.
- **Depth.** Colour spaces nest at most 8 levels (an Indexed base, an ICCBased, Separation or DeviceN alternate) and functions at most 8 (arrays, stitching functions); deeper reads as DeviceGray / an un…

title: Reload Footage shows new pixels and keeps Photoshop layers; Reload Footage Changed on Disk
author: KattKnight
body:
## What this does

Editing a Photoshop file in another app (PhotoCraft, Photoshop) and coming back to EffectCraft now shows the change, without any extra step, and File ▸ Reload Footage works for layered files.

### 1. Reload Footage fixes

On 0.6.0, two things go wrong with File ▸ Reload Footage (Cmd+Alt+L):

- **The old pixels stay.** `file.reloadFootage` updates the item's metadata, but the media pool's decoded frames and the session's layer cache are keyed by path and item, so the next render serves the old image until Edit ▸ Purge ▸ All Memory. To reproduce: import a red PNG into a comp, overwrite the file with a blue one of the same size, then Reload Footage. The comp stays red.
- **Photoshop layer items lose their layer.** Reload replaced the whole `Footage` with `importer.probe(path)`, which describes the merged document. A layer imported with *Composition – Retain Layer Sizes* came back document-sized with `layer: None`. In our test a 32×64 layer became 64×64.

Reload now:
- re-reads only what the file decides: size, a movie's duration, streams and frame rate (the conformed rate stays), codec, and a data file's text;
- keeps what the project decided: the Photoshop layer or PDF page, and the interpretation;
- finds a Photoshop layer again by name when layers were added or removed around it, taking its new bounds for Retain Layer Sizes;
- then calls a new `FootageSource::forget(path)`, which `MediaPool` implements with its existing `forget` (now also dropping the EXR aux-channel cache, which had the same per-path staleness), and clears the layer cache.

This builds on the image-sequence handling that landed on 9 October: reload still probes with `Session::probe_footage`, a sequence picks up frames added to its run and keeps its frame rate and order, and `start_timecode` (with every other interpretation field) is kept. The 11 `tests_sequence` tests pass unchanged.

title: Tests: four failures on Windows (autosave paths, GPU viewer adapter, audio preview race)
author: KattKnight
body:
## What this does

Four tests fail on Windows on `main`. The app is fine in all four cases; the tests make assumptions that only hold on macOS/Linux or on slower machines. Seen on Windows 11 with an RTX 4060 Laptop GPU. Each failure was reproduced on unmodified `main` before fixing.

### `automation::tests::autosave_is_durable_before_reply_and_queries_do_not_rotate` and `cli::mcp_autosave_survives_kill_and_restart_without_touching_desktop_settings`

**Cause:** the MCP `initialize` instructions embed the auto-save state as JSON (`server.rs`, `format!("… {}", self.autosave_info())`). A Windows path's backslashes are escaped there, so `contains(path)` never matches.

**Fix:** the tests look for the JSON form of the path, `Value::from(path).to_string()`.

### `ui_gpu::viewer_draws_gpu_frames_that_match_the_cpu`

**Cause:**
- egui_kittest's default wgpu setup prefers a CPU adapter. On Windows that is WARP on DirectX 12.
- There, FXC fails to compile the compositor's `pointwise` kernel (`create_compute_pipeline … FXC D3DCompile error … compilation aborted unexpectedly`).
- So the viewer stays on the CPU, and the test fails at "GPU compositor on egui-wgpu's device" before comparing anything.

**Fix:** the harness is built on the adapter the headless compositor picked (`name (Backend)`), like the desktop app's window, and falls back to egui_kittest's choice if that adapter isn't listed.

**Result:** the test now composites on the RTX 4060 (Vulkan), and its frames match the CPU viewer.

The DirectX 12 / FXC failure itself isn't specific to the test: a desktop session whose window lands on DirectX 12 (for example `WGPU_BACKEND=dx12`) can't build the compositor and silently composites on the CPU. Possible fixes are DXC for DX12, preferring Vulkan for the window, or working around the construct FXC chokes on in `pointwise`. Happy to open an issue for it if that helps.

title: macOS: projects open from Finder; .pcraft is PhotoCraft's again
author: LloydNicholson
body:
## Problem
- **EffectCraft takes over PhotoCraft's files.** The app bundle exports `ai.storyteller.effectcraft.document` with the extension `.pcraft`, PhotoCraft's document format. With both apps installed, macOS resolves `.pcraft` to EffectCraft's type. EffectCraft declares no document types, so Finder offers neither app for a PhotoCraft document.
- **EffectCraft's own projects have no file type.** `.ecproj` and `.ecprojx` have no type, so double-clicking a project doesn't open EffectCraft.
- **`open -a` doesn't open projects.** `open -a EffectCraft x.ecproj` starts the app without opening the project. LaunchServices sends the path as a `kAEOpenDocuments` Apple event, which winit 0.30 doesn't handle.

## Fix
- **`packaging/macos/Info.plist.in`:**
  - The exported type now tags `.ecproj` and `.ecprojx` (the extensions the app's File > Open filter uses).
  - It's described as "EffectCraft Project" and conforms to `public.data` and `public.content` instead of `public.image`.
  - `CFBundleDocumentTypes` makes EffectCraft the owner of that type.
- **`apps/effectcraft/src/apple_events.rs`:** registers the Apple-event handler with the audited [`fmv-macos-events`](https://crates.io/crates/fmv-macos-events) crate (pinned `=0.1.0`), as PhotoCraft and PdfCraft do. The Objective-C interop stays inside that crate, so the workspace keeps `unsafe_code = "forbid"`.
  - Opened paths are handed to the existing dropped-file handling (`prefs_live::dropped_files`). A project opens through `file.open`, after the unsaved-changes prompt, and other files are imported.
  - A quit event closes the window.
- **Launch timing:** the event that launches the app arrives before the UI draws. `EffectcraftApp::ui` skips its first frames until the fonts are installed, and that frame consumed the injected drop. The paths now wait until a new `EffectcraftApp::is_ready()` reports true.

The Windows installer comment in `packaging/windows/effectcraft.wxs` still says `.pcraft` is owned by EffectCraft, but…

title: Rotation: dragging the degrees field can go negative
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Fixes #569

Dragging the degrees part of a rotation value could never go negative. The field shows the size of the remainder (the sign is drawn separately), and a drag was applied to that size and then the old sign was put back on. Dragging left past zero made the size negative, which flipped the angle back to positive, so the value bounced around zero. The same field is used for rotation in the Timeline and Properties panels and for angle parameters in Effect Controls, so all of them had it.

A drag now moves the angle by the pointer distance, so it runs through zero into negative angles. Typed values still keep the sign that is shown. Position, scale and the other signed properties never had this clamp (their range is already wide open), and opacity stays 0 to 100.

Tested with a unit test on the new helper in fx_widgets.rs that failed before the change (a 1 degree drag left from 0.3 gave -0.7 then bounced) and passes now. The ui-egui package passes clippy and its tests. `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo xtask layers`, `assets` and `wasm` pass. title: Linux: default to XWayland for file drag-and-drop on Wayland desktops
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
### Rationale & History

Under Wayland sessions, dragging and dropping media assets or project files from desktop file managers onto EffectCraft showed a "no" (prohibited) cursor and drops did not function.

This occurs because `eframe 0.36.2` depends on `winit 0.30.13`. In `winit 0.30`, Wayland drag-and-drop was not implemented ([winit#1881](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/issues/1881)). Native Wayland drag-and-drop was added for `winit 0.31` in [winit#4571](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4571) (merged July 2026, tagged in `0.31.0-beta.3`). However, updating to `winit 0.31` directly is blocked by breaking event loop API changes until upstream `eframe` adds support.

On X11 / XWayland, drag-and-drop is fully supported in `winit 0.30`. This pull request adopts the established pattern from `designcraft` and `deckcraft` by Brandon Thomas:
1. Adds `winit = { version = "0.30", default-features = false, features = ["x11"] }` under `cfg(all(unix, not(target_os = "macos")))`.
2. Adds an event loop builder hook before running the native event loop: when an X server is reachable (`DISPLAY` is set) and `EFFECTCRAFT_WAYLAND` is not set, configures `EventLoopBuilderExtX11::with_x11()` to route through XWayland so file drops work out of the box on standard Wayland desktop sessions.
3. Allows users desiring pure native Wayland to opt out and preserve the native Wayland backend by setting `EFFECTCRAFT_WAYLAND=1`.

### Verification
Verified local compilation and dependency resolution with `cargo check -p effectcraft` on Linux (0 errors, 0 warnings).

title: Support continuous numeric scrubbing across monitor edges
author: kikikikier
body:
Numeric scrubbing currently stops at the edge of the monitor. This change wraps the native cursor to the opposite edge and rebases egui's input coordinates so the value continues smoothly, with one Undo step per drag gesture.

The shared hot-number widget and standard numeric editors opt into wrapping. Normal object, keyframe, panel and scrollbar drags keep their existing behavior. The implementation accounts for display scaling and monitor origins, ends on button release or focus loss, and falls back to ordinary dragging when the backend cannot warp the cursor.

Angle scrubbing applies each movement to the full signed angle, so it remains continuous through zero and whole turns while wrapping. Previously, dragging left from zero could produce a negative value and then reset to zero on the next movement because the field reapplied the displayed remainder's sign. Typed degree edits retain their existing behavior.

This is an AI-assisted community contribution, offered for consideration alongside the [standalone patch](https://github.com/kikikikier/effectcraft-infinite-drag). I see these as community additions; whether they belong in the core application is up to the maintainers.

title: Land 49 community PRs, with follow-ups
author: bflatastic
body:
This lands 49 community pull requests. Each one is merged with its author's commits intact, so GitHub marks it merged once this lands. Maintainer follow-ups go on top as separate commits.

Every PR was read line by line for malicious content: network or process calls, path traversal, credential reads, encoded blobs, build scripts, new dependencies, CI and supply-chain changes, `unsafe`, and hidden or bidi Unicode. title: Keep work-area edits inside the composition
author: vbasky
body:
Keep a composition work area inside the composition and at least one frame long.

Setting the start past the current end, or shortening the composition, stored an inverted interval. Trimming that interval then saved a negative duration.

Fixes #538

title: Move separated Position on canvas resize and crop
author: vbasky
body:
Move separated Position when the composition frame is resized or cropped.

Those edits offset the combined Position property, which a separated layer does not render. X and Y Position, including their keys, now move by the same amount.

Fixes #539

title: Move layers when Position is edited with separated dimensions
author: vbasky
body:
Move a layer when Position is edited and its dimensions are separated.

The renderer follows X, Y and Z Position once those channels exist. The Position command was writing only the combined property, so the layer stayed where it was.

Fixes #540

title: Show a layer through its first Intersect or Darken mask
author: vbasky
body:
Show a layer through its first Intersect or Darken mask.

Those modes were combined with an empty coverage, so the first one hid an opaque solid. A later mask still intersects or darkens.

Fixes #527

title: Keep the playhead on the displayed current time
author: vbasky
body:
Keep the playhead on the frame shown in the current-time field.

Timecode and Frames entries were parsed as absolute counts without the composition Start Timecode or Start Numbering Frames At offset, so committing the displayed text jumped to another frame.

Fixes #530

title: Start Linux audio preview without a silence preroll
author: vbasky
body:
Start Linux audio preview after the first mixed samples, on a short device buffer.

Pulse and PipeWire were opening a large default period and playing silence until the feeder caught up, so the picture ran while the sound started late. Once those silent samples drained, the remaining audio stayed in sync with the video. The stream now waits for queued samples and requests about 10 ms of buffering, falling back to the host default if a fixed period is rejected.

Fixes #554

title: fix(script): Property/Layer/Item.selected setters handle false to deselect
author: vbasky

Fixes three related bugs in the scripting model's  property setters:

1. **Property.selected** (Issue #549): Only handled , ignored . Now properly calls  with  to deselect.

2. **Layer.selected** (Issue #548): Used  which flipped state rather than explicitly setting it. Now uses explicit  (select) and  (deselect).

3. **Item.selected** (Issue #548): Missing  case for deselecting project items. Now properly handles both cases.

All 43 script tests pass.

title: Interface: probe Hangul so Korean text isn't drawn as boxes (#599)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #599.

`install_script_fallbacks` probed only kana (`'あ'`) and Han (`'文'`) for CJK. On macOS the kana probe resolves to Hiragino Sans, which has no Hangul, and the Han probe returns the same, already-loaded face, so it is skipped as seen. No face that draws Hangul was ever registered with egui, and Korean layer, file and panel text in the interface showed as boxes. The canvas was not affected, because the text engine has its own per-script fallback.

The fix adds a third CJK probe, `('한', "korean-system")`, after kana and Han in both orders (`[KANA, HAN, HANGUL]`, or `[HAN, KANA, HANGUL]` for the Chinese catalogs). The Japanese and Chinese order and the faces they pick do not change. Where the face already registered for kana or Han covers Hangul (for example Noto Sans CJK on Linux), the probe returns that face and the existing `seen` check skips it, so nothing is registered twice. The function's doc comment now describes the Hangul step.

Test in `crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs`:
- `hangul_gets_a_face_when_one_is_installed`: runs `install_script_fallbacks` for an English interface, then checks that the face the text engine picks for `'한'` (same bytes and same index) is among egui's registered font data. If no installed font covers Hangul, the test prints a note and returns, as the existing CJK test does. On main it fails on a machine whose kana/Han face has no Hangul (macOS with Hiragino Sans, and probably Windows with Yu Gothic or Meiryo).

Not compiled locally (no Rust toolchain here). I rely on this PR's CI checks.

title: Viewer: passive Composition viewers apply the monitor color conversion (#547)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #547.

A passive Composition viewer (View ▸ New Viewer) uploaded the rendered frame as is, while the active viewer runs it through `DisplayColor` (Use Display Color Management, the display profile in Settings ▸ Previews, Simulate Output). With a managed project and a Display P3 monitor profile the two viewers showed different pixels for the same frame, and activating a viewer swapped which one was converted.

- `viewers::set_texture` now applies `DisplayColor::of(&app.session)` to CPU frames before uploading them, the same conversion `draw_frame` applies to the active viewer's RGB view.
- The passive texture is re-uploaded when the conversion's inputs change, not only when the frame key changes. Changing the display profile or the simulation does not advance the project revision, so without this a passive viewer would keep pixels converted for the old display.
- The inputs key that `draw_frame` already built inline is moved into `viewer_tools::display_key`, so the active and passive caches use the same key.

GPU frames (the web viewer) are left as they are: the active viewer converts them through a pixel readback that passive viewers don't have.

Test: `crates/ui-egui/tests/viewer_passive_display.rs`, the issue's repro turned into the restoration check. It opens a second viewer on a Rec. 2020 project with a P3 display profile and checks that both the active and the passive texture hold the converted `[37, 89, 122, 255]`, before and after switching the active viewer. It then switches to sRGB and checks that both hold the raw `[0, 90, 125, 255]`. The P3 passive assertion fails without the fix (the passive viewer shows `[0, 90, 125, 255]`).

title: Locked viewer: re-convert pixels when the display profile or output simulation changes (#546)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #546.

The split locked viewer cached its texture under a key that held only `dc.is_some()` for display colour. Changing Settings ▸ Previews ▸ display profile or View ▸ Simulate Output does not advance the project revision, so the key stayed the same and the pane kept pixels converted for the old display.

`locked_pane` now keys the texture on the conversion's inputs, the same way the main viewer's texture caches do in `viewer_tools.rs`: the display profile, the simulation setting and, for My Custom RGB, the custom profile. Working and output space changes already advance the project revision, so they are covered.

Test: `crates/ui-egui/tests/ui_locked_color.rs`, adapted from the issue's repro. It opens the split locked viewer on a Rec. 2020 output project, captures the texture uploads, and checks the locked pane's centre pixel against a fresh render plus the current `DisplayColor` after switching the display from sRGB to P3 and after turning on the Rec. 709 output simulation. Both checks fail without the fix.

title: Effects: CC Power Pin Unstretch reverses the pin mapping (#534)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #534.

CC Power Pin declared the Unstretch checkbox but never read it, so the forward layer-to-pins mapping always ran.

- `cc_power_pin` (CPU) now reads `unstretch`. When it is on, the mapping runs in reverse: each pixel of the (Expand-grown) layer rectangle samples the source at the matching point of the pinned quad, so the region inside the pins fills the layer. The buffer is not grown in this mode, because the output stays inside the layer rectangle. Perspective blends between the bilinear and the projective quad point, as in the forward path.
- The GPU kernel has no reverse mode. Unstretch is listed in the catalog's `CPU_ONLY_CONTROLS`, like Liquify's View Mesh, so the effect renders on the CPU while the checkbox is on. `power_pin` on the GPU also returns `None` for it, as `liquify` does.

Tests:
- `power_pin_unstretch_expands_pinned_region` uses the issue's 24x16 opaque solid with pins on a centred 12x8 rectangle. Off: 96 opaque pixels (unchanged). On: all 384 pixels are opaque. With the default corners, Unstretch is still the identity. Without the fix, the "on" render equals the "off" one and the test fails.
- `cpu_only_controls_keep_effects_off_the_gpu` now also checks that Power Pin stays on the GPU by default and moves to the CPU when Unstretch is on.

title: CC Simple Wire Removal: Frame Offset takes the strip from the previous or next frame (#533)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #533.

Removal Style "Frame Offset" ran the same code as Displace and never read the Frame Offset slider, so offsets -1 and +1 gave identical output, equal to Displace.

**What changed**

- `crates/effects/src/keying2.rs` (`wire_removal`): for Frame Offset with a non-zero offset, the effect fetches its own layer at `time + offset / fps` through `EffectHost::self_at`, the same way Camera-Shake Deblur (`blur3.rs`) and Rolling Shutter Repair (`distort4.rs`) read neighbouring frames, resamples it onto the current buffer's grid as they do, and fills the wire strip with those pixels. The Slope soft edge still blends into the current frame. Outside the strip nothing changes.
- With no host (direct calls, adjustment layers) or an offset of 0, there is no other frame, so Frame Offset keeps today's Displace result. Displace, Displace Horizontal and Fade do not change.
- GPU (`crates/gpu/src/fx_pixel2.rs`): the `fp2_wire` kernel cannot read other frames, so Frame Offset with a non-zero offset and a host now runs on the CPU (it returns `None`, like Noise Reduction's Temporal Filtering). Without this, the GPU renderer would still show the Displace output.

**Tests**

- New unit test in `keying2.rs`: a fake host that returns a different flat grey for each frame. At frame 5, offset -1 puts frame 4's value in the strip and +1 puts frame 6's value. Pixels outside the strip stay as they are, and Displace output is the same for -1 and +1. Without the fix, the strip gets the current frame's displaced pixels, so the test fails.
- GPU/CPU parity: a new `effect_case` for Frame Offset with offset -2.

title: Rove Across Time keeps roving keys off the neighbouring fixed keys' times (#532)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #532.

`retime_roving` gives each roving key a time proportional to the path length up to it. When the last segment of a run has zero length, the last roving key's fraction is exactly 1.0, so it lands on the end key's time. When the first segment has zero length, the first roving key lands on the start key's time. The project then holds two keys at one time, and a later nudge of all keys merges them (same-time insertion is replacement), so a key and its label disappear.

The fix clamps each retimed key strictly between the previous key and the run's end key, leaving one tick for every roving key still to come. It only acts when the proportional time would collide or go out of order, so runs with non-zero segments keep their existing proportional times. Every caller (`keys.set`, `keys.paste`, the interpolation and key-move commands in `prop.rs`, and the key transforms in `key_transform.rs`) goes through `retime_roving`, so all entry paths are covered.

Test: `roving_keys_never_share_a_time_with_a_fixed_key` runs both cases from the issue (x = `[0, 40, 120, 120]`, zero-length last segment, and the mirrored `[0, 0, 40, 120]`) with Linear spatial keys and checks the four times stay strictly increasing. Without the fix the first case gives `[0, 1, 3, 3]` s and fails. The existing `roving_keys_get_constant_speed_times` test still covers the proportional times for non-zero segments.

title: Convert Expression to Keyframes: sort the keys by layer time on a time-reversed layer (#531)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #531.

`prop.convertExpressionToKeyframes` samples the property at each comp frame from the layer's In point to its Out point and stores each sample at `layer.layer_time(t)`. On a time-reversed layer (negative stretch), ascending comp times map to descending layer times, so the keys were stored in descending time order. Keyframe evaluation assumes the keys are sorted (it clamps to the first stored key), so after conversion the property held one constant value across the whole visible span.

**What changed**

- `crates/engine/src/commands/prop.rs` (`convert_expr_to_keys`): sort the baked keys by time before they replace the property's keys. This is the same `keys.sort_by_key(|k| k.time)` that Motion Sketch and the Puppet recorder use after they sample in comp time. Forward layers already produce ascending keys, so nothing changes for them.

**Tests**

- New test in `tests_timeline.rs`: a Rotation ramp with an expression on a time-reversed solid, converted to keyframes. It checks that the keys are strictly ascending, and that `prop.get` at comp times 0.5, 1 and 2 s returns the same values before and after the conversion. Engine unit tests have no expression host, so the conversion bakes the keyed ramp under the expression. This exercises the same sampling and key ordering as the `time * 10` repro in the issue. Without the fix, the keys are descending and all three samples return the first stored key's value.

title: Fix recording a shortcut: the field no longer types the key too, and Cmd++ parses (#467)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #467.

**Cause.** While the shortcut field records, `shortcut_editor::show` turns the pressed key into text (`Alt+R`) at the top of the frame, but the same frame's key and text events still reach the focused `TextEdit`, which then also types the character. Pressing Alt+R gives `rAlt+R` instead of `Alt+R`.

**Fix.**
- While recording, the editor removes the frame's `Key` and `Text` events after reading them, the same way `menu_keys::strip_keys` keeps a handled key from reaching the rest of the frame.
- `menus::parse_shortcut` now reads the plus key with modifiers (`Cmd++`, `Alt++`). Before, `"Cmd++".split('+')` left an empty key name, so a recorded plus shortcut was saved but never fired. It now splits the same way as its siblings `shortcut_text`, `native_menu` and `engine::shortcuts::normalize`, which already handle the `++` suffix.

**Tests** (`panels::shortcut_editor::tests`):
- `recording_a_shortcut_does_not_also_type_the_key_into_the_field` opens the editor, clicks the shortcut field, sends Alt+R as a key event plus the text `r`, and checks that the field holds `Alt+R`. Without the fix the field holds `rAlt+R`.
- `combo_text_round_trips_through_the_parser` now also checks that `+`, `Cmd++` and `Alt++` parse to `Key::Plus`. Without the fix, `Cmd++` and `Alt++` return `None`.

title: Render queue: unsaved project outputs go to ~/Movies or home, not the working directory (#446)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #446.

**Cause.** `Session::resolve_output` resolves a relative output path against Settings ▸ Export ▸ Default Output Folder, then the saved project's folder, then the process working directory. A macOS app started from the Finder has `/` as its working directory, so an unsaved project with no default output folder rendered to `/`, where the user cannot write, and the render failed.

**Fix.** Before the working directory, an unsaved project's relative outputs now go to `~/Movies` when it exists, else the home folder (`HOME`, or `USERPROFILE` on Windows). This matches FilmCraft's `export_tools::default_export_dir` (saved project's folder, else `~/Movies`, else home). The Default Output Folder setting and the saved-project case work as before. The working directory stays as the last fallback, and the web build still uses its virtual root. All callers (Render Queue panel, Output To dialog, `renderQueue.*` commands, proxies) go through `resolve_output`, so they all get the new default.

**Test.** `tests_m145::unsaved_project_renders_to_movies_or_home_not_the_working_directory` checks the new `render_queue::default_output_base` helper: a home without `Movies` gives the home folder, a home with `Movies` gives `~/Movies`, and no home gives `None`.

title: Let pan and zoom work while 3D Camera Tracker points are shown (#505)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #505.

With a 3D Camera Tracker selected, its point overlay sits on top of the viewer as a full-area `click_and_drag` widget. That blocked the viewer's own navigation in three ways:

- **Wheel zoom:** the overlay took the hover, so the viewer's `resp.hover_pos()` was `None` and the wheel did nothing.
- **Middle-button drag:** the overlay took the drag and started a marquee (the release even selected the points inside it) instead of panning.
- **Spacebar (Hand tool) drag:** same, the overlay took the primary drag, so it drew a marquee instead of panning.

Changes:

- `viewer.rs`: when another widget on top of the viewer takes the hover but the pointer is still over the viewer (`contains_pointer`), the viewer uses the pointer position, so wheel zoom (and the Info panel's pointer readout) keep working. This also covers any other overlay on the viewer.
- `camera_tracker_ui.rs`: while Space is held (`space_hand`, the same check the viewer and timeline use) the overlay only senses hover, so the viewer gets the drag and pans as usual. A middle-button drag that lands on the overlay pans the viewer the same way the viewer's own `Gesture::Pan` does (start pan + `total_drag_delta`), and no longer starts a marquee.

Clicking, Shift-clicking, marquee selection and the right-click menu on the points are unchanged.

Test: `viewer_zooms_and_pans_over_the_track_points` in `crates/ui-egui/tests/ui_camera_tracker.rs` uses the existing synthetic solve and, over a track point, checks that the wheel changes the zoom, that a middle drag pans by the drag distance and selects nothing, and that a Spacebar drag pans and selects nothing. Each of the three checks fails on `main`.

title: Reopen panels from the Window menu when the dock is empty (#529)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #529.

`DockNode::open_near` added the panel next to `near`, then fell back to Effects & Presets and Project. When none of these was docked, it did nothing, so Window > Composition / Timeline / Project left an emptied dock unchanged.

- Empty dock (every panel closed): the panel becomes the whole dock, a single tab group.
- Dock with panels but none of the anchors (for example Minimal with only Timeline closed, then Window > Timeline): the panel is added to the first group, as the doc comment on `open_near` already says ("or into the first group").

Tests: `open_near_in_an_empty_dock_makes_the_panel_the_dock` (Composition, Timeline, Project) and `open_near_without_any_anchor_uses_the_first_group`. Both fail on main.

title: fix(ui): drag all selected Project items into compositions
author: Ni-zav
body:

The same limitation affects drops onto the Composition viewer.

## Root Cause

The drag payload identifies a single Project item, and both drop handlers process only that item, even when it belongs to a larger Project selection.

## Changes

- Resolve Project drags to the full selection when the dragged item is selected.
- Preserve single-item behavior when dragging an unselected item.
- Add all selected items at the Timeline drop location.
- Preserve selection order and insertion position.
- Support multi-item drops onto the Composition viewer.
- Preserve the pointer position for inserted layers.
- Exclude folders and data-only footage from layer insertion.
- Add two headless pointer-drag regression tests.

## Regression Coverage

- `dragging_selected_project_items_adds_every_item_to_the_timeline`
- `dragging_selected_project_items_adds_every_item_to_the_viewer`

title: fix(ui): enable gradient color and opacity stop editing
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Gradient editing controls are displayed but are not interactive.

The Timeline shows "Edit Gradient..." without an associated action, Effect Controls displays a non-interactive gradient strip, and Layer Styles directs users to the Timeline despite the missing editor.

## Root Cause

Gradient values are supported by the underlying project and property systems, but the affected UI controls do not provide an editing interface.

## Changes

### Shared Gradient Editor

Introduce `gradient_editor.rs` with controls for:

- Editing individual color stops.
- Adjusting stop positions.
- Changing color and alpha values.
- Editing opacity stops independently.
- Adding and removing stops.
- Maintaining sorted stop positions.

### Panel Integration

Connect the shared editor to:

- Timeline gradient properties.
- Effect Controls gradient swatches.
- Layer Styles gradient controls.

### Property Integration

- Route modifications through the existing `prop.set` command.
- Preserve the existing gradient value representation.
- Use existing property history and keyframe behavior.
- Keep color and opacity channels independent.
- Limit the interactive stop list to 64 entries per channel.

## Regression Coverage

Added a unit test verifying that reordering gradient stops preserves their associated colors without changing independent opacity stops.

## Validation

- Changes committed and pushed to an isolated fork branch.
- Diff verified against current upstream main.
- Cross-fork comparison confirms one commit ahead with no divergence.
- Regression test added but not executed locally.
- Interactive behavior and CI validation pending.

title: Land community PRs, batch 2, with follow-ups

title: GPU: render precomp layers resident on the GPU (#640)
author: MatejKozlovsky
body:
Fixes #640.

> **Context: the overall series vs this PR.** This is PR 1 of a series that reworks GPU export
> (streaming scheduler, resident effects, GPU-side YUV, auto-tuning). The full series, measured on a
> test PC (Ryzen 7 5800X, RTX 3090 24 GB, Windows 10) with the same 10 s 4K comp: **0.7.0 stock `--gpu` 575.1 s vs patched 33.5 s (~17.2×)**;
> on 0.6.0, **540.5 s CPU vs 31.7 s (17.1×)**. Those numbers are the whole series, **not this PR**.
> This PR covers only nested comps; see below. (Test PC, 0.7.0:
> 0.52 fps → 8.96 fps; GPU util 6% → 92%.)

## Problem

The GPU compositor draws a precomp layer via `Renderer::layer_source`, which renders the nested comp on
the CPU compositor and uploads it every frame, so nested comps run at CPU speed with the GPU idle. Frames
the GPU declines fall back to the CPU without a word in the log.

## Approach (3 commits, one change each)

1. **Render:** `Renderer::precomp_source(ctx, layer)` returns the renderer one level down, the nested comp,
   its time and buffer scale, exactly as `layer_source`'s comp branch would render it, or `None` when that
   branch does more (composition proxy, Essential Properties overrides, frame blending, time-remapped
   content times, recursion, outside the nested comp's span). `run_layer_effects_on` runs a layer's
   effect stack in effect space on any `FxTarget`.
2. **GPU:** `walk::draw_precomp` renders the nested comp with `walk::render` one level down (resident),
   quantises it as `masked_source` would, runs the precomp layer's effects resident (`GpuFx`), and places it
   (`place_src`, `place`'s body without the upload) with track matte / Preserve Transparency / blend mode as
   for any layer. Layers with masks or layer styles, and anything `precomp_source` rejects, keep the
   existing path.
3. **GPU:** `Gpu::comp_frame` logs why it declined a frame (device health, or unsupported content /
   texture limit / allocation) before the caller renders it on the CPU.

title: Lint: clippy's collapsible_match passes on Rust 1.95
author: tylerjenningsw
body:
`cargo +1.95 clippy --workspace --all-targets --release -- -D warnings` (the clippy step of `cargo xtask ci`, on the workspace's minimum Rust) fails on `main` (`1446e27`) with seven `collapsible_match` errors: "this `if` can be collapsed into the outer `match`". This folds each `if` into its match arm as a guard.

| File | Arm |
|---|---|
| `crates/psd/src/lib.rs` | unsupported adjustment keys record `Adjustment::Other` only if none is set yet |
| `crates/text/src/path_text.rs` | `LineTo` skips a point equal to the last one |
| `crates/effects/src/audio_fx.rs` | Backwards swaps channels only when asked |
| `crates/effects/src/generate3.rs` | Venetian-blind mode 0 pairs entering crossings |
| `crates/pdf/src/color.rs` | PostScript calculator `{` within the nesting limit |
| `crates/pdf/src/page.rs` | `h` closes the path only with a current point |
| `crates/render/src/masks.rs` | flattened mask points skip duplicates |

**No behaviour change.** When a guard is false, the value falls through to arms that can't match it (different keys, ids or variants) and then to `_ => {}`, which is what the old `if` without an `else` did. The one place where falling through would differ is `pdf/src/color.rs`: a `{` past the nesting limit would reach `Obj::Op(op) => out.push(PsOp::Op(op))`. That case keeps an explicit no-op arm, so it's still skipped, never pushed as an operator.

## Checks (Windows 10, Rust 1.95, release)
- `cargo fmt --check`: passes.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --release -- -D warnings`: passes (it fails on `main`).
- Tests of the five changed crates (`effectcraft-psd`, `-text`, `-effects`, `-pdf`, `-render`): all pass except `text`'s `variable::tests::style_variations_change_advances_and_outlines`, which **fails identically on `main`**. title: Keyframes: auto-Bezier spatial tangents follow After Effects
author: KattKnight
body:
## What this does

Auto-Bezier motion paths now take After Effects' shape. Before, a Position path with auto-Bezier keys (After Effects' default spatial type) could run up to 28 px away from where AE puts it.

### The rule (G1, measured)

We ran one original script, `examples/ae-spatial-tangents.jsx`, unchanged in both hosts: After Effects 2026 (26.3) via `AfterFX.exe -r` and EffectCraft via `effectcraft-cli script`. It covers three original paths and ten keys, with even and uneven key timing. AE's auto-Bezier tangents follow one rule:

- **Middle key:** out tangent = (next key − previous key) / 6, and the in tangent is its mirror.
- **End keys:** (neighbour − key) / 6, mirrored the same way.
- **Key times play no part.**

That's a Catmull-Rom spline. EffectCraft gave end keys no tangent and scaled middle tangents by the length of each neighbouring segment, so all ten tangents differed.

`auto_spatial` in `crates/keyframe` now uses AE's rule. Everything that reads spatial tangents uses it automatically: evaluation, roving, the motion path overlay and its handles, `keyIn/OutSpatialTangent`, Lottie export and Keyframe Interpolation ▸ Bezier.

### Scores

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Auto-Bezier tangents equal to AE's (to 0.001 px) | 0 of 10 | 10 of 10 |
| Position on an auto-Bezier path with Easy Ease, worst of 61 samples | 25.1 px | 0.03 px |
| Position on a roving path, worst of 61 samples | 27.7 px | 0.05 px |

The rest is sub-pixel path speed from the arc-length table, a separate item. 54 rendered comparison frames are byte-identical before and after.

Per the G1 rules, only the original script and these scores are committed. AE's output stays local. `docs/fidelity/README.md` has the method and scores, and the acceptance table's Animation row is updated.

### Three tests changed on purpose

All three relied on auto-Bezier end keys having no tangent:

- `tests_timeline::spatial_bezier_gives_a_straight_path_handles`: Spatial ▸ Bezier keeps a key's current ha…

title: Fix Rust 1.99 clippy lint and two Windows-only MCP auto-save tests
author: didpublishing
body:
## What

Two small commits that get `cargo xtask ci` past its first failures on current stable Rust, on Windows:

1. **Clippy: use `as_chunks` for the constant chunk size in `parse_spimtx`.** Rust 1.99's `clippy::chunks_exact_to_as_chunks` failed `cargo clippy -D warnings` on `main` (`crates/effects/src/ocio.rs`). Behaviour is unchanged; the length is checked to be 12 just above.
2. **Tests: the MCP auto-save recovery text holds a JSON-escaped path.** The `initialize` `instructions` embed the auto-save info as JSON, so a Windows path appears with doubled backslashes. Two tests searched for the raw path and failed on Windows (automation `autosave_is_durable_before_reply_and_queries_do_not_rotate`, cli `mcp_autosave_survives_kill_and_restart_without_touching_desktop_settings`). The server output is correct; the tests now look for the escaped form.

## Checked

- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --release -- -D warnings` pass.
- Both fixed tests pass.

## Not covered

A full `cargo test --workspace` on this Windows machine (RTX 3060, ffmpeg "essentials" build) still shows failures unrelated to this PR, so I did not get a green `cargo xtask ci`:

- `av1_mp4_roundtrip`, `av1_webm_with_opus`: the local ffmpeg has no `libdav1d` decoder.
- `viewer_draws_gpu_frames_that_match_the_cpu` (`ui_gpu`): the GPU compositor doesn't attach to egui's device on Vulkan here.
- `style_variations_change_advances_and_outlines`: depends on which variable font is installed; `wght` doesn't change advances for the one found here.
- `resampled_audio_read_in_frame_pieces_matches_ffmpeg` and `auto_backend_keeps_fast_accelerators`: flaky under load, both pass alone.

Worth a maintainer run of the full gate on a known-good machine.

title: #590: scripts can't enable file and network access for themselves
author: didpublishing
body:
Fixes #590.

> Stacked on #653: this branch contains its two commits (the Rust 1.99 clippy fix and the Windows test fix). Review only the last commit, `#590: scripts can't enable file and network access for themselves`; the rest disappears from the diff once #653 merges.

## Problem

A running script could call `prefs.set` (through `app.run`, `__exec` or `engine.batch`), turn on `scripting.allowScriptsWriteFiles` and persist it, which lifts the file and network restrictions it runs under.

## Fix

- `crates/engine/src/prefs.rs`: a thread-local script-origin scope, `with_script_origin()`, restored on return, error and unwind.
- `crates/script/src/runtime.rs`: the one place scripts dispatch engine commands (`exec`) runs them inside that scope. Nested commands such as `engine.batch`, ScriptUI handlers and scheduled tasks all go through it.
- `crates/engine/src/commands/settings.rs`: `prefs.set` refuses an off-to-on change of the permission while the scope is active. It checks the final candidate preferences before anything is assigned or saved, so single keys, whole-page values, `values` maps, coercions and batches are all covered.
- The host (Settings, control channel, MCP) is unaffected and can still grant the permission.

This is based on the candidate patch in #590, re-implemented after reviewing every script-to-engine path, with a smaller test.

## Test

`scripts_cannot_enable_file_and_network_access` (crates/script) tries four routes, checks that the host can still grant the permission and that scripts can still change other preferences. It fails with the check disabled and passes with it.

- `effectcraft-engine`: 445 passed (2 ignored). `effectcraft-script`: 44 passed.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --release -- -D warnings` pass.

## Scope

JavaScript self-grant only, not a complete sandbox. Host-launched legacy JSON/JSONL command scripts remain a trusted entry point. A full `cargo xtask ci` was not green on my Windows machine…

title: Light theme: effect headers, timeline wells and bars, and the expression editor use theme colours (#644)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #644.

In the Light theme, Effect Controls and the Timeline still painted some surfaces with fixed dark colours. All the surfaces the issue names now come from theme tokens (`theme.rs`). Dark and Darker keep their current values exactly, so only Light looks different.

How each point of the issue is handled:

The same expression orange is also used for the name of a property that has an expression and for the one-line hint of a closed expression. title: Theme: Sync with System keeps egui on its System preference so macOS keeps reporting OS appearance changes (#642)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #642.

With Appearance Mode set to Sync with System, `apply_visuals` always called `ctx.set_theme(Light | Dark)`. egui then sends `ViewportCommand::SetTheme(Light/Dark)`, which pins the native window appearance; on macOS winit stops emitting `ThemeChanged` once the window has an appearance override, so the app never saw the next OS switch.

Changes:
- `theme::apply_visuals` takes a `follow_system` flag. When it is set, egui gets `ThemePreference::System` (which maps to `SetTheme(SystemDefault)`, i.e. no override). Otherwise it pins Light or Dark as before. Our tokens are still resolved from the same OS report, and `set_visuals` styles the theme egui shows.
- `EffectcraftApp::follows_system` is true only for Sync with System when egui's own report is the source (the Linux portal hook keeps the pinned path, since it gets changes from the portal and not from the window), and only when egui has a report (with no report the documented dark fallback stays pinned).
- Both places that set egui's theme preference are covered: `apply_prefs` (startup, Settings, the Tools bar appearance button, `view.theme.*`) and the first-frame/language-change `theme::install` in `logic`, which resets the preference to System afterwards. Nothing else in the app sets egui's theme (the other `theme::install` calls are in test modules).
- Fixed Light and Dark modes still pin, as before.
- `docs/preferences.md` (`appearance.appearanceMode`) notes that Sync with System leaves egui on its System preference.

Test: `sync_with_system_keeps_egui_on_the_system_preference` runs real egui passes with a Light system report and checks `theme_preference`: System for `auto`, Dark/Light for the fixed modes, then System again after you switch back to `auto`. Without the fix the first assertion fails (`Light` instead of `System`).

Not verified on a real macOS appearance switch (no Mac here). The test checks the preference that egui turns into `SetTheme(SystemDefault)`.

title: fix(timeline): create first composition from a footage drop
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Fixes #649.

Dragging footage from the Project panel into the Timeline
does nothing when the project has no active composition.

The Timeline currently displays "(no composition)" and
returns before handling Project item drops.

Users must manually create a composition or use the
Project panel's New Composition button.

## Root Cause

The Timeline's early-return path for projects without an
active composition does not provide a drag-and-drop target.

The application already supports creating compositions
from Project items through file.newCompFromSelection, but
the empty Timeline does not invoke that workflow.

## Changes

- Accept Project footage and solid items dropped onto an
  empty Timeline.
- Display a visual drop-target outline.
- Reuse file.newCompFromSelection to create the composition.
- Preserve the source item's dimensions, frame rate, and
  duration through the existing creation workflow.
- Support multiple selected footage items through the
  existing New Composition from Selection dialog.
- Ignore unsupported Project items, including folders and
  non-media data files.
- Preserve the existing Timeline behavior when a
  composition is already active.

## Regression Tests

Added two UI drag-and-drop tests:

1. Dropping one footage item onto an empty Timeline creates
   the first composition with the source dimensions, frame
   rate, duration, and layer.

2. Dropping multiple selected footage items opens the
   existing composition-creation dialog rather than
   silently creating an unintended composition.

## Validation

Reviewed the implementation against the existing Project
panel composition-creation workflow.

Reviewed the pushed changes and their affected files.

The two regression tests have been added but not executed.
Rust formatting, integration tests, interactive UI verification,
and CI remain unchecked.

## Issue

Fixes #649

title: fonts: extra font folders from EFFECTCRAFT_FONT_DIRS
author: johnstockertutorial-afk
body:
## What

`DirectorySource::system()` also scans the folders listed in `EFFECTCRAFT_FONT_DIRS`: a path list, `:`-separated (`;` on Windows), split with `std::env::split_paths`, with empty entries ignored. These folders are walked exactly like the system font folders. The variable is documented next to `text.fonts` in `docs/agents.md`.

## Why

A tool that drives EffectCraft by script can bring its own font library and hand it to EffectCraft without installing the fonts system-wide. We use this from a video tool (AutoCut) that builds EffectCraft comps from about 200 bundled Thai, Lao and Latin fonts. Before this change those comps rendered with fallback faces unless every font was installed on the machine.

title: #591: failed GPU allocations fall back to the CPU; a lost graphics device saves and exits
author: didpublishing
body:
Fixes the two crashes in #591 (the memory growth in the same issue is not addressed here, see "Not in this PR").

> Stacked on #653: this branch contains its two commits (the Rust 1.99 clippy fix and the Windows test fix) so clippy can run. Review only the last two commits; the rest disappears from the diff once #653 merges.

## Problem

On an integrated GPU (Adreno X1-85, shared memory) a failed `vkAllocateMemory` surfaced as `ERROR_INITIALIZATION_FAILED`, not out-of-memory. Two panics followed:

1. On a frame thread, wgpu's `create_buffer_init` panicked (`util/device.rs:72`, "Failed to get mapped range ... Buffer with '' label is invalid"). The failure never reached the out-of-memory guard, so the CPU fallback of #106 / #129 was not what handled it, and the device was lost.
2. On the main thread, egui-wgpu panicked painting on the lost device (`renderer.rs:984`, "Failed to create staging buffer for index data"), which ended the app and lost the open project. egui-wgpu has no device-loss handling and eframe can't swap its device.

## Fix

**`#591: a failed GPU buffer allocation falls back to the CPU instead of panicking`**
- `crates/gpu/src/buffers.rs`: `init` has the same result as `create_buffer_init` on success; on failure it logs and returns the invalid buffer, leaving wgpu's own error for the error scope. All 11 call sites use it.
- `Gpu::within_memory` now scopes validation and internal errors as well as out-of-memory, so the existing frame-thread fallback covers a failure reported as one of those.
- Test `a_failed_buffer_creation_is_reported_not_a_panic`: reproduces the exact panic from the issue when the helper is swapped back to wgpu's `create_buffer_init`, and passes with it.

**`#591: save a recovery copy and exit when the graphics device is lost`**
- When the presentation device is reported lost, the start of the frame writes an auto-save (which also refreshes the crash-recovery sentinel) and calls a new `Hooks::presentation_lost`, once, before anything…

title: Effects: text and shape layers run their stack over the whole layer region (#659, #658)
author: vbasky
body:
Effects applied to a text (or shape) layer were clipped at the content's own bounding box: CC Tiler tiled only inside the glyph rectangle and CC Smear lost its trail at the text edge (#659, #658).

The stack already measures from the comp-sized `effect_bounds` rectangle (the #227 convention, covered by `edge_pinning_displaces_all_of_a_centred_shape_layer` and friends), but the buffer handed to it spanned only the painted pixels — sized sources get this for free, authored ones did not. Effects computed the right answer outside that rectangle and then wrote into a too-small image, dropping it.

`Buf::cover` grows the effect input to the whole layer rectangle (transparent margins, content untouched, 16384 side cap, no-ops when the buffer already covers the region), applied by `run_effect_stack` when an enabled video effect will run; the GPU target reallocates and copies the texture natively instead of round-tripping.

Tests: `effects_on_text_reach_past_the_text_bounds` (CC Tiler's painted x-span must leave the text box) and `cc_smear_trails_text_past_its_bounds` (the smear's right edge must move past it) — both verified to fail without the growth and pass with it. Render, effects, gpu, engine, host and ui-egui suites (1871 tests) pass on current main; fmt, clippy and `cargo xtask layers` are clean.

title: GPU: resident effect stacks, in-frame texture reuse, upload-cache budget, stable footprint keys (#687)
author: MatejKozlovsky
body:
Fixes #687.

> **The overall series vs this PR.** This is PR 2 of a series that reworks GPU export. The full series,
> measured on a test PC (Ryzen 7 5800X, RTX 3090 24 GB, Windows 10) with the same 10 s 4K comp: 0.7.0
> stock `--gpu` 575.1 s vs the full series 33.5 s (~17.2×). **This PR alone delivers much less;** its
> numbers are below. The batch-parallel export that keeps frames off the GPU on main is addressed by a
> later PR (the scheduler); here exports are measured with `RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1` so frames stay on the GPU.

## Changes (4 commits, one change each)

1. **Render:** an adjustment layer's footprint key ignores its effects (the footprint is the source
   through the masks), so a time-dependent effect such as Noise no longer re-keys it every frame.
2. **GPU:** an `Enc` reuses the working textures it released at once. Its later commands run after
   everything it recorded before (one queue, recording order), so it may overwrite them; other encoders
   only get them after the `Enc` is gone, through the existing pool.
3. **GPU:** `GpuContext::set_upload_budget` / `upload_budget` (default unchanged, 1536 MB), and one
   warning when the upload cache is full and starts evicting layer textures.
4. **GPU:** `walk::draw_resident_fx`: a plain layer's effect stack runs resident on the GPU (`GpuFx`, in
   effect space, as 0.7.0 defines it, then rebased to layer space) and is placed directly; CPU-only effects
   in the stack read back, run and upload as before. A layer whose processed buffer is cached and unchanged
   since the last frame (`Renderer::layer_is_static`) keeps the usual path, so it uploads once instead of

title: Share docking transactions and preserve viewer lifecycle
author: skylartaylor
body:
Panel moves, tab ordering, edge splits and floating geometry use atomic shared docking transactions while retaining EffectCraft’s grouped accordion frames, active tabs, open state, heights and viewer/ScriptUI lifecycle. Keyboard focus reaches dock tabs, toolbar controls and resize handles; compact viewers scroll controls into view. Generic transactions reject invalid geometry and selection without mutation, while legacy close helpers retain selection repair.

Current and named workspaces use one guarded persistence writer. Actual-app restart and explicit-shape legacy migration tests preserve named workspaces. Unsupported future snapshots remain untouched, including when a named-workspace command tries to save.

Audio Spectrum’s 18 stale golden hashes match the existing linear frequency/amplitude renderer; a synthetic-tone regression checks placement, silence and proportional amplitude. Production rendering is unchanged.

title: Shapes: edit gradient color and opacity stops (#612)
author: tylerjenningsw
body:
Fixes the nonfunctional Timeline “Edit Gradient…” control (#612). Direct gradient manipulation in the Composition viewer remains a follow-up, so this doesn't close the issue.

The Timeline's **Edit Gradient…** on a gradient property (Gradient Fill / Gradient Stroke ▸ Colors, Gradient Overlay) only painted its label. It now opens a **Gradient Editor**.

## What it does
- **Stops:** opacity stops sit above a preview bar (with a checkerboard under it, so opacity shows) and colour stops below. Click above or below the bar to add a stop. A new stop takes its own track's value there: a colour stop the colour track's RGBA, an opacity stop the opacity track's alpha. A stop can be dragged, or moved by typing its **Location**.
- **Editing a stop:** set its **Opacity**, or its **Color** with the shared colour picker every colour input uses (#638: hex field, HSB/RGB, OK and Cancel; the stop keeps its alpha). **Delete** removes it, but never the last stop of a track, and never while typing in a field.
- **Order and selection:** the tracks stay in order while editing, so the preview and newly sampled stops are always right. The selection follows its stop when it moves past another.
- **One undo step:** the editor works on a draft. **OK** sets the property once with `prop.set` at the composition time it opened, snapped to the nearest frame, with `timeBase: "comp"`. Offset and stretched layers therefore get the keyframe where it was opened. **OK with no change does nothing**, so it never adds a keyframe.
- **Cancel / Escape** change nothing. Escape with the picker open closes only the picker and restores the colour it opened with.
- **Animated gradients:** only the keyframe at that time changes, or one is added there. When the draft's stop counts no longer match a neighbouring keyframe's, the editor shows "These adjacent keyframes cannot interpolate because their stop counts differ." (Gradient keyframes only blend with equal counts.) The edit is still allowed, and the neighbours ar…

title: Pixel Motion Blur: synthesize from motion vectors, honour Vector Detail (#535)
author: vbasky
body:
Closes #535.

`Time > Pixel Motion Blur` fetched the layer at its shutter times and averaged the decoded frames as they were, so motion rendered as doubled copies and the accepted Vector Detail parameter changed nothing.

Now PMB builds a `TimewarpPlan`: each shutter instant is decoded between the two source frames it falls between along a measured motion field — the same block-matching and in-between synthesis Time > Timewarp already uses — and the instants average into the blur. Vector Detail drives the vector grid (0 → one vector per 32 px, 100 → one per 2 px). The motion measurement gets a search radius sized to the buffer (up to a quarter-frame displacement per step) rather than Timewarp's ±4, which a full-frame move like the reported one simply exceeded.

CPU and GPU share the plan: `crates/gpu/src/fx_time.rs` now renders it with the same step loop as Timewarp (the plan renderer was factored out), so the existing `tests_fx_time` CPU/GPU parity cases for the effect compare the new path (they skip without an adapter locally and run on the GPU CI). Without a time host the old average path remains.

The `crates/render/tests/motion_blur_probe.rs` test follows the issue's repro structure but uses a textured moving block, since a flat bar in a featureless field is the aperture problem, not something any synthesizer can fill. It asserts the output is neither the still nor the plain overlay, lays trail coverage along the path, and that the two Vector Detail extremes produce measurably different frames; verified to fail on the old averaging code.

`cargo test -p effectcraft-render -p effectcraft-effects -p effectcraft-gpu -p effectcraft-engine -p effectcraft-host` (1405), `cargo fmt --all --check`, clippy and `cargo xtask layers` are clean.

title: Web: opt-in embedding bridge for host pages (?host=parent)
author: CyberFox-81
body:
A page that frames EffectCraft on the same origin can now open footage and projects in it and store what it saves and renders, through postMessage, instead of saved projects and Render Queue outputs becoming browser downloads. Built for a Nextcloud integration, but nothing in it is host-specific.

Only the web shell changes (src/host.rs):
- effectcraft:open { name, path, blob } from the parent: the file is put in the file table under /host plus the parent's path (unpersisted) and opened or imported as a picked file is
- before a project opens, footage it refers to under /host that isn't here yet is asked of the parent (effectcraft:need { paths }) and arrives as effectcraft:file { path, blob }
- files::deliver sends what would be downloaded (saved projects, renders) to the parent (effectcraft:save): a file under /host by the parent's path, anything else by its file name
- effectcraft:dirty reports unsaved changes; effectcraft:ready and effectcraft:failed report start-up. In host mode the last session, the demo and the recovery offer don't open, and the session isn't kept in browser storage.

Enabled only by ?host=parent inside a frame; only the parent window on the page's own origin is heard or answered. Without it nothing changes.

title: #596: GPU Information names the adapter, or why the GPU compositor is off
author: didpublishing
body:
Part of #596. This makes the GPU Information dialog tell the truth; it does not explain why the reporter's RTX 4070 isn't used for compositing, which needs the System Report requested on the issue.

## Problem

Settings ▸ Previews ▸ **GPU Information…** showed fixed text: "Compositing: CPU, N threads (pure Rust, rayon). Display: egui on wgpu." It never named a GPU, even while the GPU compositor was running, so a card looked undetected ("it doesn't appear … neither on the settings"). The System Report already says why there is no GPU and names the window's adapter (a220b63, #645), but the dialog did not use any of it.

## Change

- `sysinfo::gpu_summary(&Session)` builds the graphics lines: the compositor's adapter, or why compositing is on the CPU, plus the adapter the window itself got.
- The GPU Information dialog uses it, followed by the existing cache lines.

Example when the compositor declined the card:

```
Compositing: CPU, 16 threads (pure Rust, rayon).
GPU compositing is off: GPU compositor unavailable: <reason>
Window graphics: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 (Dx12, DiscreteGpu)
Layer cache: … MB  •  Preview cache: … MB.
```

## Tests

- `gpu_summary_names_the_adapter_or_says_why_there_is_none` (engine): compositor off with no reason, off with a reason and the window's adapter, and on.
- `gpu_information_names_the_adapter_and_why_the_gpu_is_off` (UI): the dialog shows the window's adapter and the reason; it fails against the old text.

title: Cache/GPU: adjustment footprint ignores the effect stack; upload starvation is reported (#687)
author: vbasky
body:
Two of the four things #687 lists, the two that are pure logic and verifiable headless. The GPU-residency and fresh-intermediate-allocation parts need a DX12/Vulkan/Metal device to measure, so they are left for that.

**1. Adjustment-layer footprint re-keyed every frame (#687.3)**
The footprint (the adjustment layer's source through its masks — where its effects show) is cached so the GPU uploads it once, but its key came from the same `key_any` as a processed layer, so the whole effects group, paint spans, the comp-camera read and the time-fold any time-dependent effect forces all entered it. Noise or Grain on a finishing adjustment changed that key every frame: the footprint re-rendered and a full-frame RGBA-f32 buffer (127 MB at 4K) re-uploaded each frame, even though the footprint's pixels never move.

`key_any` now takes an explicit `EffectScope` — `All` (processed layer), `First(n)` (a layer's input, unchanged) and a new `Footprint` that hashes none of the stack. Masks still re-key (their structure and evaluated values stay in, shutter stays keyed while masks exist); shape/text wiggle time, the effect-dependency walk and the comp-scene read behave exactly as before for the existing scopes. `All` and `First(n)` are byte-for-byte today's keys, so the existing hit/miss suites pass unchanged.

A render test drives a mask path across its keyframes with Noise enabled and asserts: identical keys at frames 1.5 and 3.5 (well past the animation), a different key where the mask actually moved, an effect-parameter edit that does not re-key, and that the cached buffer still equals the mask it should show. It fails on the old single-scope code.

**2. Silent upload-cache eviction (#687.4)**
Static layers over the fixed 1536 MB upload budget evicted live textures with no log line and every later frame paid a re-upload. Evictions of still-held buffers are now counted and the first is reported (`gpu <name>: the <N> MB upload budget cannot hold this project's layers…`), and `Gpu…

title: Match After Effects non-legacy Brightness & Contrast
author: vbasky
body:
Fixes #681.

Non-legacy Brightness & Contrast used `g = 2^(2c)`, which is much steeper than After Effects (Contrast 100 at v=0.25 was ~8/255 vs AE ~40/255).

Using kasper9n's AE ramp PNGs, Clef (Jev) chose a closed-form **brightness-first mild S-curve** over keeping the old exponent-4 curve or a discrete 2D LUT. Brightness is a power that pins 0 and 1; contrast uses `g = 1 + 0.53 c`. CPU and GPU match. B0 C-100.png was treated as a duplicate of C-50 and is not a golden.

Legacy (Use Legacy) is unchanged.

Remaining: strong negative brightness (B-100 / B-150) still has a larger 8-bit error than contrast; that was accepted to ship the screenshot mismatch.

title: Tests: six engine tests no longer assume the working directory's drive on Windows
author: didpublishing
body:
## What

Six `effectcraft-engine` tests fail on a Windows machine whose working directory and home folder are on different drives (here: repo on `D:`, home on `C:`). Test-only change: they now pass there, and nothing changes on Unix.

## Why they failed

**Five render-queue tests** used `/tmp/...` output paths:

- `rq_tests::add_configure_render`
- `tests_stubs::add_output_module_encodes_twice`
- `tests_stubs::pre_render_imports_and_replaces`
- `tests_stubs::post_render_actions_import_and_set_proxy`
- `tests_stubs::log_notify_and_overflow_settings`

On Windows `/tmp/rq/out.mov` has no drive letter, so `Path::is_absolute()` is false and `Session::resolve_output` joins it onto the home folder's base, which keeps that drive (`C:/tmp/rq/out.mov`). The tests compared with `std::path::absolute("/tmp/rq/out.mov")`, which uses the working directory's drive (`D:\tmp\rq\out.mov`). They only passed where both are on the same drive, as on CI runners. The product is consistent (it stores the path it writes to), so this is the tests' assumption, not a render-queue bug.

**One footage test** compared strings: `footage_check::tests::relative_footage_is_found_next_to_the_project`. Windows joins the stored `media/ec-relative-clip.png` onto the project's folder and leaves a path with mixed separators (`...\media/ec-relative-clip.png`) where the test expected `...\media\...`. It now compares each path by components, which treat `/` and `\` as the same.

title: fix(viewer): create a composition when dropping footage onto an empty viewer
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Dragging an imported Project item onto an empty Composition viewer does not create a composition.

Users must instead create a composition manually or drop the footage onto the empty Timeline.

## Root Cause

The Composition viewer exits through its empty-state rendering path before the normal drag-and-drop handler can process Project items.

Unlike the empty Timeline, the empty viewer has no handler for creating a composition from dropped footage.

## Changes

- Add Project item drag-and-drop support to the empty Composition viewer.

- Exclude folders and unsupported data items from composition creation.
- Display drop-target feedback and propagate command errors.

## Regression Tests

Added two UI tests:

1. Dropping a single footage item creates a composition with matching properties and the footage as its first layer.
2. Dropping multiple selected footage items opens the existing composition-creation dialog instead of silently discarding items.

## Validation

- Source changes committed and pushed.
- Verified the remote branch and its two-file diff against upstream main.
- UI regression tests added but not executed locally because the Rust toolchain was unavailable.
- CI and manual UI verification remain pending.

Fixes #684

title: fix(effects): add XYZ rotation to CC Cylinder on CPU and GPU
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

CC Cylinder exposes only a single Rotation parameter.

Users cannot independently rotate the cylinder around its X, Y, and Z axes, limiting its usefulness for perspective effects and animated compositions.

## Root Cause

The existing CPU and GPU implementations assume a cylinder aligned with the vertical axis.

Rotation affects the cylindrical texture mapping but does not provide a general three-axis transformation.

## Changes

### Rotation Controls

Add three animatable effect parameters:

- Rotation X
- Rotation Y
- Rotation Z

Preserve the existing Rotation parameter for compatibility with existing projects.

### CPU Rendering

- Apply a three-dimensional rotation matrix to the cylinder.
- Use ray-cylinder intersections to determine the visible cylindrical surface.
- Transform intersection points into cylinder-local coordinates for texture sampling.
- Transform surface normals for lighting.
- Preserve the original rendering path when the new rotation parameters are zero.

### GPU Rendering

- Pass the rotation matrix to the WGSL shader.
- Implement corresponding ray-cylinder intersection and texture-mapping calculations.
- Support independent and combined X/Y/Z rotations.
- Preserve the original GPU rendering path for existing projects.

### Tests and Documentation

- Add a CPU regression test covering cylinder tilt, rotation, and texture changes.
- Add four GPU-versus-CPU reference cases covering individual axes and combined rotations.
- Update the CC Cylinder parameter count in the effects documentation.

## Compatibility

The new parameters default to zero.

Existing projects retain their previous rotation behavior unless the new controls are changed.

## Validation

- Changes committed and pushed.
- Verified the remote branch and its five-file diff against upstream main.
- Added CPU and GPU regression coverage, but tests were not executed locally because the Rust/GPU toolchain was unavailable.
- Shader compilation, GPU parity tests, and CI remai…

title: fix(gpu): cap GPU readback staging buffers to prevent memory exhaustion
author: mjohnson7cd
body:
## Summary

Fixes storytold/artcraft#2081 - Rendering stops at frame 970/1570, PC lags until app closed on high-end system (i7-12700KF, RTX 3090, 32GB RAM).

## Problem

GPU readback staging buffers accumulated unbounded when layer bounds changed every frame (animated scale, blur radius, growing shapes). Each 1080p RGBA f32 buffer ≈ 33 MB in system RAM. At 970 frames × 33 MB ≈ 32 GB, the system exhausted available memory.

The buffers are kept for reuse (up to 2 per size), but there was no limit on total memory across all sizes.

## Solution

**Capped GPU readback staging buffers to 256 MB total.** When adding a new buffer would exceed the cap, drop buffers of other sizes while keeping the current size for reuse. Renders with consistent frame sizes still benefit from buffer reuse.

## Implementation

**Changed:** `crates/gpu/src/context.rs`, `crates/gpu/tests.rs` (+34/-1)
- Added 256 MB budget for readback staging buffers
- Eviction policy: drop other sizes when budget exceeded, keep current size
- New test: `readback_staging_stays_bounded_across_sizes`

## Test Results

**Without fix:** Test reads 120 different sizes (~480 MB), holds 620 MB, takes 28.5s (Apple M4/Metal)  
**With fix:** Same test passes in 0.54s, stays within 256 MB budget

✓ `cargo fmt`  
✓ `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`  
✓ `cargo test -p effectcraft-gpu` (204 tests passed)

## Notes

- Verified on Metal backend; not tested on Windows/DX12/Vulkan with RTX 3090
- Would benefit from reporter's project file to confirm exact reproduction
- Small rebase conflict possible with open PRs #688, #701 (also touch GPU cache code)

---
