title: perf(encoders): AV1, VP9 and HEVC encoders use every core (bit-identical output)
author: eliasx45
body:
## What
The AV1, VP9 and HEVC encoders now use every core, and their output is unchanged.

- **av1enc:** superblock rows are decided in parallel as a wavefront, in the same order as serial coding, so the bitstream is bit-identical. Uniform tiles are written in parallel and the loop filter runs in parallel. Transform trials, block decisions and snapshots reuse scratch buffers. A hash test pins the bitstream.
- **vp9enc:** tile columns (up to 4, depending on frame size) are coded in parallel. Colour conversion, phase planes and loop-filter trials also run in parallel. New `tests/tiles.rs`.
- **hevcenc:** CTU rows are coded as parallel wavefronts (WPP substreams with entry points). The stream is the same for any thread count. The half-sample planes used by motion search are built row by row in parallel and are bit-identical. Mode-decision snapshots are reused.

## Why
Exports were bound to one core during encoding. Now they scale with the machine.

## How tested
On a branch from `main`:
- `cargo test --release` for `effectcraft-av1enc`, `-vp9enc` and `-hevcenc`: roundtrip tests, bitstream hash pins, the new tile tests, and the ffmpeg oracle where it is available.
- clippy `-D warnings`, rustfmt and the wasm32 check.

title: perf(raster): faster transfer curves, blurs and blend rows (pixel-identical)
author: eliasx45
body:
## What
Faster raster and colour paths. The rendered pixels are identical: the golden hashes are unchanged.

- **Transfer curves** (sRGB, gamma 2.4, PQ, HLG) come from 4096-entry lookup tables. Colour conversions now match the transfer curve once per pixel instead of once per channel.
- **Directional Blur:**
  - an axis-aligned running-sum fast path;
  - for any other angle, the tap footprint is computed once per call, with a fast path for interior pixels.
- **Radial Blur** computes the spin angle of each sample once, outside the pixel loop.
- **Blurs** process one plane at a time when only one channel changes.
- **Layer blending and warps** pick the row function for each blend mode once, instead of matching the mode on every pixel.
- **New raster helpers:**
  - a bounded pool for canvas-sized temporaries (`raster::pool`);
  - sparse coverage planes (`raster::sparse`);
  - image comparison metrics (`raster::compare`).

`directional_blur` gains an `adjustment` argument, and its one caller in `effects/src/misc.rs` is updated.

## Why
Blurs, colour conversion and blending are among the hottest paths in a frame. These changes reduce the work done per pixel without changing any result.

## How tested
On a branch from `main`:
- `cargo test --release` for `effectcraft-raster`, `-color` and `-effects`, including the effect golden hashes, and for render;
- clippy `-D warnings`;
- rustfmt;
- the wasm32 check.

title: #473: Cryptomatte Selection keeps quoted names with commas whole
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #473 (the quoted-names point; viewer picking, the Layer popup from metadata and the CPU rank loop stay open).

## Problem
`selection_hashes` split the Cryptomatte **Selection** on every comma before stripping quotes. A name with a comma in it (Blender allows a material called `Green, Glossy`) was cut into `Green` and `Glossy`, quoted or not, so it gave an empty matte. Only its `<hex>` hash selected it.

## Fix
A small tokenizer (`selection_names`) splits at commas outside quotes:
- a name in double or single quotes stays whole, commas included: `"Green, Glossy", ring`
- a backslash takes the next character literally: `Green\, Glossy`, `\"`
- unquoted lists, apostrophes inside names (`Bob's mat`), wildcards and `<hex>` hashes parse as before; an unclosed quote runs to the end.

The CPU effect and the GPU path (`fx_depth.rs`) share the function, so both are fixed.

## Tests
- `channel3d::tests::cryptomatte_selection_keeps_quoted_names_with_commas_whole`: quoted (both quote kinds), escaped and mixed selections against a manifest, plus hashing without a manifest. It fails on main (`[1, 2]` instead of `[7]`).

## Gates
`cargo fmt --check`, `clippy -p effectcraft-effects --all-targets -D warnings`, full `effectcraft-effects` tests, `effectcraft-gpu` `ids_and_cryptomatte`, `cargo xtask layers`, wasm32 check of `effectcraft-effects`. I didn't run the full `cargo xtask ci` (shared machine).

title: #729: import STL 3D models (binary and ASCII)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #729.
Part of ranked gap #13 "3D model formats and materials" (docs/gaps.md).

## Problem
After Effects 26 imports STL models (`usdStl`) besides glTF and OBJ. We refused `.stl` files, and neither the Media Browser nor the import dialog listed them as models.

## Fix
- New `crates/model/src/stl.rs`, a pure-Rust reader written from the public format description, with no new dependencies:
  - **Binary:** 80-byte header, `u32` facet count, 50-byte facets. Bytes after the last facet are ignored.
  - **ASCII:** handles several `solid` blocks in one file and fan-triangulates loops with more than three vertices.
  - **Format detection:** an exact binary size wins over the `solid` keyword, because many binary headers also start with `solid`.
  - **Colours:** binary per-facet colours in both documented conventions (VisCAM/SolidView with bit 15 set; Materialise Magics `COLOR=` header with a part colour). Each colour becomes a plain dielectric material. Files without colour get no materials, so the renderer's default material applies, the same as OBJ without an MTL file.
  - **Geometry:** facets are flat-shaded, with the normal taken from the winding; the stored normal is used only when a facet is degenerate. Z-up (CAD/3D printing) is turned to the model's +Y-up with a proper rotation, so winding is kept.
  - **Hostile input:** truncated counts, empty files, files with no facets, non-finite coordinates and malformed ASCII vertices all return an error, never a panic. Allocation is bounded by the file size, and colour grouping uses a hash map, not a linear search.
- `.stl` is wired in everywhere models are recognised: `effectcraft_model::format_of`/`load`, `MODEL_EXTENSIONS` (import and probe, codec `STL (…)`), the Media Browser model kind, the File ▸ Import dialog filter, the system report import list and the `layer.newModel` help.

title: #738: Edit ▸ Paste pastes SVG markup as a shape layer
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #738.

Part of ranked gap #21 "Small 26.x features" (docs/gaps.md).

## Problem
After Effects 26.3 pastes copied vector artwork as editable shape layers. In EffectCraft, Edit ▸ Paste only knew the app's own clipboard, so SVG markup on the system clipboard (from "Copy SVG" in a browser, a design tool, or Illustrator with SVG code on the clipboard) was ignored. The only way to turn SVG into shapes was to import it as footage first and then run Layer ▸ Create ▸ Create Shapes from Vector Layer.

## Fix
- **Engine:** a new `edit.pasteSvg {svg, name?, comp?} → {layer, skipped}` command. It uses the same SVG → shape conversion as Create Shapes from Vector Layer: paths, fills, strokes, gradients and blend modes, with clips around the whole document becoming masks. `vector::shapes_from_vector` and the new `vector::shapes_from_svg` share one helper. The new layer is named "Shape Layer n" and goes above the selected layer, with its Anchor Point at the centre of the SVG canvas and its Position at the comp centre. The paste is one undo step. The command rejects text over 64 MB, text that isn't SVG, malformed SVG (through the existing depth-limited parser) and SVG with no shapes. It has no menu entry, so agents call it by id.
- **UI:** Ctrl/Cmd+V, and the native Edit ▸ Paste when no text field has focus, run `edit.pasteSvg` when the system clipboard text is SVG. Otherwise Paste behaves as before. title: #303: Mesh Warp's grid can be dragged in the Composition viewer
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #303.

## Problem
Mesh Warp stores its Distortion Mesh in a hidden text parameter (`mesh`: `dx,dy` offsets per vertex, row-major). The Composition viewer only draws handles for point parameters (that's why Bezier Warp works), so with Mesh Warp selected no grid showed and there was nothing to drag. The effect couldn't warp anything from the UI.

## Fix
- `fx_editors::mesh_warp_overlay`: when a Mesh Warp effect (or one of its parameters) is selected and layer controls are shown, the viewer draws the (Rows+1)×(Columns+1) grid over the layer in effect space (same mapping as effect points, so it follows transforms and 3D views), with a handle on every vertex. Automation id: `viewer.meshWarp.<fx>.<row>.<col>`.
- Dragging a vertex writes its offset to `mesh` through `prop.set`, one undo step per drag. If the stored mesh doesn't match Rows/Columns, editing starts from the undistorted grid, which is also how the renderer treats it.
- It's wired into `effect_controls::viewer_hook` next to Reshape's overlay.

Not in this PR: AE's per-vertex Bezier handles. The renderer interpolates the mesh bilinearly, so there's nothing for those handles to drive yet. Also, `mesh` is a text value, so keyframes on it hold instead of interpolating. The `#303` mentions in `docs/effects-parity.md`, `docs/gaps.md` and `docs/target-app-parity.md` are left for the maintainers' progress refresh.

## Tests

Dragging it 40 px right moves only that vertex, takes one undo step, and the handle follows it. Without the fix the handles don't exist.

After Effects 26 imports FBX models into Advanced 3D comps. EffectCraft read glTF and OBJ only, and File ▸ Import rejected `.fbx`, so FBX product shots and scenes could not be used.

title: Graph Editor: Shift constrains Bezier handle drags to one axis (#723)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #723.

In the Graph Editor, holding Shift while dragging a key already kept it on the time or the value axis, whichever the pointer moved more along. Dragging a Bezier handle ignored Shift and moved freely.

The handle drag now applies the same rule: with Shift held, only the dominant axis (time or value) changes; the other stays where it was at the press. The rule is pulled out of the key drag into a small `shift_axes` helper so both drags share it, and the key drag behaves exactly as before. Every selected key's handle on the same side still moves together, in one undo step.

Test: `panels::graph::tests::shift_locks_drag_to_dominant_axis` covers no Shift (both axes), a mostly horizontal drag, a mostly vertical drag and a diagonal tie (time wins, as for keys).

title: #732: toolbar Fill/Stroke Options change the selected shape layers' kind
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #732.

## Problem
With shape layers selected, the Tools bar's **Fill Options / Stroke Options** (None, Solid Color, Linear Gradient, Radial Gradient, and the swatch's Alt-click cycle) only changed the defaults for *new* shapes. `shape.fillStroke` had no kind, so you couldn't remove a selected layer's fill or outline, or turn it into a gradient, from the toolbar. A group with paths and no fill or stroke gets one. A new gradient spans the group's paths, the same way new shapes get one.
  - It reports the first layer's `fillType` / `strokeType`.
- Toolbar: the kind buttons in Fill Options / Stroke Options and the swatch's Alt-click apply to the selected shape layers, one undo step each. The swatch shows the selected layer's kind. Blend mode and opacity in the popup still only set the defaults for new shapes.

title: #474: decoding a multi-layer EXR no longer holds the file's samples twice
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #474 (the "drop the intermediate `Vec`" item; possibly related to #717).

## Problem
`read_exr_channels` kept the exr crate's whole decoded image alive while it built every f32 plane. It also copied each channel through an extra `Vec` (`values_as_f32().collect()`) before placing it. For the issue's 2560×1440, 32-channel Blender file, one decode briefly held ~320 MB of samples next to ~470 MB of planes, and that happens for every frame being decoded at the same time.

## Fix
- The decoded image is now consumed one channel at a time, so each channel's samples are freed (or moved) as soon as its plane is made. At peak, a decode holds about the finished planes plus one channel, not both copies.
- A channel that covers exactly the display window is converted in one pass. An f32 channel (the Cryptomatte ranks) becomes its plane without any copy.
- All other channels are placed into the display window as before, with bounds-checked indexing (`get` / `get_mut`, `try_from`, `checked_mul`) in place of direct indexing.

Not in this PR (still open in #474): keeping half channels as f16, reading only the picture layer's channels, and sizing the channel cache by bytes.

## Tests
- `exr_channels::tests::channels_become_planes_without_an_extra_copy`: a full-window f32 channel's plane is the same allocation. f16 and u32 channels, offset data windows, data windows clipped by the display window, and short sample buffers give the same planes as before.
- The existing EXR tests (layered files, Blender 5 multi-part, Cryptomatte metadata, shared decode) are unchanged and pass.

## Gates
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p effectcraft-media --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test -p effectcraft-media` (all), `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p effectcraft-media`.

title: #750: float footage follows Working Gamma and is encoded once
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #750.

Part of ranked gap #10 "Colour pipeline differences" (docs/gaps.md); the follow-up @Romasikkk reported on #495 after #645.

## Problem

With no working space and Working Gamma 2.4, After Effects converts a linear EXR with a pure 2.4 power curve (0.18 → 0.490, 0.051 → 0.290). On main the setting reached Interpret As Linear Light but not float footage: `MediaPool` sRGB-encodes float values at decode, before the renderer knows the project's curve, so a linear EXR still came out at 0.18 → 0.4627. Turning on Interpret As Linear Light for the EXR then encoded a second time on top of the decode's own encoding (0.18 → 0.7255).

## Fix

- `effectcraft-render`: new `FloatCurve` (sRGB, a pure 2.4 power curve, or the stored linear values) and `FootageSource::frame_with(item, footage, t, size, float)`. Its default calls `frame` / `frame_at_size` and ignores the curve, so sources without float footage don't change. `Pipe::float_curve(f)` picks the curve: the stored values when Interpret As Linear Light encodes them afterwards (once, with `linear_footage_space`), otherwise the Working Gamma's curve when unmanaged and sRGB when managed (the working space converts from there). The footage paths (plain, reduced size, separate fields, frame blending, comp proxies) ask through it. The frame-blend cache key includes the curve.
- `effectcraft-media`: `AlphaOp` takes the curve instead of the Preserve RGB flag (Preserve RGB still reads the stored values, whatever is asked). `MediaPool` implements `frame_with`, and the decoded-frame cache key holds the curve, so each one decodes and caches separately. `frame` / `frame_at` stay sRGB.

Integer footage (8/16-bit) decodes the same way whatever the curve. Managed projects without Interpret As Linear Light don't change.

title: #315: Front / Bevel / Side / Back Color for extruded shapes and text
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #315.
Part of ranked gap #12 "3D interaction and depth" (docs/gaps.md).

## Problem
In an Advanced 3D comp, an extruded shape or text layer rendered as one mesh in its paint colour. After Effects colours the front, bevel, side and back of an extrusion separately: shape layers have Contents ▸ Add ▸ Front / Bevel / Side / Back (the menu in #315), and text has the same under Animate. EffectCraft had neither.

## Fix

Each group holds at most one item per surface, so a second add reuses it. An item colours that surface of every extruded paint in its group and in nested groups; the innermost item wins, wherever it sits in the group.

title: #758: layers, property groups and properties are callable
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #758.
Part of #625 (scripting-host gaps).

## Problem
In After Effects, layers, property groups and properties are callable as a shorthand for `.property(nameOrIndex)`: `layer("ADBE Effect Parade")`, `layer("Effects")`, `fxGroup(1)`, `layer("Effects")("Slider Control")("Slider")`. Duik and many other scripts use this throughout. In EffectCraft these objects were Proxies around plain objects, so every such call failed with `TypeError: not a callable function`; only `.property(...)` worked.

## Fix
`crates/script/src/prelude.js`: a new `__callable(o)` helper replaces `new Proxy(this, __attr)` for `Layer` (all layer kinds), `PropertyGroup`, `MaskPropertyGroup` and `Property`. The Proxy now wraps an arrow function that holds the object's state and prototype. Its own `name`/`length` are removed, so the object's `name` getter still applies. The `apply` trap returns `self.property(arg)`, so a call behaves exactly like `.property()`: it returns `null` when nothing matches, a `Property` returns `null`, and calling with no argument gives the same script error. `instanceof`, attribute access (`layer.transform.position`, `layer.Effects`) and script result JSON are unchanged. `new` on these objects stays a TypeError, and nothing recurses.

Known difference: `typeof layer` is now `"function"`; ExtendScript reports `"object"`. A callable Proxy can't avoid this.

## Tests
New `crates/script/src/tests_callable.rs`:
- `layers_groups_and_properties_are_callable`: name, match name and index calls on a layer, the Effects and Masks groups, an effect and Transform; chained calls; calling `parentProperty`; null for absent children; `instanceof`; attribute access still works; the slider value set via a call reaches the engine. Without the fix it fails with `TypeError: not a callable function`.
- `calling_without_a_name_is_a_script_error`: `l()`, `x(null)` and `new l(...)` give script errors, not crashes; the result JSON of a layer is unchanged.

Also updated the scripting object model…

title: #762: import animated WebP as footage with its frames
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #762.

Found while measuring #719.

## Problem
An animated WebP (for example one with alpha made by `ffmpeg -c:v libwebp_anim -loop 0`) imported as a still and showed only its first frame: `probe_bytes` sent every WebP down the still path. Animated GIF already plays its frames through `gif_anim`.

## Fix
- New `crates/media/src/webp_anim.rs`, following the animated GIF path:
  - **Probe:** reads the RIFF chunk headers: the `VP8X` animation and alpha flags, plus one `ANMF` chunk per frame. A WebP with two or more frames becomes `Video` footage with codec `WebP`. Alpha is `Straight` when the VP8X alpha flag is set and `Ignore` otherwise. A still WebP, or an animation with one frame, stays a still.
  - **Timing:**
    - Delays that differ by at most 1 ms are read as the standard rate they round to. ffmpeg's 24 fps output (41/42 ms) becomes 24 fps and 1.0 s, not 1000 fps; 29.97 is handled the same way.
    - Any other timing gets 1000 / the gcd of the delays, so uneven timing stays exact.
    - Delays of 10 ms or less count as 100 ms, as in browsers and as for GIF.
  - **Decode:** every frame is decoded once with the `image` crate's WebP `AnimationDecoder`. No new dependency. Frames are cached in the pool's existing GIF slot.
- `gif_anim::Anim` now stores frame starts as `Tick`s. It serves both formats: `Anim::load` sends RIFF/WEBP data to `webp_anim::load`. `is_gif` is renamed `is_animated`. GIF behaviour is unchanged and its tests still pass.
- **Robustness:**
  - If canvas × frames is above the existing GIF memory cap (1 GiB, or 256 MiB on wasm32), the file is refused before decoding with a clear message.
  - A damaged tail keeps the frames before it.
  - A file with no decodable frames gives a decode error. Nothing panics or hangs.
- `docs/file-format-parity.md`: WebP row updated.

## Tests
- `an_animated_webp_is_a_movie_with_its_frames`: a hand-built 3-frame animated WebP probes as Video with 20 fps, 0.2 s and Straight alpha. Frame N differs from frame 0, alp…

title: #759: #include / //@include / #includepath in scripts
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #759.
Part of #625 (scripting-host gaps).

## Problem
ExtendScript's preprocessor directives weren't understood: a script, ScriptUI panel or library (Duik/DuAEF) failed to parse at its first `#include`, and `#target` / `#targetengine` / `#strict` lines broke parsing too.

## Fix
- `crates/script/src/include.rs`: before a script runs, `#include "f"` and `//@include "f"` are replaced by the file's lines. Relative names resolve against the including file's folder, then the folders of the latest `#includepath "a;b"` (or `//@includepath`); absolute paths as they are. Directives are recognised on lines of their own; quotes and a trailing `;` are optional.
- Each file is inlined once (include-once, which also breaks cycles), nesting is limited to 32, a file to 16 MiB and all included text to 64 MiB.
- Reads follow the scripts' existing file gate: the running script's own folder, the project's folder, or anywhere with *Allow Scripts to Write Files and Access Network*. Code without a file (Script Console, `script.run`) resolves relative includes against the project's folder.
- `#target`, `#targetengine`, `#strict`, `#script`, `#engine` are dropped (blank lines, so numbering stays).
- Errors in the expanded code are mapped back to the included file and its line; missing files are an error on the directive's line. Scripts without directives run exactly as before.
- `crates/script/src/scriptfile.rs` holds the shared resolution / gate / limits, so `$.evalFile` (#760, separate PR) uses the same rules.
- Docs: `docs/scripting-parity.md` and `docs/plugins.md` rows updated.

## Tests
`crates/script/src/tests_include.rs` (all three fail on main, where `#include` doesn't parse):
- `includes_are_inlined_relative_to_the_script`: `#target`/`#targetengine`/`#strict` ignored, `//@include`, `#includepath` search folders, nested includes, an include cycle inlined once.

title: #760: $.evalFile and a minimal BridgeTalk host identification
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #760.
Part of #625 (scripting-host gaps).

**Overlap with #771 (#759, `#include`):** both PRs add the same `crates/script/src/scriptfile.rs` (byte-identical: file resolution, read gate, size cap, depth limit) and make `runtime::normalize` / `project_dir` `pub(crate)`. Please merge #771 first; this branch then merges cleanly on top (checked with `git merge-tree`, and the combined tree's script tests pass).

## Problem
`$.evalFile` always threw ("scripts can't run scripts") and `typeof BridgeTalk` was `undefined`, so frameworks such as DuAEF failed during initialisation when they load their modules or ask which application they run in.

## Fix
- `$.evalFile(file[, timeout])` (native `__evalFile`) evaluates a script file in the global scope and returns its last value; thrown errors reach the caller (catchable). Accepts a path or a `File`.
- Relative paths resolve against the folder of the file being evaluated (the running script's for the outermost call, else the project's folder).
- Same rules as `#include`: the scripts' file gate (the script's own folder, the project's folder, or anywhere with *Allow Scripts to Write Files and Access Network*), 16 MiB per file, at most 32 nested calls; the bracket-depth check runs before parsing, so a hostile file can't overflow the parser's stack.
- `BridgeTalk` identifies the host honestly: `appName` = `"effectcraft"`, `appVersion` = the build version, `appSpecifier` = `effectcraft-<version>`, `appLocale`, `appStatus`; `isRunning` / `launch` / `getSpecifier` / `getDisplayName` / `getStatus` / `getTargets` answer for EffectCraft only. `new BridgeTalk().send()` throws "sending messages to other applications is not supported in EffectCraft".
- Docs: new `docs/scripting-parity.md` row; crate docs list `BridgeTalk`.

title: #770: Proportional Scrubbing of Timeline values (Ctrl+Alt / Cmd+Opt)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #770.

Part of ranked gap #21 "Small 26.x features" (ui-parity.md) (docs/gaps.md).

## Problem
After Effects 26.2 added Proportional Scrubbing (Adobe help "Proportional Scrubbing in timeline", 26.2 beta announcement): hold Ctrl+Alt (Cmd+Opt on macOS) while scrubbing a blue hot-text value in the Timeline with several layers selected. The first selected layer keeps its value, the last takes the whole change, and the layers between get even, linear shares by selection order, whichever layer you scrub. Shift still multiplies by 10. Keyframed properties get a key at the current time. Our multi-layer scrub (#491) always moved every selected layer by the same change.

## Fix
- `prop.set` (engine) takes `proportional` alongside `selected` + `offset`. Each participating layer (the scrubbed one and its same-path twins on the other selected layers) gets `index / (n - 1)` of the change, in selection order (`state.selected_layers` keeps click/add order), in one undo step that a continuing scrub merges into. The first layer is left alone, with no key added. Without `proportional` the behaviour is unchanged. Agents can drive it over the control channel / MCP.
- Timeline value editor: while Ctrl+Alt (Cmd+Opt) is held during a scrub it sends `proportional: true`. That chord no longer fine-scrubs (Ctrl alone still does) and no longer unlinks a linked Scale pair (Alt alone still does). The rule is `widgets::proportional_scrub`.
- docs/ui-parity.md Timeline row updated. docs/gaps.md not touched.

Rule chosen: Adobe's docs describe the distribution as even and linear across the selection index. I implement exactly that: share = i/(n-1) for selection index i of n.

## Tests
- `engine` `tests_timeline::proportional_scrub_spreads_the_change_by_selection_order`: selection order c, a, b (not stack order). title: #766: ScriptUI mouse events reach script listeners
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #766.
Part of #625 (scripting-host gaps).

## Problem
ScriptUI controls never sent mouse events to scripts. `addEventListener("mousedown" | "mouseup" | "mousemove" | "mouseover" | "mouseout" | "click", handler)` listeners never ran, so custom-drawn controls (`onDraw` plus mouse, which DuScriptUI relies on) couldn't react to the pointer. `docs/plugins.md` listed this as missing.

## Fix
- **`crates/script/src/scriptui.js`**: builds a ScriptUI MouseEvent, following the public JavaScript Tools Guide. It has `type`, `target`, `currentTarget`, `eventPhase`, `clientX`/`clientY` relative to the target, `screenX`/`screenY`, `button` (0/1/2), `detail` (the click count), `altKey`/`ctrlKey`/`metaKey`/`shiftKey`, `getModifierState()`, `stopPropagation()` and `preventDefault()`.
  - The event goes through the capture, target and bubble phases. `addEventListener` and `removeEventListener` now accept the `capture` flag.
  - The parent walk is bounded, so a parent cycle that a script makes can't hang it.
  - A mouse `click` does what a click already did (it toggles a checkbox and runs `onClick`) and also gives its listeners the pointer details.
- **`crates/engine/src/scriptui.rs`**:
  - New `Widget::mouse` field: the mouse events a listener on the control or one of its containers wants. Frontends send only those.
  - New `scriptui.mouse` command (`{window?, widget, type, x?, y?, button?, detail?, …keys}`). It clamps values and keeps them finite, rejects unknown event types and disabled controls, and defaults `x`/`y` to the control's centre.
- **`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/scriptui_view.rs`**: finds the control under the pointer in floating script windows and docked panels.
  - It skips layers covered by other windows or popups, and windows blocked by a modal dialog.
  - It sends `mouseover`/`mouseout`, `mousemove`, and `mousedown`/`mouseup` with a click count.
  - A pointer click is sent with its pointer details in place of the plain click the control reported, so a checkbox s…

title: #372: uncompressed QuickTime (raw RGB / ARGB) output module format
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #372.

Part of ranked gap #22 "Encoder efficiency" (docs/gaps.md): issue #372, "Add uncompressed single-file output" (maintainer bflatastic agreed to uncompressed RGBA in QuickTime .mov as an Output Module format). FilmCraft's QuickTime muxer (`filmcraft-isobmff`, already behind `crates/export`) is reused. Only the `raw ` video sample entry is new.

## Problem
The Render Queue had no single-file uncompressed output. To hand a render to your own encoder (for example ffmpeg), you had to go through a lossy codec, ProRes, or an image sequence plus a separate WAV.

## Fix
- New Output Module format **QuickTime (Uncompressed)** (`OutputFormat::Uncompressed`, `.mov`, control-channel name `uncompressed`).
- Video is stored as QuickTime `raw ` samples, following the QuickTime File Format spec (video sample description, uncompressed RGB):
  - **RGB** (and Alpha-only matte): 8-bit RGB, depth 24. Rows are padded to an even byte count, which only matters at odd widths.
  - **RGB + Alpha**: ARGB, depth 32, straight or premultiplied as set in the module.
- Muxing goes through FilmCraft's existing `Mp4Writer` in QuickTime mode. Audio is PCM (16/24-bit or 32-bit float, mono/stereo), the same as ProRes, and the UI's Sample Format menu now offers it for this format.
- The engine's disk-space estimate (`bytes_per_frame`) knows the exact frame size. The `format` parameter docs list `uncompressed`.
- Hostile input: frame sizes of 0 px or above 65535 px return an `Unsupported` error. Short frame buffers return an `Encode` error. No panics, no indexing on input-derived values.

## Tests
- `crates/export/tests/uncompressed_mov.rs` uses a 33×20 comp, so 24-bit rows need padding, and a solid on a half pixel, so its edges have partial alpha:
  - RGB and RGB + Alpha: the samples read back with FilmCraft's demuxer match the frames the lossless PNG sequence of the same job writes, **byte for byte**.
  - **ffmpeg, as an external oracle**, decodes every frame to exactly those bytes.

title: #776: Project panel arrow-key navigation and accessible names
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #776.

Part of ranked gap #25 "Accessibility" (ui-parity.md; AccessKit is enabled, tests read focus labels, but no keyboard-navigation audit, screen-reader pass or contrast check). This PR takes the keyboard-reachability and accessible-names slice for one major panel, the Project panel (docs/gaps.md).

## Problem
- With the Project panel focused, the arrow keys did nothing. In After Effects, Up / Down Arrow select the previous / next item, Shift+Up / Down extend the selection, and Right / Left Arrow open / close the selected folder.
- The panel's custom-drawn rows, sort headers, folder twirls, label swatches, proxy switches, comment cells and footer buttons reached AccessKit with no name or role, so a screen reader had nothing useful to announce. The empty list area and each row's name cell were extra, unnamed Tab stops.
- A row focused with Tab showed no focus ring, and the arrow keys then moved egui's spatial focus instead of the selection.

## Fix (`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/project.rs` only)
- **Arrow keys:** Up / Down select the previous / next visible row. With nothing selected, Down selects the first row and Up the last. Shift extends the selection from the anchor that a click or plain arrow set. Right opens the selected folder. Left closes it, or on an item inside a folder selects the folder. The moved-to row scrolls into view; the scroll is computed with `max`/`min` rather than `clamp`, so a panel shorter than one row can't panic. The keys apply only while the panel has focus and no dialog, menu or inline rename is open. A row that has keyboard focus keeps the arrows: egui's spatial move is cancelled, focus follows the selection, and the panel takes focus.
- **Screen readers:** each row is an AccessKit `TreeItem` named `"<name>, <type>"`, with selected state, level and (for folders) expanded state. title: #773: run repeating app.scheduleTask tasks until cancelTask
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #773.
Part of #625 (scripting-host gaps).

## Problem
`app.scheduleTask(code, delay, true)` queued a repeating task and then skipped it (`eval_with_tasks`: `if repeat { continue; }`), so repeating tasks never ran. ScriptUI panels use them for polling and refreshing their UI. One-shot tasks scheduled by event handlers or in the Script Console never ran either.

## Fix
- **Task store** (`crates/script/src/tasks.rs`): each script context (host) keeps its tasks with a due time. A script file's one-shot tasks still run right after it, as before. Everything else runs when it is due.
- **Tick**: the new `ScriptUi::run_tasks` hook (`effectcraft-script` installs it) runs the due tasks. The egui app calls it every frame, but only while the session has task hosts. Errors show as a toast and printed output goes to the status bar. It schedules a repaint for when the next task is due. Agents and headless hosts use the new `script.runTasks` command, which returns `{ran, output, errors, next}`. Script-host threads receive a `Tick` message, the same session hand-off as ScriptUI events. Inline hosts (the Script Console, web runs) run in their kept context.
- **Lifetime**: a repeating task runs every `delay` ms until one of these happens:
  - `app.cancelTask(id)` is called.
  - It throws. The error is reported once and the task is cancelled.
  - Its owner goes away. A script that showed windows stops when its last window closes, so closing a panel stops its tasks. Scripts that never showed a window, and the Script Console, keep their tasks until the project is closed or replaced (`ScriptUi::project_epoch`, bumped in `replace_project`). Panels are not stopped by a project change, because the panel stays open (as in After Effects).
- **Bounds**:
  - At least 50 ms between runs (`MIN_REPEAT_MS`).
  - At most 64 pending tasks per script (`MAX_TASKS`). The 65th `scheduleTask` throws.
  - A due task runs at most once per pass, so there are no catch-up bursts after a long frame.
  - Ta…

title: #329: scrubbing a long movie: superseded viewer frames call off their decodes
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #329.

## Problem

Scrubbing a long movie (dragging the current-time indicator or clicking around a 45 min clip) showed the frame under the pointer only seconds after the pointer stopped.

A single far jump is not the slow part: FilmCraft's GOP cache seeks to the preceding keyframe and decodes forward from there (one keyframe-to-target run per jump, 0.1–0.4 s here). The time goes into *superseded* viewer frames. While dragging, the viewer asks for a new frame every UI frame. Queued requests were already dropped (#284), but each request that a free frame-pool thread had started kept running: it seeked the movie's one decoder and decoded up to a whole GOP, and the frame the pointer stopped on queued behind all of them on the decoder's lock. Nothing in EffectCraft used FilmCraft's cooperative cancellation (`filmcraft_media::cancel`), although the decoder already checks it before a seek and between samples.

## Fix

- `effectcraft-render`: `FootageSource::cancellable(cancel, f)` (default: just runs `f`) and `FootageSource::called_off()`, plus `CancellableFootage`, a per-render view of a source whose `frame`/`frame_at_size` reads each run inside `cancellable` with the render's own flag. The flag travels with the render's footage reference, not with the thread, so reads made for the render on other threads (parallel loops) answer to it and reads for other renders never do. A render whose reads were called off keeps nothing in the layer cache (an effect's layer parameter could otherwise cache a layer made from a frame that came back empty).
- `effectcraft-media`: `MediaPool` implements `cancellable` with `filmcraft_media::cancel::with_cancel`; a called-off read is `MediaError::Cancelled` (not logged as a decode error, not cached).
- `effectcraft-ui-egui` (`frames.rs`): every frame job carries a cancel flag and renders through `CancellableFootage`. A new viewer (urgent) frame calls off the comp's running viewer frames of *other times* (another revision of the same fra…

title: #779: fuzz File > Open; refuse deeply nested XML projects
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #779.

Part of workstream G3 "Stability and a green main" — the fuzzing bullet: "Fuzz the inputs we don't control: project files, imported media and documents, expressions, scripts, control-channel and MCP requests. Every crash found becomes a regression test." (docs/gaps.md). This PR covers one input surface: project files.

## Problem
Nothing fuzzed project files. File ▸ Open reads `.ecproj` JSON and `.ecprojx` XML. The XML goes through a hand-written reader (`crates/engine/src/xml_project.rs`) that recursed once per nested `<arr>`/`<obj>` with no limit, so a deeply nested file overflowed the stack. A stack overflow can't be caught, so it aborts the app instead of failing to open.

## Fix
- **Fuzzer** (`crates/engine/src/tests_fuzz_open.rs`, test `fuzz_file_open_never_crashes`). It adds no dependencies, and a given seed always produces the same inputs (splitmix64).
  - Seeds: the empty project, and the demo cut down to one layer of one comp at a time, each as JSON and as XML.
  - Byte mutations: bit flips, random bytes, deletions, splices, truncation, JSON/XML/entity tokens, and deep nesting placed where a value is expected.
  - Structural JSON mutations: extreme numbers, swapped types and subtrees, dropped members, duplicated elements, and injected `id`/`parent`/`schema`/… keys. Some of these are re-encoded as XML.
  - Every input goes through the real `file.open` path with an in-memory `Services`. After that it runs `project.summary`, `comp.info` and `layer.tree` (panics caught by the command guard count as crashes) and renders the first frame at thumbnail size.
  - Each input runs on its own thread under `catch_unwind` with a 10 s deadline. A panic or a hang is reported with its iteration and seed so it can be reproduced.
  - Default run: 3,000 inputs or 6 s, whichever comes first (about 5–6 s here). Longer runs: `EFFECTCRAFT_FUZZ_ITERS`, `EFFECTCRAFT_FUZZ_SECS`, `EFFECTCRAFT_FUZZ_SEED`, `EFFECTCRAFT_FUZZ_START`.
  - It can later be wired to cargo-fuzz/li…

title: #486: move a panel into its own native window (multiple monitors)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #486.

Part of ranked gap #20 "Multi-monitor and video output" (docs/gaps.md, hardware-parity.md).

## Problem
Floating panels could only float inside the main window, so on a two-screen setup no panel could be placed on the second monitor (#486, Linux report; same on every desktop platform).

## Fix
- Panel menu ▸ **Move Panel to New Window** (desktop builds only) and a new agent/control command, `window.panelWindow {panel, window?: bool}` (no `window` toggles). Together they undock the panel if needed and show its floating group, with tab strip and panel body, in a native egui viewport (`show_viewport_immediate`, the same mechanism the existing Video Preview window uses). The window opens over the panel's old place and can then be dragged to any screen.

- The window's position and size are saved in the workspace (`workspaces.json`, a new `#[serde(default)]` field, so older files still load), and the window comes back there on the next start. Values are sanitised: finite, size 160×100…16384, position within ±100000. A window entry for a panel that doesn't float is dropped on load.
- The window system owns the position after the window opens. The builder keeps its spawn rect, so a window being dragged isn't fought every frame. Position and close requests are only read in true native viewports. Embedded viewports (browser build, kittest) show the group as an in-app window instead.

title: #788: hold opened projects and size commands to the 30,000 px limits
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #788.

Part of workstream G3 "Stability" / AGENTS.md never-crash: our File ▸ Open fuzzer (PR #785) noted that comp sizes (and likely other dimensions: layer/solid sizes, frame rate, duration, pixel aspect, resolution factor) read from a project file are not capped, so a hostile or corrupt project can trigger a huge allocation/render. After Effects limits comps to 30,000 × 30,000 px (public docs); find the existing limits used by the UI/commands (comp.new etc.) and enforce the same bounds when LOADING projects (.ecproj JSON and .ecprojx XML) and in every command that sets them — clamp or refuse with a clear error, never allocate first. Claim via a new issue (docs/gaps.md).

## Problem
`comp.new` / `comp.settings` already clamp width and height to 4–30,000 px, the frame rate to 0.001–1000 fps and motion-blur samples to 2–64. Reading a project did not apply any of those limits. This affects File ▸ Open of `.ecproj` and `.ecprojx` (the XML is converted to JSON first), the new-project template, recovery and offload. A file could set a 4-billion-px composition, solid or footage frame, a 0 or 10^18 fps rate (which makes zero-length frames), a negative duration, or 4 billion motion-blur samples, and every one of those values reached the renderer. Several commands also set sizes with no upper bound: `layer.newSolid` (0 px was accepted too), `layer.settings`, `file.importSolid`, `file.importPlaceholder`, Crop Comp to Region of Interest / Layer Bounds, and PSD import (a PSB can be 300,000 px a side). Comp sizes past 2^32 wrapped (`4294967306` became 10 px).

## Fix
- **`effectcraft_project::limits`** holds one set of limits:
  - sizes up to 30,000 px (`MAX_SIZE`, the After Effects limit)
  - frame rates 0.001–1000 fps
  - pixel aspect 0.1–10
  - Samples Per Frame 2–64 and Adaptive Sample Limit 16–256

  It also has helpers that clamp a value to these limits (`size`, `size_f64`, `pixel_aspect`, `frame_rate`).
- **Load:** `Project::from_json` brings every item and every pr…

title: #595: RAM preview prefetches nearest the playhead and keeps the frames just ahead
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #595 (parts 1–2). May also fix the freeze reported in #719.

**Builds on #784. Merge that first.** Until #784 lands, this PR also shows #784's commit (`#329: superseded viewer frames call off their footage decodes`); the change for #595 is the last commit.

## Problem
While a preview plays, the RAM preview cache evicted the **least recently used** frame. The frames just ahead of the playhead were rendered by prefetch *before* the frames just shown, so once the cache was full they were the first to go. Prefetch asked for them again, but the job queue ran prefetch in **request order**, so they waited behind every frame further ahead. The result is what #595 describes:

1. **Gap ahead of the playhead.** The frames right in front of the playhead are missing while frames far ahead are still green, and playback stalls at the gap.
2. **Stutter on "cached" frames.** Green frames get evicted just before the playhead reaches them. The workers never go idle because they keep re-rendering the same frames (about 4 renders per frame shown when the preview is longer than the cache), and the UI thread competes with them.

The prefetch window (`2 × threads × 3` frames) could also reach further ahead than the cache holds, for example 4K frames with the default budget. Frames that far ahead evicted the ones the preview needed next.

## Fix
- `Frames::set_playhead` (called by playback every UI frame, cleared when it stops) tells the cache and the queue where the preview is: the series, current frame, range, skip step and looping.
- **Eviction** while playing: frames the preview does not reach go first, least recently used first. That means other series, frames outside the range, and frames behind the playhead in a non-looping preview. After those, the frame the preview reaches **last** goes. In a loop that is the frame just behind the playhead, which is optimal for looping. When no preview plays, eviction is plain LRU as before.
- **Prefetch order:** urgent viewer frames first,…

title: #794: open movies in place instead of reading them whole
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #794.

Related: #329, #784

## Problem
`probe()` (`crates/media/src/probe.rs`) and the media pool's movie sources (`Inner::source` in `crates/media/src/pool.rs`) called `std::fs::read` and then `filmcraft_codecs::open_bytes`. Every clip cost its full size in memory, and twice that while probing. Importing a 45-minute video took gigabytes.

## Fix
- New `crates/media/src/stream.rs` with `FileReader`, a `filmcraft_media::ByteReader` that keeps the file open and serves positional reads (`read_exact_at` on Unix, a `seek_read` loop on Windows). It works like FilmCraft's own `FileReader` (FilmCraft MEM1), which came after our pinned rev `2c5ba7a`, so EffectCraft gets a copy of its own. `open_reader`/`reader_openers` are already in the pinned rev.
- **Pool:** footage on disk opens through `filmcraft_media::reader::open_reader(name, reader, reader_openers(), openers())`. MP4/MOV, Matroska/WebM, MXF, Ogg and MPEG-PS/TS read their index, then single samples on demand. Other formats fall back inside `open_reader` to reading the whole file and calling the same byte openers as before.
- **Probe:** the in-place path runs only when a reader opener claims the first 64 KiB and nothing that `probe_bytes` checks before containers would claim the file first: still or model extensions, PSD/SVG/PDF (`layered::sniff`), or image magic. Otherwise probing works as before, so results and error messages are unchanged.
- Files added with `MediaPool::add_bytes`, wasm32 builds (`cfg(not(any(unix, windows)))`) and whole-file audio (WAV/FLAC/MP3…) still open from bytes.
- Rust's default Windows share mode includes `FILE_SHARE_DELETE`, so an open clip can still be renamed or deleted.

**Overlaps:** the edits stay away from the lines my open PRs change. #784 and #752 touch other parts of `pool.rs`. #768 changes the doc comment just below `source()`. #755, #765 and #768 change `probe_bytes`. Here `probe()` only gains 4 lines at the top. #755 and #765 add still extensions and sniffers; the probe …

title: Keep footage dropped on the timeline at its full length (#795)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #795.

Dragging footage from the Project panel onto the timeline (or using Add Footage to Comp) cut the new layer at the end of the composition, so a 10 s clip in a 4 s comp became a 4 s layer that had to be stretched back out by hand.

Cause: `layer.addItem` clamped the layer's out point with `.min(comp.duration)`. Both the Project panel and the timeline drop go through `layer.addItem`, as does `file.import` with `addToComp`.

Fix: items with a duration (footage, precomps, stills given a length) now keep their full length past the comp's end, as in After Effects. Items without a duration (solids, comp-length stills) still end with the comp, so they behave as before.

Test: `add_item_keeps_footage_longer_than_the_comp_at_full_length` adds 10 s footage to a 4 s comp and expects an out point of 10 s. Without the fix the out point is 4 s.

title: Automation: a layer or comp id sent as a string resolves as an id (#749)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes point 2 of #749 (numeric ids treated as names). The other points of that issue are feature requests or docs changes and are not part of this PR.

MCP clients often send a number as a string, so `get_layer {layer: "98"}` and `render_frame {comp: "2985"}` reached the engine as names and failed with `no layer "98"` / `no composition "2985"`. The tool schemas already accept `integer | string`, and the docs describe these references as "id or name".

**Change**
- `comp_id` (behind `Session::resolve_comp`, used by `render_frame`, `render_preview` and every command with `comp`): if no comp is named by the string and the string is all ASCII digits, it is tried as a comp item id.
- `resolve_layer` (behind `get_layer`, `get_property`/`set_property` and every command with `layer`): if no layer is named by the string and the string is all ASCII digits, it is resolved the same way as the number (id first, then 1-based index, as for a JSON number).
- A name always wins, so a layer or comp actually named `"98"` still resolves by name. Signs, spaces and `#n` are unchanged.
- `docs/agents.md`: the reference paragraph now says an id can be sent as a string.

Both resolvers are shared by headless and bridge mode, so every tool and command path gets the fix.

**Test**
`numeric_string_resolves_as_id` (engine): a comp id and a layer id sent as strings resolve through `resolve_comp`, `resolve_layer` and `layer.tree`; an unknown all-digit string still fails. It fails on main (the string is looked up as a name).

title: ci: refactor workflows to use storytold/craft-common-actions
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
### Summary
Refactors repetitive CI/CD workflows across EffectCraft to call centralized reusable workflows and composite actions hosted in the organization repository [`storytold/craft-common-actions`](https://github.com/storytold/craft-common-actions).

### Design Decisions
- **Hosted in Organization Repository**: Workflows live under `storytold/craft-common-actions` (no personal fork/repository).
- **Intentionally Tracks `@main` (Not SHA Pinned)**: Callers deliberately track `@main` with an inline explanation comment so that org-wide CI improvements, security fixes, and build optimizations propagate across all 13+ craftapps automatically without requiring individual PR churn in every repository.
- **Explicit Secrets**: Only the exact required signing secrets are passed explicitly (`secrets: inherit` is avoided).
- **Node 24 Runtimes**: All composite and third-party actions inside `storytold/craft-common-actions` are updated to Node 24 (and pinned internally to immutable commit SHAs), eliminating Node 20 deprecation warnings.
- **Strict Verification**: Build utilities like `nfpm`, `actionlint`, and `trunk` are verified against SHA256 checksums.
- Preserves 100% of existing packaging, release matrix, and linting semantics for EffectCraft.

title: Import: stills and movies respect their orientation
author: pravdomil
body:
## What

Photos and phone videos shot with the camera turned imported exactly as stored, lying on their side. They now import the way they are meant to be seen.

### Stills (Exif orientation)

- `crates/media/src/probe.rs`: probing a still reads the orientation and swaps width and height for the quarter-turn orientations (5–8). A new `load_oriented` helper decodes a still and applies the rotation or mirroring to the pixels. A missing or invalid tag decodes as stored.
- `crates/media/src/pool.rs`, `crates/media/src/layered.rs`: the still decode (also used by image sequences) and an image embedded in a Photoshop smart object go through `load_oriented`.

### Movies (MP4/MOV rotation)

- `crates/media/src/probe.rs`: `video_turn` reads the video track header (`tkhd`) through `filmcraft-isobmff` and takes its rotation, snapped to the nearest quarter turn. Only the rotation is used: mirroring, scaling and offsets in the header are ignored, and other containers have none. Probing swaps width and height (and inverts the pixel aspect) for a quarter turn.
- `crates/media/src/pool.rs`: the turn is read once when the file is opened and kept beside its decoder. Decoded frames are turned, including the reduced-resolution path, which asks the decoder for the unturned size.
- `crates/media/src/convert.rs`: `turned` rotates a decoded frame by 90°, 180° or 270°.
- `crates/media/Cargo.toml`: new dependency on `filmcraft-isobmff` (already in the workspace, used by `export`).

Run locally on macOS:

title: #786: fuzz expressions; fix the overflows, hangs and panic it found
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #786.

Part of workstream G3 (Stability), fuzzing the inputs we don't control. This one covers expressions: the `crates/expr` parser and evaluator as they run on properties. It follows the File ▸ Open fuzzer in #785 (#779) and uses the same dependency-free, seeded approach. It branches from `main` on its own, with no dependency on #785.

## Problem
Expression text comes from users, agents and project files, and it runs on the render threads. A seeded mutation fuzzer found these failures in the current code:
- **Stack overflows that abort the app.** The existing nesting check only counted brackets and prefix operators, but the parser and compiler also recurse on chains that need no bracket:
  - `?:` from about 800 in a row, `=>`/`if`/`else if` from about 750, `||` from about 950, `++`/`new` from about 550–1 300;
  - left-deep chains of `.`, `<`, `,` or `()` from about 3 800–4 500;
  - 75 nested template substitutions or regex groups (each template or regex is one token to the rewriter, so its inside was never checked), and a long chain inside a single `${…}`.
- **Hangs:**
  - An expression that needs its own value, such as rotation `fromWorld(toWorld(anchorPoint))`, nested to `MAX_DEPTH` twice per level: 2^16 evaluations and 20 s per frame.
  - Reads that fan out between layers grew exponentially.
  - Each run allowed 10 million loop iterations, and the whole loop ran again for every property read after it.
  - The loop limit counts per function call, so a loop that calls a looping function, or a native-heavy body like `smooth(NaN, 1e9)`, could run for minutes.
- **Panic:** `wiggle(9007199254740993, 30)` at a late time overflowed the noise lattice index (`i64::MAX + 1`).
- **Panic in debug builds:** a path result with an array as a coordinate became NaN and tripped tiny-skia's clipping `debug_assert` when the mask was drawn.

## Fix
- **Fuzzer** in `crates/expr/src/tests/fuzz.rs`:
  - Seeds are 65 real After Effects-style expressions: `wiggle`, `loopOut`, `valu…

title: Performance: reduce UI stalls while dragging layers
author: cdinhoo
body:
Dragging layers can stall the UI in expression-heavy compositions: the red selection/bounding box and its handles lag behind the mouse, and playhead movement and visibility toggles can also feel delayed. This happens even when no expression warning is visible and reducing preview resolution does not help. Three UI paths contributed to the reported case: duplicate synchronous expression diagnostics (including non-solo layers), repeated evaluation of HUD geometry during snapping, and disk-cache content hashing while painting the timeline.

**Verified drag-overlay behavior:** in the native macOS test build, the reporter confirmed that the red selection box follows the cursor promptly with Snapping off, while the rendered composition image may trail until a frame finishes. The native fix moves automatic expression diagnostics and timeline content hashing off the UI thread, allowing selection controls to update while preview rendering continues. Automated coverage drags a selected layer and checks that its selection bounds move while a diagnostic expression remains blocked on a worker. **Remaining limit:** Snapping on still adds noticeable latency in this expression-heavy reproduction; this PR reduces that cost but does not eliminate it or claim every handle/tool interaction is latency-free.

This change:

- Unifies the viewer warning strip and runs automatic diagnostics on one native worker after 150 ms without interaction. Requests use immutable snapshots, are coalesced and bounded, cancel between properties, and reject stale results. The warning preference now controls every automatic viewer scan.
- Reuses expression results within one snapping target query, so bounds, transforms and vertices do not reevaluate identical properties. Each query starts fresh; edits and time changes keep updating the geometry.
- Computes missing disk-cache content keys on the native worker pool with bounded requests coalesced per comp. The blue cache indicator appears when the key is read…

title: #804: hardware video decoding (NVDEC / VA-API / VideoToolbox / Media Foundation) via filmcraft-platform
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #804.

**Draft:** this needs two maintainer decisions (see the last section): bumping the FilmCraft pin, and adding `filmcraft-platform`, a dependency that contains OS FFI.

## Why

Gap #15 (`docs/gaps.md`, `docs/hardware-parity.md`): After Effects decodes H.264 / HEVC in hardware, while EffectCraft decodes every frame in software on every platform. FilmCraft already has the hardware path in `filmcraft-platform`: VideoToolbox, Media Foundation / DXVA, NVDEC and VA-API, with automatic software fallback. On this Linux machine (RTX 5090 for NVDEC, Radeon 610M iGPU for VA-API), decoding H.264 / HEVC in hardware cuts the CPU cost of a frame by **5–31×** and the time of a random jump in a long-GOP file by **1.6–4×**. The output is **bit-exact** with the software decoder. Full numbers are under Measurements.

## Pin bump

All `filmcraft-*` git deps move from `2c5ba7a` (2026-10-03) to FilmCraft `main` **`4e2d0bc2`** (2026-10-10, 1078 commits later), the first revision that has `filmcraft-platform`. That change is its own commit (`Bump FilmCraft to 4e2d0bc2`). What broke, and the fixes:

- **API:** `MediaInfo.audio` → `audio_streams` (`audio()` / `has_audio()`); `VideoStreamInfo` gained `hdr`. These were mechanical fixes in `interchange`, `media` and two tests.
- **Behaviour, 6 tests (export round-trips for H.264 / HEVC / AV1 / ProRes, automation `qa::kinetic`):** FilmCraft now rounds a frame request to the track's nearest timestamp unit, halves up (FilmCraft 2b49201e, for 1 ms WebM timescales). The media pool asked for the *middle* of frame *i*. When the timescale equals the frame rate (our own 10 fps MP4 / MOV exports), that request rounds onto frame *i+1*. The pool now asks a quarter of the way into the frame. That still tolerates timestamps rounded either way, and it is a one-line change in `pool.rs`.
- **Behaviour, 8 VP9 encoder tests:** `filmcraft_vp9::Decoder::new()` now uses frame threads, so a picture can come out of a later call. The tests expect one picture …

title: Window: remember the window's size and position between launches
author: pravdomil
body:
## Problem
The app window opened at a fixed 1680 × 1020, wherever the system put it, on every launch. Nothing saved its geometry.

## Fix
- New `apps/effectcraft/src/window.rs` (ported from VectorCraft's window module, same conventions): the window's size, position and maximized state are saved to `window.json` in the config directory, when they change (at most once a second, so a session that ends badly still has them) and on exit.
- The next launch restores them, moved onto a monitor that is still connected; a window bigger than its screen opens maximized.
- The first launch fits the window to its screen (maximized where the default size leaves no room for a Dock or taskbar).
- A window restored maximized keeps the size it returns to (its first frames report the maximized size as an ordinary one).
- Agent-driven runs (`--control`) restore the saved window but don't overwrite it.
- A damaged or oversized `window.json` is ignored.
- `winit` (already in the build through eframe) becomes a dependency on every platform, not just macOS; `serde` is added to the app crate.

## Testing
- 6 new unit tests in `window.rs` (placement, monitor changes, damaged values, tracking, save/load round trip, maximized restore): pass.
- Manually on macOS with a scratch `EFFECTCRAFT_CONFIG_DIR`: a seeded geometry (normal and maximized) is restored and tracked back unchanged; a first launch writes the fitted geometry.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --release -- -D warnings` pass. The rest of `cargo xtask ci` (full workspace tests, layers, assets, wasm) was **not** run to completion locally.
- Not tested on Windows or Linux.

title: Shortcuts: Cmd+Left / Cmd+Right Arrow step a frame
author: pravdomil
body:
## What

- **Previous / Next Frame** also answer to `Cmd+Left` / `Cmd+Right Arrow` (Ctrl off macOS), next to `PageUp` / `PageDown`.
- **Back / Forward 10 Frames** also answer to `Cmd+Shift+Left` / `Cmd+Shift+Right Arrow`, next to `Shift+PageUp` / `Shift+PageDown`.

These are After Effects' second default keys for the same commands, and the only way to step frames on keyboards without Page keys (most laptops).

## How

A command spec can now list several default shortcuts: `CommandSpec::alt_shortcuts`, written as `cmd!(…, ["PageDown", "Cmd+ArrowRight"], …)`. The shortcut table adds them to the command's default keys, so they show in Edit ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts and can be rebound or removed like any other. Menus and tooltips keep showing the first key.

The plain arrows still nudge layers; while text is edited on the canvas, `Cmd+Left/Right` still moves the caret by a word (the editor holds keyboard focus, so app shortcuts don't run).

## Tests

- `tests_settings::cmd_arrows_step_frames_like_page_keys` (engine): both keys are defaults, the first is the one shown, no conflicts.
- `ui_frame_step::cmd_arrows_step_the_current_frame` (UI): key presses move the current time by 1 / 10 frames; plain arrows don't.

title: fix(script): preserve raw bytes in BINARY File reads, writes, and copies
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Scripts using `File.encoding = "BINARY"` cannot reliably read or write
binary files.

Bytes outside valid UTF-8 sequences are replaced with U+FFFD. This can
corrupt PNG files and other binary data when scripts read, write, or copy
them.

## Root cause

The file bridge decodes all reads as UTF-8 text and encodes writes as
UTF-8, even when BINARY encoding is requested.

File.copy also passes file contents through text conversion.

## Changes

- Add byte-preserving BINARY reads.
- Encode BINARY writes as one byte per character.
- Reject characters that cannot be represented as a single byte.
- Preserve binary contents when appending to files.
- Copy files directly as bytes rather than decoding and re-encoding them.
- Retain the existing file-access permission checks.
- Add regression coverage for binary signatures, high-byte values,
  writes, copies, appends, and invalid characters.

## Validation

- JavaScript syntax check: passed.
- Added Rust regression test: not executed.
- Cargo tests and CI: not run.

Fixes #817

title: fix(script): keep Undo command ID 16 stable for scripts
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Scripts using `app.executeCommand(16)` expect to undo their most recent
edit.

EffectCraft instead interprets 16 as an index into its internal command
registry, potentially executing an unrelated command.

## Root cause

Numeric command IDs are based on registry positions rather than stable
command identifiers.

## Changes

- Map numeric command ID 16 to `edit.undo`.
- Return 16 from `app.findMenuCommandId("Undo")`.
- Preserve existing command lookup behavior for other commands.
- Add a regression test that creates a layer, executes command 16,
  and verifies that the layer creation is undone.

## Validation

- JavaScript syntax check: passed.
- Added Rust regression test: not executed.
- Cargo tests and CI: not run.

Fixes #812

title: fix(script): preserve atomic undo groups beyond the history limit
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

A script can group multiple edits with `app.beginUndoGroup()` and
`app.endUndoGroup()`.

When the group contains more commands than the configured Levels of Undo,
the group's opening snapshot is removed from history.

Consequently, one Undo no longer reverses the entire group.

## Root cause

Undo-group collapsing searches the remaining history for the original
project snapshot.

When history trimming removes that snapshot, collapsing fails and the
intermediate commands remain separate undo steps.

## Changes

- Preserve the history state from before the undo group begins.
- Restore that history when intermediate commands exceed the undo limit.
- Record the complete group as one undoable action.
- Preserve earlier history entries.
- Avoid restoring stale history after a project replacement.
- Add regression coverage using 40 edits with an undo limit of 3.

## Validation

- Added Rust regression test: not executed.
- Cargo tests and CI: not run.

Fixes #810

title: feat(script): delete keyframe ranges in one undoable command
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Removing many keyframes through repeated `Property.removeKey()` calls
becomes increasingly expensive as the property contains more keys.

Each call dispatches a separate engine edit.

## Changes

Add an EffectCraft scripting extension:

`Property.removeKeys(first, last)`

The method:

- Accepts an inclusive range of one-based keyframe indices.
- Validates the requested range before modifying the property.
- Collects the referenced keyframes.
- Dispatches one existing `keys.delete` command.
- Preserves the engine's selection and undo behavior.
- Adds regression coverage for range deletion, surviving keyframes,
  undo, and invalid indices.

## Scope

This provides an efficient batch-deletion API.

It does not change the performance of individual `removeKey()` calls
or implement batch keyframe insertion.

## Validation

- JavaScript syntax check: passed.
- Added Rust regression test: not executed.
- No performance benchmark or Cargo tests executed.

Addresses #814

title: fix(script): persist layer comments and unnamed marker parameters
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Two scripting operations silently lose data:

1. Assigning `layer.comment` does not update the layer.
2. Marker parameters disappear when the marker has no cue point name.

Both operations appear valid to scripts but do not preserve the
requested values.

## Root cause

Layer.comment exposes a getter without a corresponding setter.

Marker serialization creates a cue point only when cuePointName is
nonempty, although the cue point also stores marker parameters.

## Changes

- Add a Layer.comment setter using the existing layer.setComment command.
- Preserve marker parameters even when cuePointName is empty.
- Keep existing behavior for named cue points.
- Add regression coverage for layer comments, unnamed marker parameters,
  and named marker parameters.

## Scope

This addresses two scripting problems reported in #808.

Layer coordinate conversion methods are not changed.

## Validation

- JavaScript syntax check: passed.
- Added Rust regression test: not executed.
- Cargo tests and CI: not run.

Addresses #808

title: fix(script): expose AVLayer transform property shortcuts
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Scripts commonly access transform properties directly:

- layer.anchorPoint
- layer.position
- layer.scale
- layer.rotation
- layer.opacity

EffectCraft supports the corresponding properties through
layer.transform, but these direct shortcuts are unavailable.

## Changes

- Expose the five transform shortcuts on AVLayer.
- Return the existing Property objects rather than their current values.
- Preserve support for property methods such as setValue(),
  setValueAtTime(), and keyframe inspection.
- Keep the underlying transform implementation unchanged.
- Add regression coverage for reading properties, editing position,
  adding rotation keyframes, and undo.

## Scope

This addresses the direct transform-property compatibility gap in #816.
Other APIs listed in that issue are unchanged.

## Validation

- JavaScript syntax check: passed.
- Added Rust regression test: not executed.
- Cargo tests and CI: not run.

Addresses #816

title: fix(script): preserve item and layer wrapper identity
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem
Repeated access to the same project item or layer produces
different JavaScript objects.

This breaks identity comparisons commonly used by scripts.

## Changes
- Cache project item wrappers by item ID.
- Cache layer wrappers by composition and layer ID.
- Route containingComp, usedIn, and precomposition references
  through the shared object factories.

- Add regression tests for identity comparisons and project resets.

author: Ni-zav

the scope of this PR.

title: fix: crash and hang fixes from fuzzing, Puppet overlay off the UI thread, memory release on open, CLI and test fixes
author: eliasx45
body:
## What
**Never crash: fuzzing**
- `fuzz/`: cargo-fuzz targets for every input EffectCraft doesn't control: `project_open` (`.ecproj`
  JSON and XML, loaded and rendered), `lottie_import`, `svg_parse`, `psd_parse`, `pdf_parse` (PDF /
  AI / EPS), `interchange_import` (FCP7 XML, FCPXML, OTIO, EDL), `expr_eval`, `media_probe` and
  `engine_command` (commands with fuzzed parameters on the demo project). File services deny every
  access; nothing touches the disk, network or processes. The crate has its own `[workspace]`, so
  normal builds and CI never compile it.
- `cargo xtask fuzz --list | --seeds | [TARGET…] [--seconds N] [--jobs N]`, a seed corpus
  (`fuzz/corpus/*/seed-*`, attributed in ATTRIBUTION.md), docs/testing.md "Fuzzing", findings under
  G3 in docs/gaps.md. Most of these lines are `fuzz/Cargo.lock` and seed files.
- PDF: a page tree whose `Pages` node lists itself in `Kids` was walked 3^32 times and hung the
  import; the walk now has a visit budget.
- Paths: shapes with huge coordinates (e.g. 1e30) are clipped to a safe range before tiny-skia
  rasterises them, instead of overflowing or hanging the rasteriser.

**Puppet responsiveness (#586)**
- The Puppet mesh solve is reused when only unrelated inputs change; a mesh cache hit no longer
  allocates the alpha buffer.
- A changing Puppet overlay (dragging a pin, scrubbing) is solved off the UI thread through a bounded
  mailbox on the existing frame pool; intermediate poses coalesce, and a failed or panicking solve
  shows a status message instead of taking the app down.
- `Session.epoch` counts project replacements, so the overlay cache can't show a stale mesh after
  opening another project whose comp/layer ids match.

**Memory (#591)**
- `Session::replace_project` (open, new) clears the layer cache and sends `Event::PurgeCaches`; the
  app's handler also clears the GPU upload cache. Edit ▸ Purge ▸ Memory clears it too.

title: perf: faster effects, expressions, text, caches, movie reading, project open, export and UI playback
author: eliasx45
body:
## What
**Effects**
- Four CPU kernels, bit-identical output: `Plane::transpose` is cache-blocked in 32×32 tiles (twice
  per vertical pass of `box_plane` / `gauss_plane`); Median updates its histogram inline through a
  generic column visitor; Camera Lens Blur sums iris span counts once per iris, not per pixel; Cell
  Pattern computes each cell's feature point once per frame (about 7× faster at High Quality).

**3D**
- Depth of field: the iris kernels gather only the two blur levels around each pixel's radius from
  one set of row prefix sums, instead of keeping up to eight full-image blurs (about 4× faster).
- Both 3D compositors skip preparing shadow casters when shadows are off (Draft without Realtime
  Shadows).

**Layer cache**
- Under budget pressure, quantised 8 and 16 bpc entries are packed as `u8` / `u16` (`PackedBuf`)
  instead of evicted; packing checks every value round-trips bit for bit and declines otherwise. The
  cache holds 2–4× as many 8/16 bpc layers at the same budget.

- More caches follow the Memory & CPU budget: the GPU upload cache drops freed layers' textures on
  every upload and evicts least recently used when over budget, with the texture pool sized from the
  layer-cache budget; Roto Brush segmentations get half the layer-cache budget (at most 768 MB); the
  disk-cache write queue is bounded by bytes.

**Media**
- Movies open through a file reader: the sample index is read at open and samples on demand; audio
  and movie probes read headers instead of decoding the whole file. Standalone audio is probed with
  `symphonia` (MPL-2.0, already in `Cargo.lock` through FilmCraft), now a direct dependency of
  `effectcraft-media`.

**Expressions**
- A run collects every missing host value at once and prefetches what the previous evaluation read;
  keyframe lists are read lazily; `sourceRectAtTime` on shape layers is geometric; a layer's own path
  is memoised.
- A per-thread memo shares results between evaluations; it returns a stored result on…

title: Timeline: U and UU reveal Time Remap
author: pravdomil
body:
## Problem
U (keyframed properties) and UU (all modified properties) never showed Time Remap on a layer with time remapping enabled.

## Cause
`anim.reveal` walked only the layer's top-level groups. Time Remap is a property at the root of the layer's tree, not inside a group, so it was skipped.

## Fix
`anim.reveal` also looks at the root-level properties. For the modified reveal, enabled time remapping counts as a modification in itself. The timeline already renders root-level revealed properties, so no UI change was needed.

## Tests
- `tests_timeline::reveal_shortcuts_take_in_time_remap` (engine): keyframes, animation and modified all return Time Remap once it is enabled, and nothing before.
- `panels::timeline::tests::u_and_uu_reveal_time_remap` (UI): the Time Remap row shows under the layer after U and after UU.

Both pass, along with the existing reveal tests. The full `cargo xtask ci` was not run.

## Not in this PR
The wider UU gaps (static non-default values outside Transform such as Audio Levels, Material/Geometry/Camera/Light Options, Layer Styles and text options, plus false positives on cameras, lights and separated position) are handled in the follow-up #867, which is stacked on this PR.

title: Shapes: drag gradient start and end points in the Composition viewer (#612)
author: tylerjenningsw
body:
Closes #612.

> **Builds on #694** (the Gradient Editor). Until that merges, this PR also shows its three commits: **review only the last two**, `Shapes: drag gradient start and end points in the Composition viewer (#612)` and its `docs/gaps.md` entry. Together with #694, this covers both parts of #612: the Timeline's "Edit Gradient…" and working with the gradient directly in the viewer.

With a shape layer's **Gradient Fill** or **Gradient Stroke** selected, or any property in it (Start Point, End Point, Colors…), its **Start Point** and **End Point** show in the Composition viewer as draggable ⊕ crosshairs with a guide between them, as in After Effects.

## How
- **Hook:** a new `panels/gradient_handles.rs` hook, called right after the effect point controls' hook. Like those, it runs after the viewer's own gestures, so a handle takes the press and the layer doesn't move.
- **Coordinates:** Start and End are in the space of the shape group that holds the gradient. On screen they are `l2c(layer) × shapes::item_matrix(layer, gradient)`, through the enclosing groups' transforms and then the layer's (and the 3D view's). A drag maps back the same way.
- **Undo:** a drag is one `prop.set` merge (`gesture_key`, now `pub(crate)`), so it's one undo step. On an animated point it sets a keyframe at the current time, like the viewer's other drags.
- **Show Layer Controls:** the handles follow View ▸ Show Layer Controls.
- **Automation ids:** `viewer.gradientPoint.<uid>`, the Start Point or End Point property's uid.

title: Save the active comp and open comp tabs in project files (#748)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Fixes #748

A saved `.ecproj` had no record of which composition was active, and `file.open` always opened the lowest-id comp. The desktop app, the CLI and MCP `open_project` all open through `file.open`, so all three reopened on the wrong comp.

Project files now carry `activeComp` and `openComps` (the open Timeline tabs, in order) next to `savedBy`. On open, ids that still name a comp are restored. If none of them do, or the file is older and has neither key, the project opens on its first comp like before. Save, Save As, Save a Copy, Increment and Save and the XML copy all write the keys. They live outside the `Project` struct (`SavedView`, read with `saved_view()` like `saved_by()`), so switching comps doesn't mark the project unsaved and the project content is unchanged.

No schema bump. `schema` only changes when a saved value changes meaning, and these are new optional keys. Older builds ignore them, since `Project` doesn't deny unknown fields (that's already how `savedBy` works). The project test checks that a file with the new keys still parses into the same `Project`. I added a sentence about it to docs/architecture.md.

Tests:
- project: `to_file_json_with_view` round trip, an older file with no view, and a garbled `activeComp` that gets ignored.
- engine: three comps, B active, C's tab closed, then save and reopen. Active is B and the tabs are A and B. Before the fix this failed with active = 1. The same test covers an old file without the keys (opens on A), stale ids (999 is skipped, falls back to B), a stale id with no tabs (opens on A), and an `.ecprojx` round trip.

title: UI: draw the ▸ menu-path separator instead of a missing-glyph box
author: pravdomil
body:
## What

The separator in menu paths (`EffectCraft ▸ Settings... ▸ Appearance...` in the command palette) drew as a stroked rectangle.

## Why

The separator is `▸` (U+25B8). Neither Inter nor egui's built-in fallbacks (Ubuntu Light, Noto Emoji, the emoji icon font) have a glyph for it, so the proportional, `medium` and `semibold` families fell through to the missing-glyph box. The same applied to every other `▸` in the interface: the "File ▸ Import" hints, the "Settings ▸ Memory & CPU" toast, the expression error bar.

## Fix

JetBrains Mono is already bundled and has the glyph. `theme::install` now appends it to every non-monospace family as a symbol fallback, after Inter and egui's defaults and before the system script fallbacks, so it only draws characters the others lack.

title: Timeline: UU reveals modified options and layer styles, without false positives
author: pravdomil
body:
Follow-up to #857 and stacked on it: this branch contains that PR's commit, so merge #857 first (the diff here then shrinks to the second commit).

## Problem
UU (Reveal All Modified Properties) only knew the Transform defaults of a 2D layer:
- Static changes outside Transform were never revealed.
- A camera's or light's Position always counted as modified, as did X/Y Position after Separate Dimensions.

## Fix
`anim.reveal` with `kind: modified` builds a fresh layer of the same kind and compares against it.
- **Now revealed when changed:** Audio Levels; Material, Geometry, Camera and Light Options; a text layer's Path Options and More Options.
- **Revealed in full:** every layer style (like effects and masks already are), and each overridden Essential Property.
- **False positives gone:** cameras and lights compare their Transform with their own defaults; separated X/Y Position compare with the comp centre.

## Behaviour to know about
- A camera or light made with non-default settings (another preset, intensity or colour) shows those properties under UU, since they differ from a fresh one.
- A model layer's Model Scale and Animation are not compared: they come from the file.
- Effects still reveal as whole groups rather than per changed parameter, and shape Contents are not compared.

## Tests
- `tests_timeline::modified_reveal_is_empty_for_untouched_layers`: a fresh solid (with separated position), text, shape, null, camera, and spot and ambient light reveal nothing.
- `tests_timeline::modified_reveal_takes_in_options_and_layer_styles`: Material, Camera and Light Options, a separated position, a camera rotation and a drop shadow are revealed.

These and the existing engine and UI reveal tests pass, and clippy is clean on `effectcraft-engine`. The full `cargo xtask ci` was not run. Audio, Geometry Options, text options and Essential Properties have no dedicated test.
