title: #866: Layer ▸ New ▸ Text starts typing into Source Text
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #866.

## Problem
Reported on Discord (0.8.0, Windows): a new text layer shows "Text" and the user's typed text doesn't appear in the Composition panel; the Timeline showed the typed text as the layer **name**. Layer ▸ New ▸ Text (and Ctrl+Alt+Shift+T, and New ▸ Text in the Timeline context menus) created a layer with the placeholder "Text" and no edit session, so typed keys ran shortcuts; pressing Enter renamed the layer instead.

## Root cause
The menu entry/shortcut ran `layer.newText` with no params and the Timeline context menus with `{"text": "Text"}`, neither with `edit: true`. Only the Type tool's click path started an edit session.

## Fix
As Adobe's docs describe for Layer ▸ New ▸ Text (new text layer with an insertion point in the centre of the Composition panel), `menus::invoke` runs a param-less `layer.newText` as `{"text": "", "edit": true}`; the Timeline context menus go through the same path. Typing goes into Source Text and the layer name follows it. `engine.execute` / headless `layer.newText {}` are unchanged (still "Text"). An empty layer left by Escape is removed, as with the Type tool.

## Tests
- `ui_text_edit::layer_new_text_menu_and_shortcut_start_typing_into_source_text` (kittest, menu and Ctrl+Alt+Shift+T): type, Escape, Source Text and name are the typed text. Fails without the fix.

body:

In the Timeline's Track Matte dropdown (`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/timeline.rs`) the mode items (Alpha / Alpha Inverted / Luma / Luma Inverted Matte) only pushed `layer.setTrackMatte` when the layer already had a matte layer (`&& let Some(m) = layer.track_matte`). title: #874: scan Flatpak host, XDG and fontconfig font folders on Linux
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #874.

## Problem (reported on Discord)
Prin.Ing (CachyOS, started through the ArtCraft Launcher) reported that fonts installed on the system don't appear in the font list. The launcher installs EffectCraft as the Flatpak `ai.storyteller.effectcraft`. Inside that sandbox `text.fonts` lists 25 families. The native build on the same machine lists 320.

## Root cause
On Linux, `DirectorySource::system()` scanned only `/usr/share/fonts`, `/usr/local/share/fonts`, `~/.local/share/fonts` and `~/.fonts`:
- **Flatpak:** these folders contain only the runtime's fonts. The host's fonts are at `/run/host/fonts`, `/run/host/local-fonts` and `/run/host/user-fonts`. The sandbox's fontconfig configuration names them (`conf.d/50-flatpak.conf`, `/run/host/font-dirs.xml`).
- **Native:** `$XDG_DATA_HOME/fonts`, `$XDG_DATA_DIRS/*/fonts` and the fontconfig `<dir>` entries were never scanned.

## Fix
New module `crates/text/src/font_dirs.rs`, Linux/BSD only. It lists:
- the usual folders and the Flatpak host folders;
- the XDG data folders;
- the `<dir>` and `<remap-dir>` entries of the fontconfig configuration. The configuration is `FONTCONFIG_FILE`, else `/etc/fonts/fonts.conf` or `/usr/local/etc/fonts/fonts.conf`, plus `~/.config/fontconfig`.

How the configuration is read:
- `<include>`s are followed, both files and `NN-*.conf` folders. `prefix="xdg"`, `prefix="relative"`, relative paths and `~` are resolved. Comments are skipped, and `<cachedir>` is never treated as a font folder.
- A small tag scanner does the reading, so there is no new dependency and nothing links against fontconfig.
- The work is bounded: include depth 8, at most 512 files of up to 1 MB each, and each file is read once, so cycles end.

Other changes:
- Folders are deduplicated (canonicalised) before the walk.
- The walk depth goes from 4 to 8.
- `docs/agents.md` lists the folders and shows how to grant the Flatpak an extra folder (`flatpak override --filesystem=… --env=EFFECTCRAFT_FONT_DIRS=…`).

Not chang…

title: #880: motion paths with overflowing or NaN arc length evaluate without panicking
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #880.

## Problem (reported on Discord)
BiniFn reported on Discord that EffectCraft crashes when scrubbing the timeline after adding null objects with keyframes (macOS M1). The ordinary flow did not reproduce headlessly. A fuzz of keyframe evaluation on that same path did find a crash: when spatial keys hold huge coordinates (for example Position `±1.7e308`, which the value field accepts), moving the current time over them aborts the app. It is not confirmed that this is BiniFn's crash.

## Root cause
`SpatialSeg::at_length` returned early only for `len <= 0.0`. With huge coordinates the arc length overflows to NaN (inf − inf), and `s.clamp(0.0, len)` panics on a NaN bound. The viewer's motion-path overlay (`viewer_overlays::motion_path` → `Prop::value_at` → `keyframe::evaluate`) runs on the UI thread, outside the command guard.

## Fix
`at_length` now returns the segment start unless the length is positive and finite.

## Tests
- `keyframe::tests::overflowing_or_nan_motion_paths_evaluate` covers overflowing, NaN and infinite paths, linear and eased, evaluated across the segments. It panics without the fix.
- A local seeded fuzz (not committed) ran 200k tracks through `evaluate`, `velocity`, `speed` and the spatial tangents, using NaN, inf and ±1.7e308 values. It found no other panic or hang.
- A local kittest (not committed) with a null keyframed at ±1.7e308, selected, with the Speed Graph open and the time stepped: it crashed in `motion_path` before the fix and passes after it.

## Gates
`cargo fmt --check`, `clippy -p effectcraft-keyframe --all-targets -D warnings`, full `effectcraft-keyframe` and `effectcraft-project` tests, `cargo xtask layers`, and a wasm32 check of `effectcraft-keyframe` all pass. The full `cargo xtask ci` was not run because the machine is shared.

The plain path already works (select an item, Enter opens the name field, Enter commits). title: #882: pixel-exact Composition viewer at 100 % and above
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #882.

## Problem (reported on Discord)
Arashi (Windows 10, anime footage with aliased lines): the Composition viewer looks antialiased/blurred even at Full resolution, so the viewer doesn't match the render.

## Root cause
1. The frame's screen rect was centred in the panel without snapping to physical pixels, so at 100 % each screen pixel sampled between two frame pixels and the bilinear sampler blended them. This happens at any display scaling and is worst at 125 %/150 %.
2. Viewer Zoom Quality "More Accurate" also used bilinear filtering for magnification (`zoom_texture_options` / `zoom_sampler`), so 200 %+ and lower resolutions were smoothed instead of shown as pixel blocks.
3. View ▸ Zoom In / Zoom Out (`.` / `,`) stepped through magnifications in points, so at 125 % display scaling they jumped over 100 %.

- The frame origin snaps to the physical pixel grid. `ViewerMap` carries the snapped origin, so overlays and hit-testing stay aligned with the frame.
- Magnification is nearest-neighbour in both Zoom Quality modes, for CPU texture options and the GPU frame sampler. More Accurate keeps the averaged (mipmapped/box) minification below 100 % from #417. The snapshot texture uses the same options.
- Zoom In / Zoom Out step through magnifications measured in screen pixels (…, 66 %, 100 %, 150 %, …), as the magnification menu already did.
- `docs/preferences.md` updated.

title: Plug-ins: external effect helpers (safe, out-of-process native effects) + plug-in API 2
author: glumbis
body:
## Why

This answers the review of #508. Native plug-in code (OpenFX and the like) should not run inside
EffectCraft: it needs `unsafe`, and one crash in a third-party plug-in loses the user's work.
This PR adds no OpenFX code and no `unsafe`, and loads nothing native. Instead it gives
EffectCraft a small, generic, versioned way to use effects served by **separate helper
programs**. If a helper crashes, it takes only itself down.

Decision record: `docs/adr/0001-external-effect-helpers.md`. Protocol and usage:
`docs/external-helpers.md`.

## Why this is safe to merge into `main`

The concern in #508 was that native plug-ins compromise EffectCraft's safety. This PR addresses that by design, not just by testing:

- **No native code ever runs inside EffectCraft.** `crates/helper-host` is `unsafe_code = "forbid"`, links no plug-in libraries and calls no FFI. EffectCraft's process stays 100% safe Rust. Memory bugs in third-party code cannot corrupt EffectCraft's memory, because that code lives in a different process.
- **A crashing plug-in cannot lose the user's work.** A helper that crashes, hangs or sends garbage is stopped. The render fails with a visible message, the frame is left as it was and the project keeps running. The helper restarts on the next render. Plug-ins that keep failing are turned off automatically by the block list and the restart limit.
- **The protocol is small and validated.** It uses JSON lines plus a frame exchange file. Everything a helper sends back is parsed and checked like any other untrusted input, and anything that doesn't fit the protocol is a protocol error rather than undefined behaviour. Stray plug-in output on stdout is ignored.
- **Users stay in control.** Helpers are loaded only from known folders (next to the app, the settings folder or `EFFECTCRAFT_HELPER_PATH`). Scanning can be disabled with `EFFECTCRAFT_NO_HELPERS=1`, and the web build has none. With no helpers installed, behaviour is unchanged.
- **The core stays format-neutr…

title: Text: stop capturing keyboard input after clicking away (#831)
author: tylerjenningsw
body:
Closes #831.

After typing into a text layer, clicking somewhere else, such as a solid in the Timeline, didn't stop the editing. Typed characters still went into the text, and **Space added a space instead of starting playback**.

## Cause
Two things kept the keyboard in the text:
- The edit only ended on clicks inside the Composition viewer. A click in another panel left it open.
- egui does drop the editor's focus when you click elsewhere. But the viewer took it back on the next frame "whenever nothing else holds it", which is right after any click that doesn't focus a widget (a Timeline row, say).

## Fix
- **Clicking another panel ends the edit.** Every click in a panel already sends `DockAction::Focus`. When it's for a panel other than the viewers and the panels that format the selected characters (Character, Paragraph, Properties), it now:
  - runs `text.endEdit`, so the text is kept and an empty layer the Type tool started is removed
  - surrenders the viewer's text focus, so typing and shortcuts go back to the app
- **The editor takes the keyboard back only after a click in the viewer or one of those panels**, not merely because nothing has the focus. Both rules use the same list of panels (`keeps_text_edit`).
- **Unchanged:**
  - A click elsewhere in the viewer still commits the edit, and with the Type tool it still starts new text.
  - Switching tools still commits.
  - Character / Paragraph / Properties still format the selected characters and keep the selection.

Removing the recovery entirely was considered. It breaks typing after a Character panel click: three `ui_text_edit` tests fail, the new one plus `type_tool_click_type_edit_and_commit` and `double_click_enters_editing_and_selects_words`. While text is still being edited, Space and Delete would also run as shortcuts. That's why the recovery is kept, limited to those panels.

title: #878: context menus act on the whole selection
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #878.

## Problem
Reported on Discord by Arashi (Windows 10): with two layers selected, picking **Pre-compose…** or **Delete** from the right-click menu acted on only one layer, because the menu deselected the other. The keyboard shortcuts worked.

## Root cause
`timeline::layer_context_menu` always called `layer_menu` with `&[layer.id]`, the right-clicked layer only. Every menu item first sends `layer.select` with that list, so the rest of the selection was dropped before the command ran. This affected both the layer name rows and the layer bars. Right-clicking an unselected layer also left the old selection in place until a menu item was chosen.

In the Project panel, **Move to Project Root** moved only `[id]`, while Delete and Label already used the selection. The Composition viewer was already correct.

## Fix
- Timeline rows and bars: if the right-clicked layer is part of the selection, the menu targets every selected layer (in comp order). Right-clicking an unselected, unlocked layer selects only that layer. This matches After Effects.
- Project panel: Move to Project Root uses the same `targets()` as Delete and Label.

## Tests
New tests in `crates/ui-egui/tests/ui_workflow_selection.rs`. Both fail without the fix:
- `timeline_context_menu_acts_on_the_whole_selection`: Delete from a selected row removes both layers, and Duplicate from a selected bar duplicates both. Right-clicking an unselected row selects only that row.
- `project_context_move_to_root_acts_on_the_whole_selection`

## Gates
- `cargo fmt --check`: ok
- `cargo clippy -p effectcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -D warnings`: ok
- Full `effectcraft-ui-egui` tests with `--no-fail-fast`: all pass. `ui_gpu` passes 2/2 and then aborts at process exit, which also happens on main.
- `cargo xtask layers`: ok
- No L0–L4 crates were touched, so no wasm check was needed.
- I did not run the full `cargo xtask ci` because the machine is shared.

title: Add bounded Sony ARW sensor import (A7R IV / ARW2)
author: lia-xim
body:
Sony `.arw` photographs currently fall through the generic still-image path instead of developing the sensor mosaic. This change imports supported Sony RAW sensor data as normal float still footage, with demosaicing, as-shot white balance, LightCraft spectral profiles, highlight reconstruction and EXIF orientation. Numbered ARW photographs remain individual stills.

Initial real-file coverage is Sony ILCE-7RM4 / A7R IV compressed ARW2. Uncompressed Bayer input has synthetic coverage. Other manufacturers, lossless-JPEG ARW and older Sony compressed layouts are outside this integration's support promise. Unsupported or malformed inputs return contextual errors rather than substituting an embedded JPEG.

- Pins the first-party MIT/Apache LightCraft RAW, TIFF and colour crates behind the media layer; bounds file size, metadata and image dimensions.
- Connects the file picker, media browser, probe and decoded-frame cache; adds synthetic regressions and public-API import/render examples.
- Documents memory cost and colour/format limitations, records spectral-data attribution, and includes licence/notice documents in packaging.
- Corrects two existing Windows path assertions and a system-font test assumption: weight variation may preserve advance widths. The tests retain output/missing-file checks and independently compare shaped advances against font metrics at both axis endpoints.

title: Scripting: text range selectors resolve by match name and limit the animator (#837)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #837.

The issue reports two problems. This PR fixes both.

**1. `ADBE Text Percent Start/End/Offset` returned null.** `matchnames::node` had no entries below `ADBE Text Selectors`, so the selector's match name was its internal id (`rangeSelector`) and its properties had no After Effects names. I added two tables next to `TEXT_ANIMATOR`:
- selectors: `ADBE Text Selector` (range), `ADBE Text Wiggly Selector`, `ADBE Text Expressible Selector`. These are the same names `resolve_add` already accepts for `addProperty`.
- Range Selector properties: `ADBE Text Percent Start`, `ADBE Text Percent End`, `ADBE Text Percent Offset`.

**2. The scripted selector did not limit the animator.** The renderer is fine. `addProperty("ADBE Text Animator")` calls `layer.addTextAnimator` with `properties: []`, and `build::text_animator` always adds a default "Range Selector 1" (0-100%). The script's `addProperty("ADBE Text Selector")` then added a second selector, "Range Selector 2". The script set Start on that one, but the default selector still selected every character, so the animator hit all of them. In After Effects, a scripted animator has no selectors until the script adds one. The empty-animator path (`properties: []`, used only by scripting) now clears the default selector. Animators added from the UI or with named properties keep "Range Selector 1" as before.

**Tests**
- `matchnames::tests::text_range_selector_names`: the selector and Start/End/Offset map to their AE match names.
- `tests::scripted_text_range_selector_resolves_and_is_the_only_selector`: runs the issue's script end to end. It checks that the animator has exactly one selector, that Start is set to 50 through `ADBE Text Percent Start`, and that End and Offset resolve by match name. Without the fix, the script fails on the null property, and `numProperties` would be 2.
